Ben was a jolly boy who liked to feed the animals at the farm. He liked to feed the cows, the pigs, the sheep and the chickens. He liked to see them eat and make noises.
One day, he saw a new animal at the farm. It was big and brown and had a horn on its head. Ben was curious and wanted to feed it. He asked his mom what it was.
"That is a goat, Ben. Be careful, he can be naughty sometimes. He likes to eat grass and hay, but he also likes to chew on other things. Don't get too close to his horn, he might poke you with it." Mom said.
Ben nodded and took some grass from a basket. He walked slowly to the goat and held out his hand. The goat looked at him and sniffed the grass. He opened his mouth and took a bite. Ben smiled and said, "Hello, goat. You are hungry, huh?"
The goat nodded and chewed the grass. He wanted more. He looked at Ben and saw his red shirt. He thought it was food too. He reached out his horn and pulled Ben's shirt. Ben felt a tug and said, "Hey, goat. That is not food. That is my shirt. Let go!"
The goat did not let go. He pulled harder and harder. Ben tried to pull back, but he was not strong enough. He cried out, "Mom, help! The goat is eating my shirt!"
Mom heard Ben and ran to him. She grabbed the goat's horn and pushed him away. She checked Ben and saw that his shirt was torn and dirty. She hugged him and said, "Are you okay, Ben? I'm sorry, the goat was very naughty. He should not eat your shirt. He should only eat grass and hay."
Ben nodded and said, "I'm okay, Mom. But I'm sad. The goat ruined my shirt. He was not nice. He was not jolly like the other animals."
Mom said, "I know, Ben. But you know what? You can still be jolly. You can still be kind and feed the other animals. You can still have fun at the farm. And you can still learn from this. Next time, you will be more careful and listen to me when I tell you about the animals. You will not get too close to the goat's horn. You will remember that not all animals are the same. Some are friendly, some are naughty. Some are jolly, some are not. You have to respect them and their differences."
Ben said, "Okay, Mom. I will do that. I will be more careful and listen to you. I will respect the animals and their differences. I will still be jolly and kind and feed them. Thank you, Mom. I love you."
Mom said, "I love you too, Ben. You are a good boy. Come on, let's go and find a new shirt for you. And then we can feed the cows, the pigs, the sheep and the chickens. They are waiting for you. They are jolly and kind and they like you."
Ben smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. Let's go. I like them too. They are my friends."
The end.

One night, Lily sneaked out of her bed and crawled into her crib. She hugged her teddy bear and closed her eyes. She pretended she was a baby again. She made soft noises and sucked her thumb.
But then she heard a loud noise. It was her brother Max. He came into her room and saw her in the crib. He laughed and said, "Lily, what are you doing? You are not a baby. You are a big girl. You have a bed. Why are you in the crib?"
Lily opened her eyes and felt embarrassed. She did not want Max to see her act like a baby. She said, "I was just playing. I like my crib. It is warm and cozy. Go away, Max. You are mean."
Max shook his head and said, "Lily, you are silly. You are too big for the crib. You will break it. Come on, get out of the crib and go to your bed. I will help you."
Lily did not want to leave her crib. But she knew Max was right. She was too big for the crib. She said, "Okay, fine. But don't laugh at me. And don't tell Mom and Dad."
Max smiled and said, "Okay, okay. I won't laugh. And I won't tell. But you have to promise me something. You have to act like a big girl from now on. No more crib. Deal?"
Lily nodded and said, "Deal." She gave her teddy bear a kiss and handed it to Max. He helped her out of the crib and tucked her into her bed. He said, "Good night, Lily. Sleep tight. You are a big girl now."
Lily said, "Good night, Max. Thank you. You are a good brother." She felt warm and cozy in her bed. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She did not act like a baby anymore. She was a big girl now.

"What was that?" asked Joe.
Mommy looked out the window. "It was probably just a bird, sweetheart," she said.

He slowly stepped out, but before he could take another step, Joe felt a sharp pain in his toe. He had stepped on something that made him hurt. He quickly pulled away and hopped back into his bedroom, where Mommy and Daddy were waiting.

Mommy hugged him tight and kissed his forehead. "It's okay, sweetheart. Let's go back to bed now."

Once there was a girl and her name was Sandy. She was very smart and wanted to go on an adventure. So one day she packed up a bag and stepped outside.
Sandy walked and walked for what felt like miles. She soon came across a river bank, but it was much too wide for her to jump across.
Sandy was about to turn around and go home, when she heard a strange noise. She looked up and saw a creature lying in the middle of the river.
Sandy asked the creature, “what are you doing?”
The creature replied, “I'm trying to spoil this inch, but I keep slipping and can't get across it.”
Sandy smiled and showed the creature a clever trick she had learned. She tied a rope to two tall trees and pulled them taut. Then she made a bridge across the river. Sandy said, “Now you can cross this inch and spoil it!”
The creature thanked Sandy and they both crossed the bridge together. Soon the inch was spoiled and Sandy and the creature went their separate ways. Sandy went home feeling smart and happy, having helped the creature across the river.

The lion showed Ella a small creaky door and said, "Come, you can escape through that door." But the door had a big, hard lock. Ella tried hard to open it, but it would not open. 
The lion then said, "Hold still, and I will open the door for you." The lion snapped the lock in two and the door opened! Ella was so happy and she ran away through the door.

Sam was a boy who liked to play with his cars and his blocks. He had long hair that covered his eyes and ears. His mom said he needed a haircut, but Sam did not want one. He was scared of the scissors and the noise.
"Sam, it's time to go to the barber shop," his mom said. "You will look so nice with a haircut."
"No, no, no!" Sam cried. "I don't want a haircut! I like my hair!"
"Come on, Sam, don't be afraid. The barber is very friendly and gentle. He will give you a sticker and a lollipop when he is done. And you can bring your favorite car with you."
Sam still did not want to go, but he saw his mom was sad. He did not want to make his mom sad. He loved his mom. He decided to be brave and try a haircut.
"Okay, mom, I will go with you. But I want to keep some of my hair."
"Of course, Sam, you can keep some of your hair. You can choose how much you want to cut. Let's go, then."
Sam and his mom went to the barber shop. Sam was nervous, but he held his car tightly. The barber smiled at him and said his name.
"Hello, Sam, I'm Bob. I'm going to give you a nice haircut. Don't worry, it won't hurt at all. You can tell me how you want your hair to look."
Sam looked at the barber and said, "I want to keep some of my hair. I don't want it too short."
"Sure, Sam, no problem. I will just trim a little bit, so you can see better and hear better. You will still have plenty of hair. You are very brave, Sam."
The barber started to cut Sam's hair. Sam felt the scissors snip snip snip, but it did not hurt. He heard the noise buzz buzz buzz, but it was not too loud. He saw his hair fall on the floor, but he still had some on his head. He was brave.
"Wow, Sam, you look great!" his mom said. "You have a very nice haircut. You are so handsome!"
Sam looked in the mirror and saw his new haircut. He liked it. He could see his eyes and his ears. He felt his hair and it was soft and smooth. He smiled.
"Thank you, Bob," he said. "You are a good barber. I like my haircut."
"You're welcome, Sam," Bob said. "You are a good boy. You were very brave. Here is your sticker and your lollipop. Come back anytime."
Sam took his sticker and his lollipop and hugged his mom. He was happy. He had a haircut and he was brave. He was proud of himself.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things at the beach, like shells, crabs, and birds.
"Look, mom, look!" Lily said, pointing at the sea. "There is a big wave!"
Mom looked and saw a huge wave coming towards the shore. It was taller than the trees and the houses. It was a giant wave!
"Wow, that is a giant wave!" mom said. "But don't worry, it won't hurt us. It is just a silly wave. It likes to make noise and splash, but it will go back to the sea soon."
Lily and Tom laughed. They thought the wave was silly too. They waved at the wave and said, "Hello, silly wave! You are very big and loud, but we are not scared of you. We like to play at the beach!"
The wave heard them and smiled. It was happy that the children were not afraid of it. It wanted to play with them too. It made a smaller wave and sent it to the shore. The smaller wave reached the children and tickled their feet.
"Ha ha ha!" Lily and Tom giggled. "The wave tickled us! Thank you, silly wave! You are very fun and nice!"
The wave nodded and winked. It was glad that the children liked it. It made another smaller wave and sent it to the shore. The smaller wave brought some shells and crabs for the children to see.
"Wow, look, mom, look!" Tom said, picking up a shell. "The wave gave us a gift! It is a pretty shell!"
Mom smiled and said, "That is very kind of the wave. It is a good friend. Let's say thank you to the wave."
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Thank you, silly wave! You are a good friend. We like you very much!"
The wave beamed and said, "You are welcome, Lily and Tom. You are good friends too. I like you very much too!"
They all smiled and waved at each other. They had a wonderful day at the beach.

"Wow, it's so pretty. Can we fly it?" Max said.
"Sure, why not? It's available. No one is using it," Lily said.
They grabbed the kite and ran to the edge of the roof. They threw the kite in the air and watched it soar. They felt happy and free.
"Look, we can fly the kite. It's so fun," Lily said.
"Yes, it is. We're like birds," Max said.

They screamed and cried. They were hurt and scared.
Mom heard them and ran to the barn. She saw them lying on the ground, covered in mud and blood. She was shocked and worried.

She was also relieved and grateful. She was glad they were alive and not too badly hurt. She loved them very much.
She hoped they learned their lesson. She hoped they would be more careful and listen to her.
She hoped they would still love to play outside. But not on the roof. And not with kites.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. She stayed in bed and drank water. Her mom said she had to take medicine to feel better.
But Lily did not like medicine. It was bitter and made her face scrunch up. She tried to hide under the blanket when her mom came with a spoon.
"Lily, you have to take your medicine. It will help you work your cough away," her mom said.
"No, no, no! I don't want it! It's yucky!" Lily said.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "I know, sweetie. But it's only a little bit. And I have a surprise for you after you take it. Something sweet and yummy."
Lily looked at her mom with curious eyes. "What is it?"
Her mom whispered in her ear. "A chocolate chip cookie."
Lily's eyes lit up. She loved cookies. She decided to be brave and take the medicine. She opened her mouth and swallowed the bitter liquid. She made a funny face and stuck out her tongue.
"Good girl! You did it!" her mom praised her. She gave her a kiss and a cookie. "Here you go. This will make the bitter go away."
Lily smiled and took a big bite of the cookie. It was soft and warm and melted in her mouth. She felt happy and cozy. She thanked her mom and cuddled with her.
"Maybe medicine is not so bad," she thought. "If I get a cookie after."

Once upon a time there was a bear called Barry. Barry was feeling very ill and could not breathe properly.
His friend, Cat, asked him what was wrong. 
Barry replied, “My lung is not working properly.”
Cat suggested, “Let’s go the doctor to get you fixed up.”
So they went to the doctor's office. 
The doctor told Barry, “I am going to attach a special machine to your shoulder to make sure your lung is safe.” 
Barry was very scared so Cat hugged him and said, “It’s ok, the doctor will make sure you are safe.” 
After a few minutes, the doctor said, “Barry, your lung is safe now. You can go home.” 
Barry smiled and thanked the doctor for making him feel better. 
Then, Barry and Cat went home and were very happy. 
The End.

"Okay, Mom," said Lily. "I will share my spaghetti. But can I have some more cheese and sauce?"
"Of course, Lily," said Mom. "You are a good girl. Here you go."
Lily smiled. She gave some of her spaghetti to Mom and Dad. They thanked her and praised her. They ate together and enjoyed their meal. Lily was not angry anymore. She was happy. She fit in her family. She loved spaghetti.

Ben and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and make castles and shapes. They had a bucket and a shovel and some cups and spoons.
"Look, Ben, I found a crab!" Lily said, holding a small red crab in her hand. "He has big claws and eyes on sticks. Do you want to see?"
Ben nodded and ran over to Lily. He looked at the crab and touched it gently. "He is hard and rough," he said. "Can we keep him?"
"No, we can't keep him," Mom said, coming over to them. "He belongs to the sea. We have to let him go. But we can make him a friend. Do you want to help me?"
Ben and Lily said yes and followed Mom to the water. Mom filled the bucket with water and sand and stirred it with a spoon. "We are going to mix the water and the sand to make mud," she said. "Mud is soft and smooth and sticky. We can use it to make a crab shape."
Mom poured some mud on the sand and shaped it into a round body. Then she added four legs on each side and two claws in front. She used a cup to make eyes and a spoon to make a mouth. "There, we made a mud crab," she said. "He looks like your crab, Lily. Do you like him?"
Lily smiled and nodded. She put her crab next to the mud crab and said, "Hello, crab. This is your friend. He is made of mud. He is smooth and nice. Do you want to play with him?"
The crab waved his claws and blinked his eyes. He seemed to like the mud crab. Ben and Lily clapped and laughed. They were happy to make a new friend for the crab. They played with the crabs until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the crabs and put them back in the water. They hoped they would see them again.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Max had a car. They were having fun until Max saw Lily's doll and wanted it.
"Give me your doll!" Max demanded. "It is pretty and has a dress."
"No!" Lily said. "It is mine and I like it. You have your car."
"But I want your doll too!" Max said. He tried to grab the doll from Lily, but she held it tight.
"Stop it, Max!" Lily said. "You are being mean and rude. You can't have everything."
They started to fight over the doll, pulling and pushing. They made a lot of noise and mess.
Their mom heard them and came to the living room. She was not happy.
"What is going on here?" she asked. "Why are you fighting?"
"Lily won't share her doll with me!" Max said.
"Max wants to take my doll!" Lily said.
Mom looked at the doll and the car. She had an idea.
"Do you know where these toys came from?" she asked.
They shook their heads.
"These toys are very old and special. They belonged to your grandma and grandpa when they were little. They are ancient toys. They gave them to you because they love you and want you to enjoy them."
Lily and Max looked at the toys with surprise. They did not know they were ancient.
"They are ancient?" Lily asked.
"Yes, they are. And they are very precious. You should take good care of them and share them with each other. That is what grandma and grandpa would want. How about you take turns playing with them? You can play with the doll for one minute, and then Max can play with it for one minute. And the same with the car. Does that sound fair?"
Lily and Max nodded. They felt sorry for fighting.
"OK, mom. We will share and take turns. We are sorry for being loud and messy." they said.
Mom smiled and hugged them.
"That's good. I'm glad you are sorry and you learned something. Now, let's clean up this mess and then you can play nicely with your ancient toys." she said.

Tom and Sue cried. They did not know what to do. They wished their dad was home. He would scare the cat away.

"Leave Fluffy alone!" Spot said. "He is my friend. You are a bad and cowardly cat. You can't bully him. You have to face me!"
The cat was surprised and afraid. It saw Spot's teeth and heard his bark. It knew it could not win. It let go of the cage and ran away.
Tom and Sue cheered. They hugged Spot and thanked him. They opened the cage and took out Fluffy. They petted him and gave him a carrot.
"Fluffy, you are safe!" Tom said. "Spot saved you!"
"Spot, you are a hero!" Sue said. "You chased the cat away!"
Fluffy was happy. He licked Spot's nose and said, "Spot, you are a good and kind dog. You are my friend too. Thank you!"

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park, share their toys and help each other. One day, they saw a big slide in the park. It looked fun, but also scary. Ben wanted to try it, but Lily was afraid.
"Come on, Lily, it's not hard. I'll go first and show you. Trust me, you'll like it," Ben said.
He climbed up the ladder and slid down the slide. He laughed and waved at Lily. "See? It's fun! Your turn!"
Lily hesitated. She wanted to be brave, but she also wanted to stay safe. She looked at the slide and felt nervous. She looked at Ben and felt sad. He was her friend, but he was also pushing her.
"No, Ben, I don't want to. It's too high. I want to stay here," Lily said.
Ben frowned. He didn't understand why Lily was so scared. He thought she was being silly and stubborn. He wanted her to join him and have fun. He thought she was missing out.
"Lily, you're being a baby. Don't you want to have fun? Don't you trust me? Come on, it's easy. You're gifted, you can do anything," Ben said.
He tried to pull her hand and make her climb the ladder. Lily resisted. She felt angry and hurt. He was her friend, but he was also hurting her.
"Ben, stop it! You're being mean. I don't want to go. I don't have to do everything you do. I have my own choices. You're not gifted, you're bossy," Lily said.
She pushed him away and ran to the swings. Ben was shocked and sorry. He realized he had been wrong. He had not respected Lily's feelings and choices. He had not been a good friend.
He ran after her and apologized. "Lily, I'm sorry. I was mean. I should have listened to you. You don't have to go on the slide if you don't want to. You're still my friend. You're still gifted. Can we play together?"
Lily looked at him and smiled. She forgave him. She knew he was sorry. She knew he was still her friend. She knew he was still gifted.
"Sure, Ben. I'm sorry too. I should have told you how I felt. You're still my friend. You're still gifted. Let's play together," Lily said.
They hugged and went to the swings. They learned to trust each other and respect each other. They learned to stay friends and have fun. They learned to be gifted and kind.

One day, they saw a big elephant with long tusks and a trunk. Lily wanted to take a picture of it, but Ben was scared. He said, "No, Lily, it is too scary. It might hurt us. Let's go away."
But Lily did not listen. She said, "No, Ben, it is not scary. It is beautiful. I want to take a picture. You stay here with the sack. I will be back soon." She ran towards the elephant with the camera.
Ben was very worried. He watched Lily get closer and closer to the elephant. He saw the elephant raise its trunk and make a loud noise. He thought the elephant was angry. He shouted, "Lily, come back! Come back!"
But Lily did not hear him. She was too busy taking pictures. She smiled and said, "Wow, what a great picture. I am so brave."
Suddenly, she heard a rustle behind her. She turned around and saw a big monkey. The monkey had a naughty look on its face. It grabbed the sack from Ben and ran away. It opened the sack and took out the food and water. It ate the sandwiches and drank the juice. It threw the empty bottles and wrappers on the ground.
Lily and Ben were very sad. They had no food and water left. They had to go back to their dad and tell him what happened. Their dad was not happy. He said, "You should have listened to Ben, Lily. He was right. The elephant was scary. You were lucky it did not hurt you. And you should have stayed with the sack, Ben. You should have protected it from the monkey. You were careless. You wasted the food and water. You made a mess. You have to learn to be careful and respectful when you go on safari. The animals are not toys. They are wild and free. You have to respect them and their home."
Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We learned our lesson. We will be careful and respectful next time. We will not be brave or careless. We will be smart and kind."
Their dad hugged them and said, "I love you, twins. I am glad you are safe. I hope you enjoyed the safari. But next time, please listen to me and to each other. And please, do not forget the sack."

She runs to her mom and dad and tells them what happened. They say, "We are sorry, Lily. The parrot did not know. It is not polite to break things. But it is also not polite to yell. Maybe you can teach the parrot to be nice."
Lily thinks. She says, "OK. I will try." She goes back to the parrot and says, "Hello, parrot. I am Lily. Do you want to be my friend?" The parrot says, "Hello, Lily. I am Polly. Yes, I want to be your friend." Lily smiles.
She says, "Friends do not break things. Friends share things. Do you want to share my crayons?" The parrot says, "Yes, I want to share your crayons." Lily gives the parrot a crayon and they draw together. They draw a ball and a dog and a flower. Lily is happy.
She says, "You are a good parrot, Polly. You are polite." The parrot says, "You are a good girl, Lily. You are polite." They hug. Lily is happy.

Tommy liked to play in the garden with his dog, Spot. Spot had a long, furry tail that he wagged when he was happy. Tommy liked to chase Spot and pull his tail, but Spot did not like that. He barked and ran away from Tommy.
One day, Tommy saw some new flowers in the garden. They were pink and purple and smelled nice. Tommy was curious. He wanted to touch the flowers and see if they were soft. He walked towards the flowers, but Spot followed him. Spot was curious too.
"Spot, no!" Tommy said. "These are not for you. These are for Mommy. She likes flowers. They make her smile."
But Spot did not listen. He ran past Tommy and jumped on the flowers. He bit them and tore them with his teeth. He wagged his tail and made a mess.
"Spot, bad dog!" Tommy shouted. "You ruined the flowers! Mommy will be sad!"
Tommy tried to stop Spot, but it was too late. The flowers were all gone. They were only stems and petals on the ground. Tommy felt bad. He loved his dog, but he also loved his mommy. He did not know what to do.
Then he heard his mommy's voice. She was coming back from the store. She had a big bag in her hand.
"Tommy, Spot, I'm home!" she said. "Guess what I have for you?"
Tommy and Spot ran to meet her. They hoped she would not see the garden. They hoped she would not be angry.
"Mommy, look what I have!" she said. She opened the bag and took out a big, colorful bouquet of flowers. "I saw these at the market and I thought of you. They are so pretty and they smell so good. Do you like them?"
Tommy and Spot looked at the flowers. They were the same as the ones in the garden. They were pink and purple and smelled nice. Tommy felt happy. He hugged his mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy! I love you! I love the flowers!"
Spot wagged his tail and licked his mommy's face. He said, "Woof, woof! I love you too! I love the flowers!"
Mommy smiled and said, "I love you both! You are my sweet boys! Come on, let's go inside and find a vase for the flowers. They will look beautiful in the living room."
Tommy and Spot followed her. They did not tell her about the garden. They decided to keep it a secret. They were glad that Mommy had bought more flowers. They were glad that she was happy. They learned a lesson. They would not touch the flowers again. They would only look at them and smell them. They would let them bloom and grow.

"OK!" Tom said. "I have pepper and salt and bread."
They put everything in the pot and stirred it with the spoons. They smelled the soup and smiled.
"It smells good!" Tom said. "Can we taste it?"
"Yes!" Lily said. "But be careful, it might be hot."
They each took a spoonful of soup and put it in their mouths. Lily liked it. It was sweet and creamy. But Tom made a funny face. He spit out the soup and coughed.
"Yuck!" Tom said. "It's spicy and rough!"
Lily looked at the pot. She saw a lot of black dots in the soup. She realized that Tom had put too much pepper in it. Pepper was spicy and rough. It made Tom's mouth hurt.
"I'm sorry, Tom!" Lily said. "I didn't know you put pepper in it. Do you want some water?"
"Yes, please!" Tom said. "And some bread. Bread is soft and nice."
Lily got some water and bread for Tom. She gave him a hug and said sorry again. Tom drank the water and ate the bread. He felt better.
"It's OK, Lily," Tom said. "We can make soup again. But next time, let's use less pepper. OK?"
"OK!" Lily said. "And more cheese. Cheese is yummy!"
They laughed and hugged. They were still friends. They liked to play in the kitchen. But they learned to be careful with pepper.

The rhinoceros heard Sara's voice and looked up. It saw Sara's hand and thought it was food. It opened its mouth and moved its head towards Sara. Sara did not know what the rhinoceros wanted. She thought it wanted to play with her. She smiled and moved her hand closer.
Her mom saw what was happening and got very worried. She knew the rhinoceros could hurt Sara with its teeth or horn. She shouted "Sara, no! Don't touch the rhinoceros! It might bite you!" She grabbed Sara's arm and pulled her back from the fence.
Sara was surprised and scared. She did not understand why her mom was angry and why the rhinoceros was not friendly. She started to cry and said "Mom, why did you do that? I just wanted to pet the rhinoceros. It looked so nice."
Her mom hugged Sara and said "I'm sorry, Sara. I know you like the rhinoceros, but it is not a pet. It is a wild animal. It does not know you and it might think you are food. You have to be careful around wild animals. They can be dangerous. I love you and I don't want you to get hurt."
Sara calmed down and said "I love you too, mom. I'm sorry I made you worried. I didn't know the rhinoceros was wild. Can we still watch it eat?"
Her mom said "Yes, we can. But we have to stay away from the fence and not touch it. OK?"
Sara said "OK, mom. Thank you for letting me see the rhinoceros. It is still my favorite animal. But I will not try to pet it again."
Her mom said "You're welcome, Sara. I'm glad you like the rhinoceros. But remember, some animals are better to look at than to touch."

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play with boats. They have many boats of different colors and sizes. They pretend to be sailors and go on adventures.
One day, they find a big boat in the park. It is white and blue and has a sail. They think it is a real boat. They want to play with it.
"Can we go on the boat?" Ben asks Sam.
"I don't know. Maybe it is someone's boat. Maybe they will be angry if we touch it." Sam says.
They discuss what to do. They look around. They do not see anyone. They decide to go on the boat.
They climb on the boat. It is fun. They pretend to steer the boat and look for islands. They sing songs and tell jokes.
But then, they feel something cold. They look at the water. It is icy. It is winter. The water is freezing. They are scared.
"Help! Help!" They shout. "We are stuck on the boat!"
They hear a voice. It is a man. He is wearing a hat and a coat. He is a real sailor. He has a rope. He throws the rope to them.
"Grab the rope! I will pull you to the shore!" He says.
Ben and Sam grab the rope. The sailor pulls them to the shore. They are safe. They are happy.
"Thank you, thank you!" They say to the sailor.
"You're welcome, boys. But you should not play with boats in the winter. It is dangerous. The water is icy. You could get hurt." The sailor says.
"We are sorry, sir. We did not know. We just wanted to have fun." Ben and Sam say.
The sailor smiles. He is not angry. He is kind.
"I understand. But next time, ask before you use someone's boat. And wear warm clothes. And stay away from the icy water." He says.
Ben and Sam nod. They have learned a lesson. They thank the sailor again. They go home. They tell their parents what happened. They hug their parents. They are glad to be home. They are still friends. They still like to play with boats. But they are more careful. They do not go on boats in the winter. They wait for the spring.

One day, three brave explorers ventured into the deep, dark forest. The forest was silent, except for the rustling of leaves and snapping twigs underfoot. As soon as they reached the centre of the forest, they stumbled upon a tall, bald tree.
"This tree looks special," the first explorer said. He handed the second explorer a pin and said, "Here, weigh it."
The second explorer carefully took the pin and lightly placed it on one of the tree's branches.
Suddenly, the bald tree's branches trembled and grew larger. Its trunk creaked and growled - the tree was alive! 
"Quick! Grab what you can before it's too late!" the first explorer shouted. The three explorers ran with whatever they could as the tree chased after them. 
But it was too late. The three brave explorers were soon overpowered by the bald tree. None of them escaped, apart from the pin which the second explorer had dropped.
The explorers were never seen again. This is a story of how two brave explorers were fooled by the power of a bald tree. They will always be remembered.

"Look, Ben, I have a penny. I want to make a wish in the fountain. Do you have a penny too?" Lily asked.
Ben shook his head. He did not have a penny. He felt sad and jealous. He wanted to make a wish too.
"Can I have your penny, Lily? Please?" Ben begged.
Lily frowned. She did not want to give her penny to Ben. She wanted to keep it for herself.
"No, Ben, this is my penny. You can't have it. Go find your own penny." Lily said.
Ben was angry. He tried to grab Lily's penny from her hand. Lily pulled it away. They started to fight over the penny. They did not see the fountain behind them.
Splash! The water from the fountain sprayed them. They got wet and cold. They dropped the penny. It rolled into the fountain. They could not see it anymore.
They stopped fighting. They looked at each other. They felt silly and sorry.
"Lily, I'm sorry. I should not have tried to take your penny. That was mean." Ben said.
"Ben, I'm sorry too. I should have shared my penny with you. That was selfish." Lily said.
They hugged each other. They were friends again. They did not care about the penny anymore. They just wanted to have fun.
They ran to the slide. They slid down. They laughed. They forgot they were soaked. They were happy.

She looked so nice all dressed up. But she was still scared. Then, she saw something stupid. There was a silly clown standing on the steps of the building. He was wiggling his red nose and making funny faces. 
And Sally wasn't scared anymore. She giggled and ran towards him. She was ready to go inside and explore!

The guest was very surprised and she tried to calm the girl down. She said to the girl, if you get angry, you won't be able to play. The girl was still very mad, but she stopped shouting. The guest reminded her that if we get angry, it doesn't help anyone.
The guest said the best thing to do is to take a deep breath and release her anger. The girl thought about what the guest said and took a deep breath. She slowly let out her breath and felt her anger drop away.
The girl thanked the guest. She now felt calm and happy. Then she went back to playing with her blocks. 
The moral of the story is that when we feel angry, it's best to take a deep breath and release our anger. This will help keep us calm and help us to enjoy our playtime.

"Oh," said the girl. "Will your web make things better?" 
The spider laughed. "No, but if you pray hard enough, you'll see something wonderful. So don't stop praying!"
The girl smiled. She remembered why she was praying in the first place, and she knew it would work. She thanked the spider, then continued to pray. She prayed until the gloom had gone and everything was back to normal.

"Let's go, Tim!" Sam said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"
"I don't know, Sam," Tim said. "Mom said we should not go out of the yard. And I am scared of the hole. What if there is a big dog or a mean man?"
"Don't be scared, Tim. We can be fast and quiet. And we can replace the fence when we come back. No one will know. Come on, it will be an adventure!"
Sam grabbed Tim's hand and pulled him to the hole. They crawled through and found themselves in a different yard. There were many flowers and trees and a small pond. They also saw a big red ball.
"Wow, look at that ball!" Sam said. "It is so big and shiny! Let's play with it!"
Sam ran to the ball and kicked it hard. It flew in the air and landed in the pond with a splash. Tim followed him and laughed.
They had fun playing with the ball in the pond. They did not notice that someone was watching them from the window of the house. It was an old lady with a stern face. She did not like children in her yard. She opened the door and shouted at them.
"Hey, you! Get out of my yard! That is my ball! How dare you take it and make a mess!"
Tim and Sam were scared. They dropped the ball and ran to the hole. They crawled back to their yard and replaced the fence. They hoped the old lady would not tell their mom.
They decided to never go through the hole again. They learned that it was not nice to take things that did not belong to them. And they learned that some adventures were not worth the trouble.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Tom and Sarah. They were walking along the beach and watching the sun setting. Suddenly, Tom saw a whale in the sea.
Sarah said “Be careful Tom, the whale might get you!”
Tom replied “No, I think whales are graceful creatures.”
They decided to get closer and look at the whale from the shore. Tom said “Hey whale, how can I help you?”
The whale replied “Thank you for asking. Would you please go fishing and serve me fresh fish?”
Tom and Sarah went fishing and served the whale fresh fish. The whale thanked them and went away.
The moral of this story is that we should do our best to help others, no matter how small the job may be. As Tom and Sarah demonstrated, even a small service like providing fresh fish to a whale can make a big difference.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to spin around and around until they felt dizzy. They laughed and fell on the grass.
"Look, an animal!" Lily said, pointing to a small brown thing with a long tail. It was a mouse. It ran out of a hole and looked at them.
"Hello, mouse!" Tom said. "Do you want to play with us?"
The mouse was scared. It did not like big people. It squeaked and ran back to the hole.
"Come back, mouse!" Lily said. "We are nice. We will not hurt you."
But the mouse did not come back. It hid in the hole and waited for them to go away.
Tom and Lily were sad. They wanted to make a new friend.
"Maybe the mouse does not like to spin," Tom said. "Maybe it likes to do something else."
"Like what?" Lily asked.
"Maybe it likes to be tidy," Tom said. "Maybe it likes to clean its hole and sort its things."
Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea.
"Let's help the mouse be tidy," she said. "Let's find some things for it to use. Maybe it will like us then."
Tom agreed. They looked around the garden and found some things. They found a leaf, a twig, a pebble, a feather and a berry. They put them near the hole.
"Look, mouse!" Lily said. "We brought you some things. You can use them to make your hole nice and tidy."
They waited and watched. The mouse peeked out of the hole. It saw the things. It was curious. It came out and sniffed them. It liked the things. It picked them up and carried them to the hole.
"Thank you, big people!" the mouse said. "You are nice. You gave me things to be tidy. Do you want to see my hole?"
Tom and Lily nodded. They followed the mouse to the hole. They saw how the mouse had used the things. It had made a bed with the leaf, a door with the twig, a table with the pebble, a pillow with the feather and a snack with the berry.
"Wow, mouse!" Tom said. "Your hole is very tidy. You are very clever."
"Thank you, big people!" the mouse said. "You are very kind. Do you want to be my friends?"
Tom and Lily smiled. They said yes. They were happy. They had made a new friend. They played with the mouse and learned how to be tidy. They did not spin anymore. They did not need to. They had more fun with the mouse.

One day, they want to make a cake with a spell. They read the words in the book and wave their hands. But nothing happens. They try again and again, but still no cake.
"Maybe we need a wand," Tim says. He looks around and sees a stick on the floor. He picks it up and says, "This will do."
He points the stick at the table and says the spell again. But instead of a cake, a big ball of fire comes out of the stick. It flies across the room and strikes the curtain. The curtain catches fire and makes a lot of smoke.
"Uh-oh," Mia says. "We have to put it out."
They run to the kitchen and get some water. They splash the water on the curtain, but it is not enough. The fire grows bigger and bigger.
"Help! Help!" they shout. "We made a fire with a spell!"
Their mom hears them and comes running. She sees the fire and the smoke and the stick. She grabs a fire extinguisher and sprays the fire. She puts it out and opens the window.
"What were you doing?" she asks, very angry. "You could have burned the house down!"
"We were trying to make a cake with a spell," Tim says, looking down. "But we are clumsy with magic."
"You are not supposed to play with magic," mom says. "It is dangerous and not for children. Where did you get that book of spells?"
"We found it in the attic," Mia says, holding the book.
Mom takes the book and looks at it. She sees the words and the pictures and the symbols. She gasps and says, "This is my old book of spells. I used to play with it when I was young. But I forgot I had it. I should have thrown it away."
She hugs Tim and Mia and says, "I'm sorry, my darlings. I didn't mean to leave this book here. It was very foolish of me. But you are also very foolish for trying to do the spells. You don't know what they can do. You have to promise me you will never play with magic again."
Tim and Mia nod and say, "We promise, mom. We are sorry, too. We just wanted to make a cake."
Mom smiles and says, "Well, maybe we can make a cake together. But with no magic. Just with eggs and flour and sugar and butter. And maybe some chocolate. How does that sound?"
Tim and Mia smile and say, "That sounds yummy, mom. Can we do it now?"
Mom says, "Yes, we can. Come on, let's go to the kitchen. And no more spells, okay?"
Tim and Mia say, "Okay, mom. No more spells."

She drew a big fat desk for her teacher, with a lot of drawers and a big chair. She drew a fat bookcase with many books and a fat lamp. She drew a fat clock and a fat calendar and a fat globe. She cut out her drawings and taped them on the wall.
She was very proud of her design. She showed it to her teacher and said, "Look, teacher, I made a new classroom for you!"
Her teacher looked at her design and smiled. She said, "Thank you, Lily, for your thoughtful gift. But do you know why I don't need a new classroom?"
Lily shook her head. She did not know.
Her teacher said, "Because I already have the best classroom in the world. Do you know what makes a classroom the best?"
Lily thought for a moment. She said, "Is it the desk? Or the bookcase? Or the clock?"
Her teacher said, "No, Lily, it is not the desk, or the bookcase, or the clock. It is the students. The students make the classroom the best. They are the ones who learn and grow and share and care. They are the ones who make me happy every day. You are one of them, Lily. You are one of the best things in my classroom."
Lily smiled. She understood. She said, "I'm sorry, teacher, I did not mean to make you sad. I just wanted to make you happy."
Her teacher said, "You don't have to be sorry, Lily. You made me very happy. You showed me how creative and kind you are. You showed me how much you love to design things. And you showed me how much you love me. That is more than enough."
Lily hugged her teacher. She said, "I love you, teacher. And I love our classroom. It is the best classroom in the world."

Tim closed his eyes and counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Ready or not, here I come!" He opened his eyes and looked around. He saw Spot and Fluffy, but he did not see Kim.

Kim smiled back and said, "You are a good seeker, Tim! Let's play again! This time, you hide and I count!" Tim agreed and ran to find a hiding spot. Kim closed her eyes and counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Ready or not, here I come!" She opened her eyes and looked around. She saw Spot and Fluffy, but she did not see Tim.

Kim told them what happened. She said, "We were playing hide and seek in the wheat field. Tim tripped and hurt his knee. He cried and I helped him. We came back to you. He needs a band-aid and a hug."
Mom and dad hugged Tim and Kim. They said, "You are brave, Tim. You are kind, Kim. We are proud of you. We'll take care of you. We'll clean your wound and put a band-aid on it. We'll give you some juice and cookies. We'll read you a story. We love you."

Tim slapped the ball as hard as he could. The ball went up, up, up into the sky. But then, the ball came back down and hit the big branch. It broke the branch, and the branch fell down. Tim was sad, but he learned that it is important to be careful when playing golf.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. On Tuesday, they go to the park with their moms. The park is lively. There are many kids and dogs and birds.
Tom sees a big slide. He wants to go on it. He says to Jen, "Come on, let's go on the slide. It looks fun."
Jen is scared. The slide is too high and steep for her. She says to Tom, "No, thank you. I don't want to go on the slide. It looks scary."
Tom says, "Don't be scared. It's not scary. It's fun. I recommend it. Trust me."
Jen does not trust Tom. She shakes her head. She says, "No, thank you. I want to stay here."
Tom is mad. He says, "Fine. Be a baby. I'm going on the slide by myself."
He runs to the slide. He climbs up the ladder. He sits on the top. He smiles. He says, "Watch me, Jen. I'm going to slide down fast."
He pushes himself off. He slides down fast. He screams. He is happy.
But he slides too fast. He does not stop at the end. He flies off the slide. He lands on the ground. He hurts himself. He cries.
Jen hears him cry. She runs to him. She sees him on the ground. He is bleeding. He is sad. She says, "Oh, Tom. I'm sorry. Are you okay?"
Tom says, "No, I'm not okay. I'm hurt. I'm stupid. I should have listened to you. You were right. The slide was scary. I don't recommend it."
Jen says, "It's okay, Tom. You're not stupid. You're brave. But you were too fast. You need to be careful."
She hugs him. She says, "I'm your friend. I'm here for you."
Their moms come. They see them on the ground. They are worried. They say, "What happened? Are you okay?"
They take them to the doctor. The doctor gives Tom a bandage. He says, "You'll be fine. But you need to rest. And you need to be more careful."
Tom says, "I know. I'm sorry. I learned my lesson."
Jen says, "I'm glad you're fine. But I'm sad you're hurt."
Tom says, "I'm glad you're my friend. But I'm sad I made you scared."
They say, "I'm sorry. I forgive you."
They hug. They are still friends. But they don't go on the slide again. They play on the swings instead. The swings are not scary. They are fun. They recommend them.

Once upon a time, there were two neighbors who lived close to each other. One day, one neighbor tried to steal something from the other neighbor. He snuck into the other neighbor's yard and picked up a useful tool.
The other neighbor saw him and shouted, “What are you doing? You can’t steal from me!”
The thief was startled and quickly put the tool down and ran away, feeling very sorry for what he had done.
The moral of the story is that stealing is wrong. Everyone should be careful when trying to take someone else's things. Stealing can hurt people and will not make anyone happy. It's much better to ask for someone else's things instead of taking them without permission.

Lily was wearing a pink dress and a purple hat. She said, "No, I did not take your blue necklace. I like pink and purple, not blue."
Sara did not believe her. She thought Lily was lying. She said, "Yes, you did take it. You always take my things. Give it back to me now!"
Lily got angry. She said, "No, I did not take it. You are being mean. Go away!"

Sara and Lily stopped yelling. They looked at their mom. They felt ashamed. They said, "Sorry, mom."
Their mom said, "Why are you fighting over jewelry? Jewelry is not important. What is important is being kind and sharing with your sister. Do you understand?"
Sara and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. We understand."

Sara and Lily hugged and said, "I love you, sister." They smiled and helped their mom look for the blue necklace. They found it under the bed. Sara put it on and said, "Look, mom. It is so pretty."

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big hill and wanted to climb it. They ran up the hill, but it was very hard. They got tired and stopped to rest.
"Look, Tom, what is that?" Lily pointed to a big shape behind the trees. It was a giant. He was very tall and had a long beard and a big coat. He was carrying a big bag.
"Wow, Lily, he is so big! Do you think he is nice or mean?" Tom asked.
"I don't know, Tom. Maybe we should say hello to him. He might be lonely." Lily said.
They walked slowly to the giant. He saw them and smiled. He put down his bag and knelt down to talk to them.
"Hello, little ones. What are you doing here?" He asked in a deep voice.
"Hello, Mr. Giant. We are playing in the park. We climbed the big hill and saw you. What are you doing here?" Lily asked.
"I am collecting things for my home. I live far away, in the mountains. I like to find nice things to decorate my home. Do you want to see what I have in my bag?" He asked.
"Yes, please, Mr. Giant. We are curious." Tom said.
The giant opened his bag and showed them what he had. He had a big clock, a big lamp, a big hat, a big book, and a big ball. He told them stories about where he found them and what they were for.
Lily and Tom liked the giant. He was very kind and patient. He answered all their questions and played with them. He even let them try his big hat and his big ball.
They had a lot of fun with the giant. They forgot about the time and the park. They only remembered when they heard their mom calling them.
"Mom is here, Tom. We have to go." Lily said.
"OK, Lily. Bye, Mr. Giant. Thank you for showing us your things and playing with us. You are very nice." Tom said.
"Bye, little ones. You are very brave and friendly. I hope to see you again. Have a good day." The giant said.
He gave them a gentle hug and a wave. He picked up his bag and walked away.
Lily and Tom ran to their mom. They told her about the giant and his things. She smiled and nodded. She did not believe them, but she was happy to see them happy.
They shrugged and did not mind. They knew the giant was real and they liked him. They hoped to see him again. They waved to the hill and said goodbye.

Lily liked to read novels. She had many novels in her room. She liked to look at the pictures and make up stories in her head. Sometimes she read the words too, but they were hard.
One day, Lily saw a big novel on the shelf. It was her mom's novel. It had a shiny cover and many pages. Lily wanted to read it. She climbed on a chair and reached for the novel. But the novel was too heavy for her. It slipped from her hand and fell on the floor. The novel made a loud noise.
Mom heard the noise and came to Lily's room. She saw the novel on the floor and Lily on the chair. She was angry.
"Lily, what are you doing?" Mom asked. "That is my novel. You are not supposed to touch it. You are being naughty."
Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to be naughty. She just wanted to read the novel.
"I'm sorry, Mom," Lily said. "I like novels. I wanted to see your novel. I did not know it was so heavy. It fell by itself."
Mom sighed. She picked up the novel and checked for damage. She was glad it was not torn or stained. She put it back on the shelf.
"Lily, I know you like novels, but you have to be careful. You could have hurt yourself or the novel. You have to ask me before you touch my things. Do you understand?" Mom said.
Lily nodded. She understood. She hugged Mom and said, "I love you, Mom. I'm sorry I was naughty."
Mom hugged Lily back and said, "I love you too, Lily. I'm sorry I was angry. Next time, I will read you a novel if you want. But now, you have to get down from the chair and clean up your room."
Lily got down from the chair and cleaned up her room. She was happy that Mom was not angry anymore. She hoped that Mom would read her a novel soon. She liked novels.

"Wow, they smell so good!" Lily said.

They looked at the flowers. They were pink, yellow and white. They had many petals and a yellow middle.
"I don't know. Maybe we can ask Mom or Dad. They know many things," Lily said.
They decided to pick some flowers for Mom and Dad. They reached for the bush and pulled some flowers. But they did not see the bees. The bees were hiding in the bush. They did not like Tom and Lily taking their flowers. They came out of the bush and buzzed angrily.
"Ouch! Ouch! Ouch!" Tom and Lily cried. They dropped the flowers and ran away. The bees followed them and stung them on their arms and legs.
They ran to Mom and Dad, who were sitting on a bench. They showed them their stings and tears.
"Mom, Dad, help! The bees hurt us!" they said.
Mom and Dad hugged them and checked their stings. They gave them some ice and medicine. They told them to be careful with the bees and the flowers.
"Why did the bees hurt us? We just wanted to give you some flowers," Lily said.
"Bees are very protective of their flowers. They make honey from them. They think you are stealing their food. They don't like that," Mom said.
"That's not fair. The flowers are for everyone. The bees are mean," Tom said.
"Bees are not mean. They are just doing their job. They are important for the plants and the animals. They help them grow and live. They are not disgusting. They are amazing," Dad said.
Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not understand. They did not like the bees. They thought they were disgusting. They did not want to discuss them anymore. They wanted to play something else. They asked Mom and Dad if they could go to the slide. Mom and Dad said yes. They took their ice and medicine and went to the slide. They forgot about the bees and the flowers. They had fun on the slide. They laughed and smiled. They were happy.

Lily liked to play in the pond with her friend, Ben. They liked to look for frogs and fish and bugs. One day, they saw a very small frog on a big leaf. It was green and brown and had black spots.
"Look, Ben, a frog!" Lily said. "Can I hold it?"
Ben nodded and helped Lily catch the frog. She was very gentle and careful. She put the frog in her hand and looked at it. It was soft and wet and had big eyes.
"Hello, frog," Lily said. "You are so small and cute. Do you want to be my pet?"
The frog did not like being held. It wanted to go back to the pond. It croaked and wriggled and tried to jump.
"Let me go, let me go!" the frog said. Lily did not understand the frog, but she heard a noise.
"What did you say, frog?" Lily asked.
"Let me go, let me go!" the frog repeated. It demanded to be free.
Ben heard the frog too. He knew what it wanted.
"Lily, the frog wants to go back to the pond," Ben said. "It is not happy here. We should let it go."
Lily felt sad. She liked the frog and wanted to keep it. But she also wanted the frog to be happy.
"OK, Ben," Lily said. "We will let the frog go. But can we say goodbye first?"
Ben smiled and nodded. They both said goodbye to the frog and thanked it for letting them hold it. Then they put the frog back on the leaf and watched it hop into the water.
"Bye, frog," Lily said. "Maybe we will see you again."
The frog was glad to be free. It croaked and waved to Lily and Ben. Then it swam away with the other frogs.
The end.

Sara and Ben were twins who loved candy. They always asked their mom for candy when they went to the store. Mom said they could have one candy each, but they had to eat it after dinner.
One day, they saw a big jar of candy on the kitchen table. It had a note that said "For Grandma's birthday. Do not touch." Sara and Ben looked at each other. They wanted to try the candy so much. They thought mom would not notice if they took one each.
They reached for the jar, but then they heard a voice behind them. "What are you doing, children?" It was mom. She looked angry. "Did you not read the note? This candy is for Grandma. You cannot have it. It will spoil your dinner and your teeth."
Sara and Ben felt ashamed. They knew they did something bad. They said sorry to mom. Mom hugged them and said, "I forgive you, but you have to learn to respect other people's things. How would you feel if someone took your candy without asking?"
Sara and Ben said they would feel sad and mad. Mom said, "That's how Grandma would feel if she saw the jar empty. She loves candy too, you know. She is very graceful and kind. She always shares her candy with you when she visits. Don't you want to make her happy on her birthday?"
Sara and Ben nodded. They said they loved Grandma and wanted to give her a nice gift. Mom said, "The best gift you can give her is your love and your good manners. Now, go wash your hands and get ready for dinner. Maybe, if you eat well and behave well, you can have a small piece of candy later."
Sara and Ben smiled. They ran to the bathroom and washed their hands. They decided to never touch the candy jar again. They wanted to be good children and make mom and Grandma proud.

"But I want to see the wheel. It looks fun," Lily said.
She ran to the mill and Tom followed her. They went inside the mill and saw many machines and bags of flour. They touched everything and made a big mess.
Suddenly, they heard a loud voice.
"Hey, who are you? What are you doing here?" It was the miller, the man who worked at the mill. He was angry and scared them.
"We are sorry, sir. We just wanted to see the mill," Tom said.
"Well, you should not be here. This is not a place for children. You could get hurt or break something. You have to leave now and never come back," the miller said.
He took them outside and saw their mom. She was looking for them and was very worried.
"Mom, we are sorry. We went to the mill and made a mess," Lily said.
Mom was frustrated and sad. She thanked the miller and took Lily and Tom home.
She said, "You have been very naughty. You did not listen to me and you went to a dangerous place. You could have been hurt or lost. You have to punish for what you did. You have to clean your room and no TV for a week."
Lily and Tom felt bad. They knew they did wrong. They said sorry to mom and hugged her. They went to their room and cleaned it. They learned their lesson and never went to the mill again.

Ben smiled and grabbed the symbol. It had a star and a moon on it. "And I am a wise wizard, and this is my powerful symbol!" he said. He waved it in the air and made funny noises.
They played for a long time, having fun and imagining adventures. They did not see the spider web in the corner of the box. It was very big and sticky. A spider lived there. It was not playful. It was hungry.
The spider watched the children play. It waited for the right moment. It wanted to catch them in its web. It saw Lily put down the bow and reach for a hat. It saw Ben drop the symbol and look for a wand. It saw its chance.
It crawled out of the web and jumped on the box. It was fast and quiet. Lily and Ben did not hear it. They did not see it. They only felt it when it landed on their heads.
"Ah!" they screamed. They dropped their toys and ran out of the attic. They were scared and angry. They did not like the spider. It was not nice. It was mean.
They told their mom what happened. She hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. It was just a spider. It can't hurt you. It was probably more scared of you than you were of it."
She took them back to the attic and showed them the spider. It was still on the box. It looked small and harmless. It did not move. It was not hungry anymore. It was full.
Lily and Ben felt sorry for the spider. They realized it was just a living thing, like them. They decided to be kind to it. They gave it a name and a toy. They called it Bob and gave it the symbol. They hoped it would like it.
They said goodbye to Bob and took the bow and the hat. They went back to their room and continued their play. They were happy and brave. They were archers and wizards. They were best friends.

The stable was big and smelly. Lily saw many horses inside, some brown, some black, some white. They neighed and snorted when they saw the farmer and Lily. The farmer gave Lily a big fork and showed her how to scoop the hay from a pile and put it in the horses' troughs. Lily tried to do the same, but the fork was heavy and the hay was prickly. She dropped some hay on the floor and on her head.
"Oops!" Lily said. "Sorry, horses!"
The horses did not mind. They ate the hay happily and licked Lily's hand. One of them, a white horse with a black spot on his nose, nuzzled Lily's cheek. Lily giggled and hugged his neck.
"Hello, horse!" Lily said. "What is your name?"
The farmer smiled and said, "His name is Spot. He likes you, Lily. You are a good helper. Do you want to ride him?"
Lily's eyes widened. She had never ridden a horse before. She nodded eagerly and said, "Yes, please!"
The farmer lifted Lily and put her on Spot's back. He held the reins and walked with them around the stable. Lily felt the wind in her hair and the warmth of Spot's fur. She felt happy and brave.
"I love you, Spot!" Lily said. "You are my friend!"
Spot neighed and shook his mane. He loved Lily, too. He was glad she served him hay and gave him a hug. He was a lucky horse.

Once upon a time there were two friends called Mary and Bob. Mary was very friendly and Bob was very selfish.
One day Mary and Bob were playing together near Mary's desk. Mary wanted to share her favourite toy but Bob said "No! It's mine!" Mary was very sad and Bob was being selfish.
Then something strange happened - the desk began to part. It split into two pieces and behind it was a magical garden!
Mary and Bob were very excited and they ran into the garden. While playing, they spotted a big bright butterfly. Mary asked Bob if he wanted to share her net and he said "Yes, please!". Both of them caught the butterfly and let it go.
The garden then disappeared and their desk was back to normal.
Since then, Mary and Bob have played together nicely, sharing all their toys.

Lily and Ben are playing in the garden. They have a big box of toys. They like to make cars and houses and animals with the toys. But they also make a lot of mess. The toys are everywhere on the grass and the dirt.
"Look, Lily, I made a big truck!" Ben says. He shows Lily his toy truck. It has four wheels and a door and a window.
"Wow, Ben, that's a nice truck!" Lily says. She likes Ben's truck. She wants to play with it too. "Can I have a turn?" she asks.
"OK, Lily, but you have to be careful. The truck has a lock. You need a key to open the door." Ben says. He gives Lily a small toy key. "Here, this is the key. You have to put it in the hole and turn it. Then you can unlock the door and get in the truck."
Lily takes the key and tries to unlock the door. She puts the key in the hole and turns it. But the key is stuck. She can't unlock the door. She pulls and pulls, but the key won't come out.
"Ben, help me! The key is stuck!" Lily cries. She is sad and scared. She thinks she broke the truck.
Ben runs to Lily and tries to help her. He pulls the key too, but it won't come out. He is angry and frustrated. He thinks Lily ruined his truck.
"Lily, you are so messy! You don't know how to play with my truck! You made the key stuck!" Ben shouts. He pushes Lily away from the truck.
Lily falls on the ground and hurts her knee. She feels a sharp pain and a warm wetness. She looks at her knee and sees blood. She starts to cry.
"Ben, you are so mean! You pushed me and made me bleed! You don't want to share your truck!" Lily sobs. She holds her knee and feels sorry for herself.
Ben hears Lily cry and sees her blood. He feels sorry for her too. He knows he was mean and he hurt her. He wants to make her feel better.
"Lily, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to push you and make you bleed. I was mad because the key was stuck. But it's not your fault. It's just a toy. It doesn't matter." Ben says. He goes to Lily and hugs her.
"Ben, I'm sorry too. I didn't mean to make the key stuck. I just wanted to play with your truck. But it's not worth it. It's just a toy. You matter more." Lily says. She hugs Ben back.
They both smile and wipe their tears. They forget about the truck and the key and the lock. They go to the house and ask their mom for a band-aid and a cookie. They are friends again. They decide to play with something else. Something that doesn't make a mess.

Whiskers started to teach Lucy how to play the piano. They were having so much fun. But then, something unexpected happened. The piano started to freeze! Lucy and Whiskers looked at each other in surprise. They did not know why the piano was so cold.

The snowman helped them unfreeze the piano. Then, they all played music together. Lucy learned that she was not stupid. She just needed a little help from her new friends.

Lily was scared. She saw blood on Tom's head and hand. She saw smoke from the stove. She smelled something bad. She cried and cried.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big kite in the sky. It is red and yellow and blue. The wind makes it fly high and fast.
"Wow, look at the kite!" Lily says. "I want to fly a kite too!"
"Me too!" Tom says. "Let's make our own kites!"
They run to the house and find some paper, sticks, string and tape. They cut and stick and tie and make two kites. One is green and purple and pink. The other is orange and black and white.
They run back outside and hold their kites. They wait for the wind to blow. But the wind is very quiet. Their kites do not fly. They only hang down.
"Oh no, the wind is gone!" Lily says. "What can we do?"
"Maybe we can make the wind!" Tom says. He has an idea. He is very smart. He takes a big fan from the house and plugs it in. He turns it on and points it at the kites.
The fan makes a loud noise. It also makes a lot of wind. The wind hits the kites and makes them fly. Lily and Tom are very happy. They laugh and clap and run with their kites.
But the fan is too strong. It makes too much wind. The wind pulls the kites hard. The string breaks. The kites fly away.
"Oh no, our kites are gone!" Tom says. He is very sad. He drops the fan and sits on the ground.
Lily sees Tom is sad. She wants to help him. She is very kind. She goes to him and hugs him. She says, "It's okay, Tom. We can make new kites. We still have paper and sticks and string and tape. And we still have each other. We are friends. We support each other."
Tom feels better. He hugs Lily back. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are right. We are friends. We support each other. And we still have fun."
They smile and get up. They go to the house and make new kites. They are more careful with the fan. They fly their kites and have fun. They are happy.
The end.

"No, Sam!" Lily said. "That is not fair. The ants found it first. They brought it to their hill. It is their treasure. You should not take it. You should put it back."

She took the stone from Sam and Lily. She said, "You were very naughty. You destroyed the ants' home and took their treasure. You should say sorry to the ants and put the stone back. Then you should go to your room and think about what you did."
Sam and Lily felt sorry. They said sorry to the ants and put the stone back. They went to their room and thought about what they did. They learned to respect the ants and their home. They never poked the hill again.

Ben and Lily liked to play at the park. They liked to swing, climb and slide. One day, they saw a big mill near the park. It had a tall tower and a big wheel that turned with the wind.
"Let's go see the mill!" Ben said.
"OK, but we have to be careful. Mom said not to go too far," Lily said.
They ran to the mill and looked around. They saw a door that was open. They peeked inside and saw a lot of sacks and machines.
"Wow, this is where they make flour!" Ben said.
"Flour? What is that?" Lily asked.
"It's what you use to make bread and cake and cookies. Mom uses it all the time," Ben said.
"Can we take some?" Lily asked.
"No, that would be bad. It belongs to the miller. He is the man who works here. He is very reliable. He makes good flour for everyone," Ben said.
"Who is the miller? Where is he?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Maybe he is outside. Maybe he is on the tower. Let's go see," Ben said.
They went outside and saw a ladder that led to the tower. Ben wanted to climb it, but Lily was scared.
"Ben, don't go up there. It's too high. You might fall," Lily said.
"Don't worry, Lily. I'll be careful. I just want to see the view. You can wait here," Ben said.
He climbed the ladder and reached the top of the tower. He saw the park, the town and the fields. He also saw the miller, who was walking back to the mill.
"Hi, miller!" Ben shouted.
The miller looked up and saw Ben. He was surprised and angry.
"Hey, you! What are you doing up there? Get down right now! This is not a place for children!" the miller yelled.
Ben was scared and sorry. He climbed down the ladder as fast as he could. He ran to Lily and they both said sorry to the miller.
The miller was still mad, but he calmed down a bit. He told them that the mill was dangerous and they should not go inside or on the tower. He also told them that they should listen to their mom and not go too far from the park.
Ben and Lily nodded and promised to be good. They thanked the miller for his flour and ran back to the park. They decided to play on the slide, where it was safe and fun. They learned their lesson and never went to the mill again.

Once upon a time, there was a cool table in the middle of a forest. Every day, it seemed to get a little bit heavier. But no one knew why. 
One day, a mother and her three-year-old daughter came across the table in the forest. 
The mother saw how heavy the table was, and said to her daughter: “Can you help me weigh this table? It looks much too heavy for me to lift.” 
The daughter tried her very best to help her mother weigh the table. After a few minutes of struggling and pushing, they finally got it to move. 
Suddenly, they heard an unfamiliar voice. “Thank you for helping me,” said the voice. 
The mother and her daughter looked around, but they couldn't see anyone. Then, they noticed a small blue fairy hiding under the table. 
The fairy explained that it had been the one weighing down the table all this time. 
The daughter smiled and said: “That's ok. It was cool to help have helped you.” 
The mother smiled too and said to her daughter: “See, we can all make a big difference when we work together.” 
The small blue fairy flew away, and the mother and daughter went home together. This story teaches us the importance of teamwork and helping others in need.

"Mom, why did my rose die?" Lily asked.
"Because you picked it, my dear," her mom said. "Roses need water and sun and soil to live. When you keep them away from these things, they cannot grow and bloom. They are happier in the garden, where they can share their beauty with everyone."
Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to hurt the rose. She wanted to make it happy. She learned that keeping something for herself was not always good. Sometimes, it was better to let it go and enjoy it from afar.
She gave the rose back to the garden. She buried it in the soil and said, "I'm sorry, rose. Thank you for being so pretty. I hope you will grow again and make more roses."
Then, she hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. You are like a rose. You are pretty and sweet and smooth. But I will not keep you. I will share you with everyone."
Her mom smiled and kissed her. She said, "I love you too, Lily. You are like a rose too. You are bright and lovely and soft. And you have learned a valuable lesson. Keeping is not always caring. Sometimes, caring is letting go."

"That's a cauliflower, Lily. It's a vegetable that you can eat raw or cooked. Do you want to try a piece?" Mom said.
Lily nodded. She liked to try new things. Mom cut a small piece of cauliflower and gave it to Lily. Lily put it in her mouth and chewed. It was crunchy and a little bitter. She made a face and spit it out.
"Yuck! I don't like cauliflower!" Lily said.
Mom smiled and said, "That's okay, Lily. You don't have to like everything. Maybe you'll like it better when it's cooked. Can you help me put the cauliflower in this pot of water?"
Lily said yes. She wanted to help mom. She picked up the cauliflower and walked to the stove. But she was not careful. She tripped over the rug and dropped the cauliflower. It fell on the floor and broke into many pieces.
"Oh no! I'm sorry, mom!" Lily said.
Mom came over and hugged Lily. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's okay. Accidents happen. You're not hurt, are you?"
Lily shook her head. She was not hurt, but she felt bad. She wanted to be a good helper.
Mom said, "You are a good helper, Lily. And you are a brave girl for trying something new. Let's clean up the mess and finish the salad. Do you want to help me wash the lettuce? It's green and leafy and graceful."
Lily said yes. She liked lettuce. She hoped it was not bitter like cauliflower. She followed mom to the sink and washed the lettuce. She thought it was pretty and graceful. She smiled and said, "I like lettuce, mom. Can I have some in my salad?"
Mom said, "Of course, Lily. You can have as much lettuce as you want. And maybe someday you'll like cauliflower too. But for now, let's enjoy our salad and have a nice dinner."

One day, a little boy named Ben and his big sister Lily went to the garden to dig up some potatoes. They liked to help their mom make potato soup for dinner. Ben had a small shovel and Lily had a big one. They worked hard and found many potatoes under the dirt.
"Look, Ben, this is a mighty potato!" Lily said, holding up a large and round potato. "It's bigger than your head!"
Ben laughed and reached for the potato. He wanted to see how big it was. But as soon as he touched it, the potato disappeared!
"Hey, where did it go?" Ben asked, looking around.
Lily was surprised too. She did not see the potato anywhere. She wondered if it was a magic potato that could vanish.
"Maybe it went back to the ground," she said. "Or maybe it flew away to the sky."
Ben was curious. He wanted to find the potato. He thought maybe it was hiding somewhere. He looked under the leaves, behind the rocks, and in the bushes. He did not find the potato.
"Come on, Ben, let's go back to the house," Lily said. "We have enough potatoes for the soup. Maybe the potato will come back later."
Ben nodded and followed his sister. He still wondered where the potato went. He hoped it was happy and safe.
When they got to the house, they saw their mom in the kitchen. She was chopping some carrots and onions for the soup. She smiled when she saw them.
"Wow, you two did a great job!" she said. "You found so many potatoes!"
She took the basket from Lily and poured the potatoes into a big pot of water. She put the pot on the stove and turned on the heat.
"Can you help me stir the soup, Ben?" she asked.
Ben nodded and climbed on a stool. He took a wooden spoon and stirred the soup. He liked to help his mom cook. He smelled the yummy soup and felt hungry.
Suddenly, he saw something pop out of the soup. It was the mighty potato! It had not disappeared after all. It had just jumped into the basket when Ben touched it. It had been hiding among the other potatoes. It had been waiting for the right moment to escape.
"Look, mom, look!" Ben shouted. "It's the mighty potato! It's back!"
Mom and Lily looked at the pot. They saw the mighty potato too. They were amazed and amused. They laughed and clapped.
"What a clever potato!" mom said. "It must have a lot of fun. But I'm sorry, potato, you can't stay in the soup. You have to go back to the garden."
She took a big spoon and scooped the potato out of the pot. She wrapped it in a napkin and gave it to Ben.
"Here, Ben, you can take the potato back to the garden," she said. "Maybe it will make some friends there. Maybe it will grow more mighty potatoes."
Ben smiled and took the potato. He felt happy and proud. He had found a magic potato. He had a new friend.
He ran to the garden and dug a hole. He put the potato in the hole and covered it with dirt. He watered it and said goodbye.
"Bye, mighty potato," he said. "Thank you for the fun. I hope you have a good life. Maybe I'll see you again someday."
He waved and went back to the house. He joined his mom and sister for dinner. They ate the potato soup and enjoyed it. They talked about the mighty potato and laughed. They had a good time. They had a good story.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady who lived deep in a cave. Every morning, she would stir up a pot of delicious smelling soup. One morning she noticed a small creature peeking around the corner, who said to her, "That soup smells so yummy! Can I try some?" 
The elderly lady was surprised, as she had never seen anyone in her cave before. She shook her head and said, "No, this soup is only for me. I have to have something to eat." 
The creature was disappointed, but it did not give up. "Please," it asked in a sweet voice, "I'm very hungry and I haven't eaten for days!" 
The elderly lady felt sorry for the little creature and reluctantly agreed to let it have a bit of her soup. She smiled as the creature ate hungrily and reassured it that it would be alright. 
Just then, the creature stopped stirring and said, "I'm so full! Thank you for the soup, it was delicious!" 
The elderly lady was very pleased and said to the creature, "You are very welcome here anytime. Now, go out and explore the world, little one!" 
And so, the creature went out into the world, happy and full of energy, while the elderly lady stayed in her cave, stirring her pot of soup.

"Sure, why not? Let's try it," Sam says.
They each take a bite of the pepper. They make a funny face. The pepper is very spicy. It burns their mouth and tongue. They run to the kitchen. They need water.
"Mom, Mom, help! We ate a spicy sock!" Tom cries.
"A spicy sock? What do you mean?" Mom asks.
She sees the pepper in their hands. She laughs.
"That is not a sock, boys. That is a pepper. It is very spicy. You should not eat it like that. Here, drink some water. It will make you feel better," Mom says.
She gives them a glass of water. They drink it. They feel better.
"Sorry, Mom. We did not know. It looked like a ball," Tom says.
"It's okay, boys. Next time, ask me before you taste something new. And please, do not eat socks. They are not food. They are for your feet," Mom says.
She hugs them. They hug her back.
They learned a new word today. Spicy. They do not like spicy food. They like sweet food. Like cookies. Mom gives them a cookie. They smile. They taste the cookie. It is yummy. They are happy.

A little boy named Tim saw the wagon and wanted to play with it. But his friend, Sue, wanted to play with it too. They both pulled the wagon, trying to take it for themselves. "I want the wagon!" Tim shouted. "No, I want it!" Sue yelled back. They were not happy and started to cry.
A wise old man saw the children fighting. He walked over and said, "Children, why are you fighting over the wagon? You can both play with it and have fun together." Tim and Sue stopped crying and looked at each other. They decided to share the wagon and play together.
Tim and Sue had so much fun playing with the ancient wagon. They took turns pulling each other and laughed all day long. They learned that sharing the wagon was more fun than fighting over it.
The moral of the story is that sharing is better than fighting, and playing together is more fun than playing alone.
