Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb it.
"Let's go up the tree," Tom said. "It looks fun."
"I don't know," Lily said. "It looks high. What if we fall?"
"Don't be scared," Tom said. "We are brave. We can do it."
They went to the tree and started to climb. They held on to the branches and moved up. They felt happy and proud. They reached the top and looked around. They saw the sky, the birds and the flowers. They felt wonder.
"Wow, this is so pretty," Lily said. "We are so high."
"Yes, this is amazing," Tom said. "We are the best climbers."
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was thunder. They saw dark clouds and lightning. They felt fear.
"Oh no, it's a storm," Lily said. "We have to go down."
"Quick, follow me," Tom said. "Be careful."
They tried to climb down, but it was hard. The wind was strong and the rain was wet. The branches were slippery and shaky. They lost their grip and balance. They screamed.
"Help, help," they cried.
A man heard them. He was a park ranger. He ran to the tree and saw them. He had a rope and a ladder. He threw the rope to them and told them to hold on. He climbed the ladder and reached them. He wrapped the rope around them and helped them down. He was kind and strong.
"Are you okay?" he asked.
"Yes, thank you," they said.
"You are lucky," he said. "That was a dangerous thing to do. The tree could have been struck by lightning. You should never climb a tree during a storm. You could get hurt."
"We are sorry," they said. "We didn't know. We were just having fun."
"I understand," he said. "But you have to be careful and listen to the weather. Climbing a tree is fun, but only when it's safe. Do you promise?"
"Yes, we promise," they said.
"Good," he said. "Now, let's go to the shelter and dry off. You can have some hot chocolate and cookies. How does that sound?"
"That sounds good," they said.
They followed him to the shelter. They felt grateful and sorry. They learned a lesson. They still liked to climb trees, but only when it was sunny and calm. They were brave, but also smart.

Lily giggled. She liked the bald eagle. She thought it was funny.
"Can I see the book?" she asked.
"OK, but be careful. Don't get it wet!" Ben said. He gave her the book.
Lily opened the book and looked at the pages. She saw a giraffe, a zebra, a snake, and a penguin. She liked the penguin. She thought it was cute.
"Look, Ben, this is a penguin. He has a black and white coat. And he can swim in the cold water. He is not afraid of the splash!" Lily said.
She held the book over the water and pretended to make the penguin swim. She moved the book up and down and made splash sounds.
Ben watched her and smiled. He thought it was fun.

Splash!
The book got wet. The pages got soggy. The pictures got blurry.
Lily gasped. She dropped the book. She looked at Ben. She was scared.
"Ben, I'm sorry! I didn't mean to get the book wet!" she said.

Lily smiled. She hugged him back. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I'm sorry for the book. I love you."

Tim wants to try the hat too. He takes the scissors and cuts a hole in the hat. He makes a hole for his eyes. He puts the hat on his head. He looks in the mirror. He laughs. "I look funny too!"

Tim and Sam are scared. They panic. They do not know what to say. They are sorry. They did not mean to cut the hat or the hair. They just wanted to play.
"Sorry, dad. Sorry, Tim. We were playing. We did not know. We are sorry." they say.
Tim's dad sighs. He is not angry anymore. He is calm. He hugs Tim and Sam. He knows they are good boys. He knows they made a mistake. He knows they are sorry.
"It's okay, boys. I forgive you. But you have to be careful with scissors. They are sharp. They can cut things. They can hurt you. Do you understand?" he says.
Tim and Sam nod. They understand. They are careful. They do not play with scissors anymore. They play with crayons and stickers. They make new shapes and animals and cars. They are happy. Tim's dad is happy too. He buys a new hat. He likes his new hat. He still loves his old hat. He still loves Tim. He does not mind his bald spot. He thinks it is funny. He laughs.

"OK, mom. But can we swing a little more?" Anna said.
"No, honey. It is not safe to swing when there is thunder and lightning. Come on, let's go," Anna's mom said.

She kissed her teddy bear and put it on her bed. She climbed on her bed and pulled the blanket over her. She closed her eyes and smiled. She dreamed of swinging in the park with her teddy bear and Ben. She was happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big tree with many nuts on it. They wanted to pick some nuts and eat them.
"Look, Ben, nuts!" Lily said. "Let's get some."
"OK, Lily, but be careful. The tree is high and the nuts are hard," Ben said.
They climbed the tree and reached for the nuts. But the nuts were not easy to get. They were stuck to the branches and had prickly shells. Lily and Ben tried to pull and twist the nuts, but they could not.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a squirrel. The squirrel was angry. It wanted the nuts for itself. It ran up the tree and started to chatter and scold at Lily and Ben.
"Hey, these are my nuts! Go away, you silly kids!" the squirrel said.
Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to fight with the squirrel. They let go of the nuts and climbed down the tree. But as they did, they slipped and fell. They landed on the grass with a thud.
"Ouch!" Lily and Ben said.
They looked at each other. They had dirt and leaves on their clothes and hair. They felt silly and embarrassed. They hoped no one saw them.
But someone did. It was their mom. She was sitting on a bench and watching them. She saw what happened. She got up and walked to them. She smiled and hugged them.
"Are you OK, my sweeties?" she asked.
"Yes, mom, we are OK. Just a little dirty and sore," Lily and Ben said.
Mom kissed their heads and brushed off their clothes and hair. She was gentle and kind. She did not scold them.
"It's OK, my loves. You were just curious and adventurous. But next time, be more careful and respectful of the animals and their food. They work hard to find and store their nuts. They don't like to share them with strangers," she said.
Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They said sorry to the squirrel and the tree. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with something else. They saw a ball and a hoop. They ran to them and had fun. They forgot about the nuts and the squirrel. They were happy and safe.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they are thirsty. They go to the kitchen to get some juice.
"Can you send me the juice, please?" Anna asks Ben. Ben is holding the juice bottle.
"OK, here you go," Ben says. He tries to send the juice to Anna, but he throws it too hard. The juice bottle flies in the air and lands on the floor. The juice spills everywhere.
"Oh no!" Anna and Ben say. They look at the mess. They are sad and scared. They do not want to get in trouble.
"Mommy! Daddy! Help!" they cry. Mommy and Daddy come to the kitchen. They see the juice on the floor. They are not happy.
"What happened here?" Mommy asks.
"We wanted some juice, but Ben threw it too hard and it broke," Anna says.
"Is that true, Ben?" Daddy asks.
"Yes, I'm sorry. I did not mean to do it," Ben says.
Mommy and Daddy sigh. They are not angry, but they are disappointed.
"Anna and Ben, you should be more careful. Juice is not a toy. You should not throw it or waste it. You should ask for help if you need it. Do you understand?" Mommy says.
"Yes, Mommy. We understand. We are sorry," Anna and Ben say.
"OK, then. Let's clean up this mess together. And then we can have some normal juice in a cup. How does that sound?" Daddy says.
"Good. Thank you, Mommy and Daddy," Anna and Ben say.
They help Mommy and Daddy clean up the juice. They learn their lesson. They do not throw juice anymore. They drink it nicely. They are good friends.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big aeroplane in the sky. It was white and shiny and made a loud noise.
"Wow, look at the aeroplane!" Lily said. "It is so big and fast. I want to fly in an aeroplane one day."
"Me too," Tom said. "But how do they fly? How do they stay in the air?"
Lily thought for a moment. She was very smart. She remembered what her dad had told her.
"They have wings, like birds," she said. "And they have engines, like cars. The wings help them lift up and the engines help them move forward. That's how they fly."
Tom nodded. He was impressed. He thought Lily was very clever.
"That makes sense," he said. "But I have another question. How do they land? How do they come down?"
Lily thought again. She was not sure. She had never seen an aeroplane land.
"Maybe they have wheels, like bikes," she said. "And maybe they have brakes, like cars. The wheels help them touch the ground and the brakes help them stop. That's how they land."

One day, Sophie went over to Amanda’s house to play. When Sophie got there, Amanda pulled out a wire. She started to tease Sophie with it, waving it around her head. ‘Amanda, stop!’ Sophie said. But Amanda kept teasing her.
Sophie was getting very frustrated. She grabbed the wire from Amanda’s hand and held it tight. ‘Why are you teasing me?’ she asked.
Amanda smiled. ‘Because it’s fun! I’m so lucky to have a wire, I can tease you with it because I’m wealthy.’ she said.
Sophie thought for a moment, then smiled too. ‘Okay, if you are so wealthy then we can play together with the wire. That would be much more fun for both of us!’ she said. And so, the two friends started playing with the wire together.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a polite girl named Amy. Amy had a little garden where she grew her favorite food, peppers. Every day, she would water her pepper plants and watch them grow.
One day, Amy went to her garden to pick some peppers for dinner. But when she looked at her plants, all the peppers had vanished! "Oh no!" cried Amy, "Where did my peppers go?" Just then, she saw a little rabbit hopping near the garden. She asked the rabbit, "Did you see who took my peppers?"
The rabbit looked at Amy and said, "I saw a big bird fly away with your peppers. I can help you get them back!" Amy and the rabbit went on a journey to find the big bird. They walked and hopped through the forest, looking for the bird's nest.
Finally, they found the nest on top of a tall tree. The big bird was there, and so were Amy's peppers! Amy politely asked the bird, "Can I please have my peppers back?" The bird looked down at Amy and the rabbit and said, "I took your peppers because I thought they were pretty. I didn't know they were your food. I'm sorry."
The big bird gave Amy her peppers back, and they all became friends. From that day on, Amy shared her peppers with the bird and the rabbit, and they all lived happily together.

"I want vanilla," Ben said.

Spot was watching them with his tongue out. He wanted some ice cream too. He barked and wagged his tail.
"Can Spot have some ice cream?" Mia asked the man.
"Sorry, kids. Ice cream is not good for dogs. It can make them sick," the man said.
"But he looks so hungry," Ben said.
The man smiled and reached into his cart. He took out a bone and offered it to Spot.
"Here, this is for Spot. It is delicious and healthy for dogs," the man said.
Spot sniffed the bone and wagged his tail harder. He took the bone and ran to a shady spot under a tree. He chewed the bone and made happy noises.
Ben and Mia finished their ice cream and joined Spot. They petted him and told him he was a good dog.
They all enjoyed their treats in the park.

Lily and Tom are playing in their room. They have a big scale that can weigh things. They like to put different toys on the scale and see how heavy they are.
"Look, Tom, this bear is very heavy!" Lily says, holding a big, fluffy bear. "It makes the scale go down a lot!"
"Let me see!" Tom says, taking the bear from Lily. He puts it on the scale and watches the needle move. "Wow, you are right! The bear is heavier than the car and the ball!"
They take turns weighing different toys and comparing them. They have fun seeing how the scale changes.
Then, Lily has an idea. She opens a drawer in their dresser and takes out a black hat. It is their dad's hat. He wears it when he goes to work.
"Tom, look at this!" Lily says, holding the hat. "Do you think it is heavy or light?"
Tom shrugs. "I don't know. Maybe light?"
"Let's find out!" Lily says, running to the scale. She puts the hat on the scale and waits.
But nothing happens. The scale does not move at all. The hat is too light to weigh.
Lily and Tom are confused. They look at the hat and the scale.
"Why is the hat not heavy?" Lily asks.
"I don't know," Tom says. "Maybe it is magic?"
They giggle and try to weigh the hat again. But it still does not work.
They hear their mom calling them for lunch. They put the hat back in the drawer and run to the kitchen.
They forget about the hat and the scale. But they do not know that the hat is not really magic. It is just very old and has a hole in it. And inside the hole, there is a feather. A very light feather that makes the hat weigh nothing.

Once there was a family who lived by a river. Every day the dad would take his two kids to the river to feed the ducks. One day, the dad noticed that a bridge over the river was broken. He warned his kids to be careful, as the broken bridge was dangerous. 
The dad told the kids he had to repair the bridge. But a job like this would cost a lot of money which the dad didn't have. The kids wanted to help, but they had nothing to offer.
The family went home and the next day the kids asked their dad if he had managed to repair the bridge. The dad said he had managed to do it - but not with money - with celery! The family had been saving celery in the fridge and the dad had offered it to a nearby farmer who exchanged it for materials to repair the bridge.
The kids learned a valuable lesson - even if you don’t have money, you can still do something to help.

Her mother smiled. “Maybe, but you must be very careful,” she said. 
Lily nodded, carefully opened the door and ran outside. She could see the goose waddling around in the grass. She slowly crept up to it and reached out her hand.
“Hello, goose!” she said softly.
But the goose seemed scared. It started flapping its wings and moved away from Lily. She tried again, but it wouldn't come near.
Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily could see the goose was getting wet. She knew what she had to do. Quickly, she grabbed a big, soft towel and ran outside again.
When she held the towel out to the goose, it stepped onto it and stayed there. Lily carefully carried the goose back into the house and dried him with the towel.
When it was dry again, the goose went back outside. Lily gave it one last hug, waved goodbye and watched it as it flew away.

Tom and Mia look at each other. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Tom. Sorry, Mia."
They hug and say, "We are friends. We love each other."

Tim and Lily are playing with their crayons and paper. They like to draw different things, like animals, cars, and flowers. Tim draws a big lion with a yellow crayon. Lily draws a pink car with a purple crayon.
"Look at my lion!" Tim says. "He is very strong and loud. He can scare anyone."
"Look at my car!" Lily says. "It is very fast and pretty. It can go anywhere."
They show each other their drawings and smile. They are proud of their work.
But then, Tim sees something on Lily's paper. It is a small mark with a green crayon. It looks like a bug.
"Hey, what is that?" Tim asks. He points at the mark.
"That is nothing," Lily says. She tries to hide the mark with her hand. "It is just a mistake."
"A mistake?" Tim says. He grabs Lily's paper and looks closer. "It is a bug! You drew a bug on your car!"
Lily feels angry and embarrassed. She did not mean to draw a bug. She was trying to draw a flower, but the green crayon slipped from her hand.
"It is not a bug!" Lily says. She tries to get her paper back. "It is a flower!"
Tim does not believe her. He thinks she is lying. He laughs at her.
"A flower? That is a silly flower. It has no petals, no stem, no leaves. It is just a dot. A green dot. A bug!"
Lily feels more angry and sad. She does not like Tim laughing at her. She wants to erase the mark. She looks around and sees an eraser on the table. It is a big, white eraser. It is flexible and soft. She has an idea.
She reaches for the eraser and pushes Tim away. She rubs the eraser on her paper, hard and fast. She wants to make the mark disappear.
"Stop it!" Tim says. He pushes Lily back. He wants to keep the paper. He thinks it is funny. "You can't erase a bug! It is still there!"
They push and pull, push and pull. They fight over the paper and the eraser. They do not hear their teacher coming.
"Tim! Lily! What are you doing?" their teacher says. She is not happy. She sees the paper and the eraser. She sees the crayons and the drawings. She sees the mark and the mess.
She takes the paper and the eraser from them. She looks at them with a stern face.
"You two need to calm down and apologize," she says. "You need to respect each other's work and feelings. You need to share and be nice."
Tim and Lily feel ashamed and sorry. They know they did wrong. They look at each other and say sorry.
"I'm sorry, Lily," Tim says. "I should not have laughed at your drawing. It is not a bug. It is a flower."
"I'm sorry, Tim," Lily says. "I should not have pushed you and erased your drawing. It is not a mistake. It is a lion."
They hug and make up. They give each other their paper and their crayon. They finish their drawings and add more details. They make the lion more fierce and the car more shiny. They make the flower more colorful and the bug more friendly.
They show their teacher their drawings and smile. They are proud of their work and their friendship.

Jack smiled and said yes. He threw in a few more pebbles and kept count. The frog bounced up and down and sang out each number. When Jack reached his highest score he delighted in the sound of the frog.
When Jack was done, the frog said "Well done, Jack! You have a very comfortable score." Jack was pleased and thanked the frog for playing with him. He said goodbye and went home with a big smile on his face.

"Do not touch me," the flower said.
Lisa was surprised, she had never heard a flower talk before.
"Why not?" Lisa asked.
The flower said, "if you pick me, I'll wilt and die. And I'm too pretty to die."
Lisa understood, she smiled and said, "I won't pick you, I'll lift you, that way you can get a better view and others can admire your beauty too”
The flower was pleased, it lifted itself and waved its petals in welcome, as Lisa followed it around the garden.
The moral of this story is to always show respect for the things around us. When we lift them, we help them to be better, instead of taking something away.

Once there was a little boy named Tom. Tom had a closet full of toys and clothes. His favorite toy was a brand-new truck.
One day, Tom was playing with his truck inside the closet. He was being very careful not to spoil anything inside. Suddenly, an elderly woman stuck her head inside the closet and saw Tom. 
"What are you doing in there?" She asked.
Tom was too scared to answer.
"This is my Grandma's closet, and you are spoiling it," the elderly woman said. 
Tom knew he had to leave the closet immediately. He ran out of the closet, leaving his truck behind. He was so scared he forgot to close the closet door. 
When Grandma came back, she saw the mess in the closet and knew it was not Tom's fault. She closed the closet door and gave Tom a big hug. Tom knew he was safe now.

Lila and Tom are playing in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They see a big hill with grass and flowers. They want to climb it and see what is on the other side.
"Come on, Tom, let's go!" Lila says. She grabs Tom's hand and they rush to the hill. They are fast and happy.
They reach the top of the hill and look around. They see a pond with ducks and frogs. They see a tree with a nest and eggs. They see a fence with a sign that says "Do not enter".
"What is behind the fence?" Tom asks. He is curious and brave.
"I don't know, let's find out!" Lila says. She is adventurous and bold.
They crawl under the fence and enter a new place. They see a lot of strange things. They see a pile of metal and wires. They see a box with buttons and lights. They see a tube with water and bubbles. They see a spike that is shiny and sharp.
"Wow, this is cool!" Lila says. She touches the spike and feels a pain. She cries out loud.
"Ouch, ouch, ouch! The spike hurt me!" Lila says. She holds her finger and bleeds.
"Are you okay, Lila?" Tom says. He is worried and scared.
"No, I'm not okay, Tom. The spike is bad. We need to go back!" Lila says. She is hurt and sad.
They run back to the fence and crawl under it. They see a man with a coat and glasses. He is angry and stern.
"Hey, you two, what are you doing here? This is a dangerous place. You are not allowed here. You could have been hurt badly. You are very naughty!" The man says. He shouts and points.
"We are sorry, sir. We were just playing. We didn't know. We won't come back. Please don't be mad." Tom says. He is sorry and polite.
Lila says nothing. She is still crying and bleeding. She needs a band-aid and a hug.
They leave the fence and the man. They go back to the hill and the park. They find their mom and dad. They tell them what happened. They get a band-aid and a hug. They learn a lesson.
They never go near the fence and the spike again. They play with other things that are safe and fun. They are flexible and smart. They are still fast and happy.

Once upon a time there was a small mole called Tom. Tom liked to complain about everything. One day, Tom was complaining about how terrible the weather was. He shouted, "It's too warm! This weather is terrible!" 
Suddenly, a wise old frog appeared from a nearby pond and said, "You know, it doesn't help to complain. You can't change the weather by complaining."
Tom thought about this for a moment and then said, "You're right! I shouldn't complain about the weather." 
The frog smiled and said, "Why don't you find something else to do, instead of complaining? That would make you feel much better." 
Tom thanked the frog for the advice and decided that he wouldn't complain anymore. Instead, he decided to go and explore his burrow and look for something interesting to do. Tom had a great time exploring, and he even found some delicious worms to snack on. From then on, Tom was much happier, and he never complained again.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She made pictures of flowers, animals, and her family. She wanted to be a painter when she grew up. She thought painters had fun and made beautiful things.
One day, her mom took her to a museum. There were many paintings on the walls. Lily was excited to see them. She hoped to learn from the painters and get new ideas.
But when she looked at the paintings, she felt confused. They were not like her pictures. They had strange shapes and colors. Some of them looked messy and ugly. Lily did not understand them. She thought they were boring.
"Mom, why are these paintings so boring?" she asked. "They don't look like anything. I don't like them."
Her mom smiled and knelt down to her level. "Lily, these paintings are not boring. They are different. They are called abstract. The painters wanted to show their feelings and thoughts, not just what they saw. They used shapes and colors to express themselves. They wanted to make people think and feel something new."
Lily frowned. She did not think that was a good way to paint. She liked to draw what she saw and what she liked. She did not want to make people think and feel something new. She wanted to make them happy and smile.
"Mom, I don't want to be an abstract painter. I want to be a real painter. I want to make pretty pictures that look like something. Can we go home and draw with my crayons?"
Her mom hugged her and said, "Of course, sweetie. You can be any kind of painter you want. You can draw with your crayons or with anything else. You can make your own style and your own rules. As long as you enjoy it and have fun, that's what matters."
Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you."
They left the museum and went home. Lily took out her crayons and made a new picture. She drew her mom and herself holding hands. She wrote, "I love you, mom" on the bottom. She gave it to her mom and said, "This is for you, mom. This is my painting. Do you like it?"
Her mom looked at it and said, "I love it, Lily. It's beautiful. It's the best painting I've ever seen. You are a wonderful painter. I'm so proud of you."
They hugged and kissed. Lily was happy. She did not care about the boring paintings in the museum. She had her own paintings and her mom. That's all she needed.

"Hi, Spot!" Tim says. He gives the dog his baseball bat. Spot takes it in his mouth and runs away.
"Hey, that's mine!" Tim says. He chases the dog.
"Come back, Spot!" the man says. He follows them.
Ben watches them go. He is still scared of the dog. He sits on the grass and holds his baseball glove. He wishes Tim would come back and play with him.

They all got up and carried the blocks back to their room. They put them away in their box, and then they went to the kitchen. Their mom had made them a yummy dinner, and they ate it together. Lily was so happy and excited. She hugged her teddy bear and said, "Thank you, God. I love you." Then she closed her eyes and fell asleep.
The next morning, Lily woke up early. She jumped out of her bed and ran to the window. She looked up at the sky and gasped. There, shining brightly, was a beautiful star. It was big and bright and sparkly. It looked like a diamond.
Lily clapped her hands and shouted, "Wow! God, you are amazing! You gave me my wish! Thank you, thank you, thank you!" She felt a warm feeling in her heart. She knew God loved her and heard her prayers.
She ran to her parents' room and knocked on the door. She said, "Mommy, Daddy, come and see! God gave me a beautiful star!" She pulled them to the window and pointed at the sky. They smiled and hugged her. They said, "Lily, you are a lucky girl. God is good. He gave you a beautiful star and a beautiful heart." They kissed her and said, "We love you, Lily. And so does God."

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had a lock on it.
"Let's open it!" Lily said. "Maybe there are more toys inside."
"How?" Ben asked. "We need a key."
Lily looked around. She saw a shiny thing on the wall. It looked like a key. She took it and ran to the box.
"Look, I found it!" she said. "Let's unlock the box!"
She put the key in the lock and turned it. The box opened. Inside, there was a penguin. It was black and white and soft. It looked cool.
"Wow, a penguin!" Ben said. "Can we play with it?"
"Sure!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Penguins need cold and water. They don't like hot and dry."
They took the penguin out of the box and put it on the floor. They petted it and hugged it. The penguin made a noise. It sounded sad.
"Maybe it's thirsty," Lily said. "Let's give it some water."
They went to the kitchen and filled a bowl with water. They brought it back to the penguin. The penguin drank some water. It looked happier.
"See, it likes water," Lily said. "Let's give it some ice too. Ice is cool and fun."
They went to the freezer and took out some ice cubes. They put them on the floor next to the penguin. The penguin played with the ice. It looked even happier.
"See, it likes ice too," Ben said. "Let's give it some fish. Fish are yummy and good for penguins."
They went to the fridge and took out some fish. They put them on the floor next to the penguin. The penguin ate some fish. It looked very happy.
"See, it likes fish too," Lily said. "We are good friends with the penguin. It loves us."
They smiled and cuddled with the penguin. They felt warm and cozy.
But they did not see the door open. They did not hear the footsteps. They did not notice the angry face.
It was Dad. He came home from work. He saw the mess in the garage. He saw the open box. He saw the penguin. He saw the water, the ice, and the fish. He was very mad.
"Who did this?" he yelled. "Who took my penguin?"
Lily and Ben were scared. They looked at Dad. They did not know what to say.
Dad grabbed the penguin and put it back in the box. He locked it with the key. He took the key and put it in his pocket.
"You are in big trouble," he said. "This is not a toy. This is a rare and expensive penguin. I bought it for a special project. You ruined it. You made it sick. You wasted my food. You are bad kids."
He glared at them and left. He slammed the door.
Lily and Ben cried. They felt sorry and sad. They missed the penguin. They wished they could say sorry. They wished they could play with it again. They wished they had a different dad.

One day, a little bird flew down to the village market. She flew over the stalls and saw all the nice things the villagers were selling. She nodded her head in approval. 
Suddenly, a cat appeared from behind a fruit stall. He was big, and his eyes glinted in the sun. He didn't seem harmless.
The little bird was frightened, but she stayed still. "Oh, don't worry," said the cat. "I won't hurt you. Please don't be scared." She nodded again, trying to believe the cat.
The cat took her up to the rooftop of the nearest house. But as soon as they got there, he grabbed the little bird in his mouth and swallowed her in one gulp. The little bird was so shocked, she couldn't even make a sound. 
The cat sat on the roof, licking his lips. The little bird was gone, but the market hummed happily below, just like always.

"Maybe it is a fake cross," Tom said. "Maybe someone put it here for fun."
He pushed the cross with his hand. It did not move.
"See? It is real. It is stuck in the ground," Lily said.
She pushed the cross too. It still did not move.
They pushed harder and harder. They wanted to make the cross fall.
But the cross was too strong. It did not fall.
They heard a voice behind them.
"Hey, what are you doing?" the voice said.
They turned around and saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He looked angry.
"This is my cross. I made it for my garden. It is not fake. It is not for playing. Stop pushing it!" the man said.
Lily and Tom felt scared. They did not know the man. They did not know he owned the cross.
They said sorry to the man. They ran away from the cross. They did not want to push it anymore.
They went back to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She was reading a book.
"Mom, we saw a cross in the park. It was real. A man made it for his garden. He was mad at us. We pushed it," Lily said.
"Really? That was not nice of you. You should not push things that are not yours. You should respect other people's things. You should say sorry if you make a mistake," mom said.
"We did say sorry, mom. We were just curious. We thought it was fake," Tom said.
Mom hugged them and kissed them.
"I know, my loves. You are still learning. But you have to be careful. Some things are not for playing. Some things are special to someone. You have to ask before you touch them. You have to be polite and kind," mom said.
Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They felt sorry for the man and his cross.
They said they would not push it again.
They asked mom if they could play with their ball instead.
Mom smiled and said yes.
They took their ball and went to play.
They had fun with their ball.

The active group said, "You won't be lazy anymore if you come with us!"
The sleepy group said, "We don't want to."
The active group said, "You'll have fun and feel more alive!"

Sam is not happy. He wants a zoom car too. He says, "No, Tom, your car is not faster than my cars. My cars are faster and better. Let me try your zoom car!"

Sam is angry. He tries to grab the zoom car from Tom. Tom pulls it back. They start to fight over the zoom car. They shout and push each other.

Tom and Sam stop fighting. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Tom. Sorry, Sam."

Tom and Sam smile. They like peanut butter cookies. They say, "Yes, Mom, we like peanut butter cookies!"
Mom says, "Good. Then come to the kitchen and have some cookies. And bring your cars too. You can play with them on the table. But be careful. Don't let them zoom off the table!"
Tom and Sam say, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom!"

Lily was sad. Her doll had a big hole in her dress. She loved her doll very much. She wanted her doll to look normal again.
She went to her mom and showed her the hole. "Mom, can you fix my doll?" she asked.
Mom smiled and hugged Lily. "Of course, sweetie. Let me see what I can do." She took the doll and a needle and some thread. She found a piece of cloth that matched the dress. She sewed the cloth over the hole. She made small stitches and tied a knot.
She gave the doll back to Lily. "There you go. Your doll is fixed. She looks normal and pretty again."
Lily was happy. She hugged her doll and her mom. "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you and my doll." She said.
Mom kissed Lily and her doll. "You're welcome, honey. I love you too. Now, why don't you go and play with your doll and your friends?" She said.
Lily nodded and ran to her room. She found her other dolls and toys. She made a tea party for them. She invited her mom to join them. They had a lot of fun. Lily was not sad anymore. She was glad that her mom could fix her doll.

"Can we go on it?" Tim asks a big person who works in the park.
"Yes, you can. But be careful. It can go very fast. Hold on tight to the bars. And don't get dizzy." The big person says.
Tim and Mia get on the round thing. They sit on the seats and hold on to the bars. The big person pushes a button. The round thing starts to spin.
"Wow, this is fun!" Tim says. He likes the speed. He feels the wind in his hair. He laughs.
"I don't like it!" Mia says. She does not like the speed. She feels sick in her tummy. She cries.
"Can we stop?" Mia asks the big person.
"Okay, okay. I will stop it." The big person says. He pushes another button. The round thing slows down and stops.
Tim and Mia get off the round thing. Mia runs to a bench. She sits down and breathes. Tim follows her.
"Are you okay, Mia?" Tim asks.
"I'm okay. I just don't like the round thing. It makes me feel bad." Mia says.
"I'm sorry, Mia. I didn't know you don't like the round thing. I like it. It makes me feel good." Tim says.
"Why do you like it?" Mia asks.
"I don't know. I just do. I like to go fast. It is fun." Tim says.
He shrugs. He does not know how to explain.
Mia nods. She does not understand. She likes to go slow. It is safe.
They are different. But they are still friends. They hug.
"Let's go play something else." Tim says.
"Okay. Let's go." Mia says.
They hold hands and walk to the slide. They play together. They are happy.

Lily and Ben said, "Sorry, Mom. We were just joking. We won't play with the iron again."
Mom said, "I know, my loves. You are good and gentle children. But jokes can sometimes be risky. Next time, play with your toys or books or crayons. They are safe and fun."
Lily and Ben said, "Okay, Mom. We love you."
Mom said, "I love you too." She kissed them and put the iron away. She gave them their toys and books and crayons. They played with them and made up new stories and jokes. They were happy and careful.

Ben and Lily looked at Mom, and then at the dishwasher. They thought about it, and nodded. They decided to try. They took the dishes, and put them in the dishwasher. They closed the door, and pushed the button. They heard the water and the soap and the noise. They smiled and said, "We did it, Mom. We put the dishes in the dishwasher."

Lily and Ben went to the farm with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. But Lily's favorite animal was the goat. She wanted to pet the goat and feed it some grass.
"Can I go to the goat, Mom?" Lily asked.
"Sure, honey, but be careful. The goat might be shy or hungry," Mom said.
Lily ran to the fence where the goat was. She held out some grass in her hand and said, "Hello, goat. Do you want some grass?"
The goat looked at Lily with its big eyes and ears. It was excited to see the grass. It came closer to the fence and leaned its head over. It sniffed the grass and then nibbled it from Lily's hand. Lily giggled and stroked the goat's soft fur.
"Good goat, good goat," she said.
Ben watched Lily and the goat. He wanted to pet the goat too. He walked to the fence and reached out his hand. But the goat was full of grass and not interested in Ben. It turned away and walked to the other side of the pen.
"Hey, goat, come back!" Ben said.
But the goat did not come back. Ben felt sad and angry. He kicked the fence and shouted, "Bad goat, bad goat!"
The goat heard Ben and did not like his noise. It came back to the fence and leaned its head over again. But this time, it did not want grass. It wanted to teach Ben a lesson. It opened its mouth and bit Ben's finger.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried.
Mom and Dad heard Ben and ran to him. They saw the goat and the bite mark on Ben's finger. They hugged Ben and said, "Are you okay, Ben?"
Ben nodded, but he was still in pain and scared. He did not like the goat anymore.
Lily saw what happened and felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The goat was nice to me, but not to you. Maybe it was just full or scared. Do you want to pet another animal?"
Ben looked at Lily and smiled. He said, "Yes, Lily. Thank you. Let's go to the cows. They are big and gentle."
Lily and Ben held hands and went to the cows. They petted the cows and fed them some hay. They forgot about the goat and had fun at the farm. Mom and Dad watched them and smiled. They were happy that Lily and Ben were friends again.

Max walks around the garden. He looks under the flowers, behind the rocks, and in the birdhouse. He does not see Lily. He gets tired and bored. He sits on the grass and yawns. He does not want to play anymore.
Lily is still hiding behind the tree. She does not hear Max. She wonders where he is. She peeks out from the tree and sees him sitting on the grass. She thinks he is still looking for her. She giggles and stays behind the tree. She does not know he is lazy.
She waits and waits and waits. She gets bored too. She wants to play something else. She also gets hungry and thirsty. She needs oxygen and water and food. She decides to come out from the tree and tell Max. She runs to him and says, "Max, I'm here! I was hiding behind the tree. You did not find me. You are lazy. Let's play something else. I'm hungry and thirsty. I need oxygen and water and food."
Max looks at her and says, "Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. I did not see you. I was tired and bored. I did not want to play anymore. I'm hungry and thirsty too. I need oxygen and water and food too. Let's go inside and have a snack. Maybe we can play something else later."
Lily and Max go inside and have a snack. They drink water and eat cookies and fruit. They breathe oxygen and feel better. They are not bored anymore. They are happy. They hug each other and say, "We are friends. We like to play together. Hide and seek is fun, but not too long."

Ben and Mia like to play in the garden. They look for bugs and flowers and rocks. One day, they see something new. It is a lizard. The lizard is red and has a long tail. It runs fast on the grass.
"Wow, look at that!" Ben says. "It is a red lizard. I want to catch it."
"Me too!" Mia says. "Let's be quiet and sneak up on it."
They kneel on the ground and crawl slowly. They try not to scare the lizard. But the lizard sees them and runs away. It hides under a big leaf.
"Where did it go?" Ben asks. He lifts the leaf and peeks under it.
"Shh, there it is!" Mia whispers. She reaches out her hand and touches the lizard gently. The lizard feels smooth and warm. It does not bite or scratch.
"Hello, little lizard," Mia says. "You are so pretty. Can we be your friends?"
The lizard looks at Mia and Ben with its small eyes. It does not run away. It seems to like them. It flicks its tongue and makes a soft sound.
"Maybe it is saying hello back," Ben says. He smiles and strokes the lizard's head. "Do you think we can keep it as a pet?"
"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe it has a family or a home. Maybe it likes to be free."
They think for a moment. They like the lizard, but they also want it to be happy.
"Maybe we can visit it sometimes," Ben says. "But we should let it go now. It might miss its friends."
"OK," Mia says. "Bye, red lizard. Thank you for playing with us."
They put the lizard back on the grass and watch it run away. They wave and say goodbye. They feel happy and sad at the same time.
They go back to their house and tell their mom about the red lizard. She hugs them and says they are very kind and gentle. She gives them some cookies and milk. They eat and drink and talk about their new friend. They hope to see it again.

Mia was a chubby girl who liked to eat a lot of cake. She did not like to share her cake with anyone, not even her friends. One day, she brought a big slice of cake to school for snack time. She put it on her desk and went to play with her toys.
Lily was a thin girl who liked to eat healthy food. She saw Mia's cake and thought it looked yummy. She did not have any snack of her own, because her mom forgot to pack it. She felt hungry and sad. She went to Mia's desk and asked, "Can I have some of your cake, please?"
Mia came back and saw Lily near her cake. She got angry and said, "No, you can't! This is my cake, and I don't want to share it with you. Go away!"
Lily felt hurt and said, "But I'm hungry, and you have so much cake. You should be nice and share with your friends. Sharing is caring, you know."
Mia did not care. She said, "I don't care. This is my cake, and I like it. You can't have any of it. It's mine, mine, mine!"
Lily tried to grab a piece of cake, but Mia resisted. She pushed Lily away and said, "Stop it! Leave me alone!"
Lily cried and ran to the teacher. She told her what happened. The teacher was not happy with Mia. She said, "Mia, that was very rude and selfish of you. You should apologize to Lily and share your cake with her. Or else, you will have to go to the time-out corner."
Mia did not want to go to the time-out corner. She did not want to apologize either. But she did not want to lose her cake. She thought for a moment and said, "Fine. I'm sorry, Lily. You can have a little bit of my cake. But only a little bit, okay?"
Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mia. That's very kind of you. Can we be friends?"
Mia nodded and said, "Okay. We can be friends. But only if you don't touch my cake again."
Lily agreed and said, "Okay. I won't touch your cake again. But can I have a bite of yours?"
Mia sighed and said, "Okay. Just one bite. But that's it."
Lily took a bite of Mia's cake and said, "Mmm, this is good. Do you want to try some of my carrot?"
Mia looked at the carrot and said, "No, thank you. I don't like carrots. They are yucky."
Lily shrugged and said, "Suit yourself. I like carrots. They are crunchy and healthy."
Mia and Lily ate their snacks and talked about their toys. They learned to share and be nice to each other. They became friends and played together. The teacher was proud of them and gave them both a sticker. They were happy and said, "Yay!"

"Sorry, Mom. I didn't mean to shut it so hard," Ben said.
"It's okay, Ben. I know you were trying to help. Thank you for the cheese," Mom said.

"Come on, kids. Pasta with sauce is ready. It's hot and yummy," Mom said.
Lily and Ben ran to the table. They smelled the pasta and sauce. They saw the cheese on top. They were very happy.
"Thank you, Mom. This looks delicious," Lily said.
"Yes, thank you, Mom. You are the best," Ben said.

But Sam is jealous. He does not have a bucket or a shovel. He wants to play with Tom and Anna. He asks them, "Can I play with you?"
Tom and Anna say, "Yes, you can play with us. We have enough mud for everyone. You can use our bucket and shovel."
Sam is happy. He says, "Thank you, Tom and Anna. You are very nice."
But Sam is not nice. He does not share. He takes the bucket and the shovel and runs away. He says, "Ha ha, they are mine now. I have the best toys."
Tom and Anna are sad. They say, "Sam is mean. He took our bucket and shovel. He did not ask. He did not say sorry. He is not our friend."
Sam runs to the other side of the park. He tries to make mud pies. But he is not happy. He feels lonely. He sees Tom and Anna playing with other children. They have sticks and stones and leaves. They make a castle and a bridge and a boat. They have fun.
Sam wants to join them. He says, "Can I play with you?"
Tom and Anna say, "No, you cannot play with us. You are not nice. You took our bucket and shovel. You did not ask. You did not say sorry. You are not our friend."
Sam is sad. He says, "I am sorry, Tom and Anna. I was wrong. I was jealous. I did not share. I want to be your friend."
Tom and Anna say, "You can be our friend, but you have to give back our bucket and shovel. You have to say sorry. You have to share."
Sam says, "I will give back your bucket and shovel. I will say sorry. I will share."
He carries the bucket and the shovel to Tom and Anna. He says, "I am sorry, Tom and Anna. Here are your bucket and shovel. Can I play with you?"
Tom and Anna say, "Yes, you can play with us. We forgive you. We are happy."
They all play together. They make mud pies and castles and bridges and boats. They share and help and laugh. They are friends.
The moral of the story is: Do not be jealous. Do not take what is not yours. Do not be mean. Be nice. Share and say sorry. Be a good friend.

Tom and Mia were playing near the pond. They liked to watch the fish and the frogs. Sometimes they saw a big bird with a long neck and a funny beak. They called it a giraffe-bird.
One day, they saw something else in the water. It was long and green and had many teeth. It was an alligator. Tom and Mia were scared. They wanted to run away, but the alligator was blocking their path.
"Help! Help!" they shouted. "There is an alligator!"
A man heard their cries and came running. He had a stick and a rope. He was brave. He threw the rope around the alligator's mouth and tied it. Then he hit the alligator with the stick until it stopped moving.
"Are you okay, kids?" he asked. "That was a dangerous animal. You should not play near the pond."
"Thank you, mister," Tom and Mia said. "You saved us. You are very brave."
The man smiled. "You are welcome. I am a ranger. I take care of the animals and the plants. I will take this alligator to a safe place. It does not belong here. It came from far away."
"How did it get here?" Tom asked.
"Maybe it escaped from a zoo or a farm. Or maybe someone brought it here and left it. That is very bad. Alligators need a lot of space and food. They can hurt people and other animals."
"Can we see it?" Mia asked.
"Sure, but be careful. It is still alive. It can bite and scratch. I will show you how I managed to catch it. It was not easy. You have to be quick and smart and brave."
Tom and Mia followed the man to his truck. They saw the alligator in a big cage. They were curious and amazed. They learned a lot about alligators from the man. They thanked him again and said goodbye.
They decided to play somewhere else. They did not want to meet another alligator. They were glad they had a brave ranger to protect them.

Lily loved flowers. She liked to smell them, touch them, and look at their colors. She had a garden with many flowers. She watered them every day and sang to them.
One day, she saw a new flower in her garden. It was big and red and shiny. It looked like a mask. Lily was curious. She wanted to see it closer. She walked to the flower and bent down.
"Hello, little girl," the flower said. "Do you like me?"
Lily was surprised. She had never heard a flower talk before. She was a little scared, but also excited.
"Yes, you are very pretty," she said. "But how can you talk?"
"I am a special flower," the flower said. "I can talk and think and feel. I came from a faraway land. I bloomed here to make friends."
Lily smiled. She liked to make friends. She asked the flower many questions. She learned that the flower's name was Ruby, and that she liked the sun and the rain and the wind.
They talked for a long time. They became friends. Lily was very happy.
But then, Lily's mom called her. She said it was time to go inside and have lunch. Lily did not want to leave Ruby. She wanted to stay with her.
"Can I come back later?" she asked Ruby.
"Of course," Ruby said. "I will be here. But you have to promise me something."
"What is it?" Lily asked.
"You have to promise me that you will not tell anyone about me," Ruby said. "I am a secret flower. If people find out about me, they might take me away or hurt me. I only trust you."
Lily nodded. She understood. She did not want Ruby to be sad or scared. She wanted Ruby to be cheerful.
"I promise," she said. "You are my secret friend. I will not tell anyone."
She hugged Ruby and said goodbye. She ran to her mom and had lunch. She did not say anything about Ruby. She kept her promise.
She could not wait to see Ruby again. She hoped Ruby would be happy too.

"Look, mom, a big bird!" Ben said, pointing to a colorful parrot. "It can talk!"
"Yes, it can, Ben. It is a parrot. Do you want to say hello?" mom asked.
"Hello, parrot!" Ben said.
"Hello, hello!" the parrot said back, making Ben laugh.
Anna saw a sign that said "Reptile House". She wanted to see the snakes and lizards. She pulled mom's hand and said, "Can we go there, mom? Please?"
"Sure, Anna. Let's go see the reptiles. But remember, we have to be calm and quiet. They don't like loud noises," mom said.
They entered the reptile house and saw many glass cages with different reptiles. Anna saw a big snake that was coiled around a branch. It had yellow and black stripes. She read the sign that said "Python".
"Wow, mom, look at that snake! It is so long and strong!" Anna said.
"Yes, it is, Anna. It is a python. It can squeeze its prey with its body," mom said.
"Does it eat people?" Anna asked, feeling a little scared.
"No, Anna, it doesn't. It eats small animals, like rats and birds. And it is behind the glass, so it can't hurt us. See, it is very calm. It is just resting," mom said.
Anna felt better and looked at the snake with curiosity. She saw that it had a forked tongue that it flicked in and out. She learned that it used its tongue to smell the air.
"Mom, can I display my tongue like the snake?" Anna asked.
"Sure, Anna, you can. But only here, not at home or at school, okay?" mom said.
"Okay, mom," Anna said, and stuck out her tongue and flicked it like the snake. Ben saw her and did the same. They both giggled and pretended to be snakes.
Mom smiled and took a picture of them. She was happy that they had fun at the zoo.

The caterpillar said, "Yes, bird! I would like to come play with you." So, the bird and the caterpillar played together. They played in the grass and under the big tree. They had lots of fun. The caterpillar liked the bird very much.
After they played, the bird said, "Caterpillar, I have to go now. I will come back to play with you again." The caterpillar said, "Okay, bird. I will wait for you to come back." And so, the bird flew away, and the caterpillar waited for its new friend to come back and play again.

One day, a big gorilla went for a walk in the forest. He was very tired, but he wanted to see his friend, the little bird. With each step, the gorilla felt more tired, but he kept going.
As he walked, he saw the little bird on a tree. "Hello, little bird," said the tired gorilla. "I am so tired, but I wanted to see you." The little bird smiled and said, "Thank you, gorilla. Let's sit and rest together."
While they sat and talked, a big wind came and blew the little bird far away. The gorilla was sad, but he knew he had to help his friend. He took a big step and jumped high to catch the little bird. The wind stopped, and the gorilla saved his friend.
The little bird thanked the gorilla, and they both felt happy. The tired gorilla learned that even when you are tired, you can still help your friends. And that is what makes a true friend.

Once upon a time, there were two children, Alex and Sam. They both were hairy, and were going fishing together. 
Alex carried a long wooden kayak to the beach. As they arrived, the children pulled the kayak into the ocean.
Alex helped Sam get into the kayak. Sam brightly shouted “Yay! Can I pull the oars?”
“Yes, you can,” Alex said.
The children began to row. Sam was squealing with delight, pulling the oars and splashing. They both laughed as they paddled across the ocean.
They kept on rowing until they found a nice place to fish.
“Let’s stop here,” Alex said.
Sam happily agreed and both children eagerly prepared for fishing. Their adventure into the sea had only just begun.

One time, the ball went over the fence and into the road. Lily and Tom ran to the fence and saw a big car coming. They were scared and wanted their ball back. They did not see the sign that said "Stop".
"Tom, we have to get the ball!" Lily said.
"No, Lily, it is too dangerous!" Tom said.
But Lily did not listen. She climbed over the fence and ran to the road. She did not look left or right. She only saw the ball.
The man in the car saw Lily and tried to stop. He pushed the brake hard and honked the horn loud. But it was too late. The car was too fast and Lily was too small. The car hit Lily and made a loud noise.
Tom saw what happened and started to cry. He panicked and did not know what to do. He wanted to help Lily but he was afraid of the car and the road. He shouted for help but no one heard him.
The man in the car got out and saw Lily on the ground. He was very sad and sorry. He called for help too but it was too late. Lily was not moving or breathing. She was gone.
The end.

Lily liked to play in the park with her friends. She liked to swing, slide and run. But her favorite thing was to fish in the pond. She had a red pole that her dad gave her. She felt very happy when she caught a fish.
One day, she went to the pond with her pole and some bread. She saw a boy sitting on a bench. He had a blue pole and a bucket. He looked sad. Lily wanted to be nice, so she walked to him and said hello.
"Hello," the boy said. "What are you doing?"
"I'm fishing," Lily said. "Do you want to fish with me?"
The boy shook his head. "No, thank you. I don't like fishing."
Lily was surprised. "Why not? Fishing is fun. You have a pole and a bucket. You can catch fish and put them in the bucket."
The boy sighed. "I have a pole and a bucket, but I can't catch any fish. I've been here all morning and nothing bites. My pole is broken. It's not attractive to the fish."
Lily felt sorry for the boy. She had an idea. She smiled and said, "Maybe you need some bread. Bread is good for the fish. They like to eat it. I have some bread. Do you want some?"
The boy looked at Lily. He saw her red pole and her bread. He saw her friendly face. He felt a little hopeful. He nodded and said, "Yes, please. Can I have some bread?"
Lily was happy. She gave the boy some bread and showed him how to put it on the hook. She said, "Now, throw your pole in the water and wait. You will catch a fish soon. I know it."
The boy did what Lily said. He threw his pole in the water and waited. He watched the bread float on the surface. He hoped a fish would come. He hoped Lily was right.
After a few minutes, he felt a tug on his pole. He gasped and pulled. He saw a silver fish on his hook. He was amazed. He had caught a fish. He smiled and said, "Look, Lily, I caught a fish. You were right. The bread worked. Thank you."
Lily clapped and cheered. She was proud of the boy. She said, "You're welcome. You did a good job. You have a good pole. It is attractive to the fish. You just needed some bread."
The boy took the fish off the hook and put it in his bucket. He looked at Lily and said, "Do you want to be my friend?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Do you want to be my friend?"
The boy nodded and said, "Yes, I do. What is your name?"
Lily said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"
The boy said, "My name is Ben. Nice to meet you, Lily."
Lily said, "Nice to meet you, Ben. Do you want to fish some more?"
Ben said, "Yes, I do. Let's fish some more."
Lily and Ben fished some more. They caught more fish and put them in their buckets. They talked and laughed. They had fun. They became friends. They liked to fish in the pond. They liked their poles and their bread. They liked each other.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in the park. One day, they brought a sandwich each for lunch. They put their sandwiches in a bag and left it under a tree.
They saw some ducks in the pond. They wanted to feed them. They took some bread from their bag and threw it to the ducks. The ducks came closer and quacked.
"Look, Ben, the ducks are happy!" Sam said.
"Yes, they are, Sam. They are hungry, like us. Let's eat our sandwiches now," Ben said.
They went back to the tree. But they could not find their bag. They looked around and saw a big dog. The dog had their bag in its mouth. It was chewing their sandwiches.
"Hey, that's our lunch! Give it back!" Ben shouted.
He ran towards the dog. The dog growled and ran away. Ben chased the dog. Sam followed him.
They ran across the park. They ran across the street. They did not look for cars. A car was coming fast. It honked its horn.
"Ben, Sam, watch out!" a voice yelled.
But it was too late. The car hit them. They fell to the ground. They did not get up. The dog dropped the bag and ran away. The sandwiches were all gone.
The voice was their mom. She had come to pick them up. She saw what happened. She cried and cried. She called for help. But no one could help them. Ben and Sam were gone.
The moral of the story is: Do not chase after things that are not yours. Be careful when you cross the street. Listen to your mom.

One day, a big bird flew over the land. He saw many things: trees, flowers, animals, and people. He liked the land. He wanted to live there.
He saw a small nest on a tall tree. He flew down and said to the nest, "Hello, nest. You are nice and cozy. Can I stay with you?"
The nest said, "No, bird. You are too big and ugly. You will break me and make a mess. Go away."
The bird was sad and angry. He said, "Fine, nest. You are mean and rude. I will show you. I will spread my wings and cover the land. Then you will have no sun, no rain, no air. You will be sorry."
The bird did what he said. He spread his wings and covered the land. The land became dark and cold. The trees, flowers, animals, and people were scared and unhappy. They could not see, grow, or play.
The nest saw what the bird did. He felt sorry and ashamed. He said to the bird, "Please, bird. Stop. You are hurting the land and everyone on it. You are not ugly. You are strong and beautiful. You can find another nest that is big and cozy. Please, let the land have sun, rain, and air again."
The bird heard the nest. He felt sorry and ashamed too. He said to the nest, "You are right, nest. I was wrong. I am sorry. I will not hurt the land and everyone on it. I will lift my wings and let the land have sun, rain, and air again. I will find another nest that is big and cozy. Thank you, nest, for being kind and wise."
The bird did what he said. He lifted his wings and let the land have sun, rain, and air again. The land became bright and warm. The trees, flowers, animals, and people were happy and grateful. They could see, grow, and play again.
The bird flew away and found another nest that was big and cozy. He lived there happily. He never spread his wings and covered the land again. He learned to be nice and respectful. The end.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play soccer in the park. They have a ball and two goals. They take turns to kick the ball and try to score.
One day, they see a big man in a blue shirt. He is holding a whistle and a flag. He walks to the middle of the pitch. He is a referee. He is going to watch the game and make sure the rules are followed.
"Hello, boys," he says. "Do you want me to be your referee?"
"Yes, please," Ben and Sam say. They are excited. They think it will be fun to have a real referee.
"OK, then," the referee says. "Let's start the game. I will blow my whistle when the ball goes out or when there is a foul. And I will wave my flag when there is a goal. Are you ready?"
"Yes, we are," Ben and Sam say. They run to their goals and wait for the whistle.
The referee blows his whistle and throws the ball in the air. Ben and Sam run to get the ball. They kick it and pass it and try to score. The referee watches them and blows his whistle and waves his flag when he needs to. He is very serious. He does not smile or laugh.
Ben and Sam have a lot of fun. They score many goals. Sometimes they cheer and sometimes they groan. They do not mind when the referee says they did something wrong. They say sorry and try again.
The game ends when the sun goes down. The referee blows his whistle and waves his flag one last time. He counts the goals and tells Ben and Sam the score.
"Well done, boys," he says. "You played very well. You both scored six goals. It is a draw. You are both winners."
"Thank you, referee," Ben and Sam say. They are happy. They shake hands with the referee and with each other. They pick up their ball and their goals and say goodbye.
"See you next time," the referee says. He waves to them and walks away.
Ben and Sam wave back and run to their homes. They can't wait to play soccer again.

"Look, it's Santa!" Lily said. "Let's go and say hello."
Ben was not sure. He thought the man looked funny. He did not have any reindeer or a sleigh. He did not look happy.
"Maybe he is not Santa," Ben said. "Maybe he is just a man in a costume."
Lily did not listen. She ran to the man and smiled.
"Hello, Santa," she said. "Are you here to give us presents?"
The man looked at Lily and frowned. He did not want to talk to her. He was not Santa. He was a magician. He was waiting for his show to start. He had a lot of tricks in his sack.
"Go away, kid," he said. "I'm busy. I'm not Santa. I'm a magic man."
Lily was sad. She did not like the man. She thought he was mean. She wanted him to be Santa.
"No, you are Santa," she said. "You have a beard and a red coat and a sack. You are Santa and you have to give us presents."
She pulled on his sack and tried to open it. The man was angry. He did not want her to touch his sack. He had a lot of secrets in it.
"Stop it, kid," he said. "Let go of my sack. You are ruining my magic."
Lily did not stop. She insisted. She wanted to see what was in the sack. She wanted to find a present for her and Ben.
"Please, Santa, please," she said. "Give us a present. We have been good. We have been very good."
The man had enough. He did not like Lily. He did not like kids. He did not like anyone. He wanted to be alone. He wanted to do his magic.
He reached into his sack and pulled out a wand. He pointed it at Lily and said a word.
"Zap!"
Lily felt a tickle on her nose. She sneezed. She looked at her hands. They were covered in fur. She looked at Ben. He was laughing. He pointed at her.
"Lily, you are a cat!" he said. "You are a funny cat. You have whiskers and a tail."
Lily was shocked. She did not want to be a cat. She wanted to be a girl. She wanted to be herself. She looked at the man. He was smiling. He had a wicked smile.
"That's what you get, kid," he said. "That's what you get for bothering me. That's my magic. That's my present for you."
He put his wand back in his sack and walked away. He left Lily and Ben in the park. He left Lily as a cat.
Lily was scared. She did not know what to do. She did not know how to change back. She did not like being a cat. She wanted to be a girl. She wanted to be Lily.
She ran to Ben and meowed. She hoped he would help her. She hoped he would find a way to make her a girl again.
Ben was sorry. He did not mean to laugh. He did not like the man. He did not like his magic. He did not like what he did to Lily.
He hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. Don't worry, cat. I will help you. I will find a way to make you a girl again. I will find a way to break the magic. I will find a way to make you Lily again."

Lily's mom said, "Sure, why not. Let me get another cup of juice."
Lily said, "Yay, thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever."

Tom and Sam were playing with their cars in the yard. They liked to make loud noises and crash their cars into each other. They had a lot of fun.
But then they saw a big, ugly bug on the grass. It had many legs and eyes and a long handle on its back. It looked scary and mean.
"Look, a bug!" Tom said. "Let's destroy it!"
"No, don't do that!" Sam said. "It's not nice to hurt bugs. They are living things too."
But Tom did not listen. He took his car and drove it fast towards the bug. He wanted to smash it with his car.
But the bug was not stupid. It saw the car coming and moved away. It used its handle to flip the car over and make it stop. Then it crawled on top of the car and bit it with its mouth.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The bug destroyed my car! It broke it!"
Sam ran to help Tom. He picked up the car and saw the bite marks. He felt sorry for Tom, but he also felt sorry for the bug.
"See, Tom, this is what happens when you try to destroy bugs. They can destroy back. Maybe next time you should leave them alone. They are not toys, they are friends."
Tom nodded. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to the bug and to Sam. He hugged his car and hoped it would be okay.
They decided to play something else. They looked for flowers and butterflies and bees. They did not destroy anything. They had a lot of fun.

Clara looked up, and saw it was a friendly rainbow standing in the sky.

One day, Tom and Mia went to the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things on the beach, like shells, crabs, and seaweed.
"Look, Tom, what is that?" Mia asked, pointing to a big, clear thing on the sand. It looked like a balloon, but it had long, thin parts.
"That is a jellyfish, Mia. It lives in the water, but sometimes it comes to the shore. We should not touch it, it can hurt us," Tom said.
"Why can it hurt us, Tom?" Mia asked.
"Because it has stings, Mia. The stings can make us feel pain and itch. Some jellyfish are very bad, they can make us very sick," Tom said.
"Oh, I see. But why is it on the sand, Tom? Does it not like the water?" Mia asked.
"Well, Mia, sometimes the water pushes the jellyfish to the sand, and then they cannot go back. They need the water to live, Mia. If they stay on the sand, they die. They rot," Tom said.
"What does rot mean, Tom?" Mia asked.
"Rot means that they become bad, Mia. They smell bad, they look bad, they fall apart. They are not alive anymore, Mia. They are gone," Tom said.
"That is sad, Tom. I wish the jellyfish could go back to the water and be happy," Mia said.
"Me too, Mia. Me too. But look, there are more jellyfish in the water. They are light and shiny. They are alive and happy. Let's watch them, Mia. They are beautiful," Tom said.
"Okay, Tom. Let's watch them. They are beautiful," Mia said.
They watched the jellyfish in the water, and they smiled. They liked the beach, and they liked the jellyfish. They were happy.

Lily and Tom ran after the rude boy. They tried to get their ball back. But the rude boy was fast and he ran to the other side of the park.

But he did not know that the slide was very hot. The sun had made it hot. It burned his bottom. He screamed and dropped the ball. He slid down the slide very fast and hurt himself.
Lily and Tom saw the ball fall. They ran to the slide and picked up the ball. They were happy. They had their ball back.
They looked at the rude boy. He was crying and rubbing his bottom. He was sorry. He had learned his lesson.
"Are you okay?" Lily asked.
"That slide was hot!" the rude boy said. "It hurt me!"

"Okay, you can play with us," Lily said. "But you have to share and be nice."
The rude boy agreed. He said thank you and sorry. He played with Lily and Tom. They kicked the ball to each other and caught it. They were having fun.

Benny smiled and said, "Yes, I do. Follow me." They walked together until they found a small puddle. The water was not much, but it was enough for the two ants. They drank the water and felt better.
After they drank, Andy and Benny decided to help each other. They would work together to find more water and make the network wet again. They knew that if they worked together, they could make their home a better place for all the ants.

One day, a kid named Ben went to the park with his mom. He saw a big slide and wanted to try it. He ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. He was very happy and excited.
But when he reached the top, he saw another kid sitting on the slide. The other kid was bigger than Ben and had a mean face. He said, "This is my slide. Go away. You can't play here."
Ben felt sad and scared. He wanted to slide, but he didn't want to fight. He looked at his mom, who was watching him from a bench. She smiled at him and said, "Ben, you can share the slide with the other kid. Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy."
Ben nodded and took a deep breath. He said to the other kid, "Hi, I'm Ben. Can we slide together? It will be more fun."
The other kid was surprised. He had never heard anyone say that to him before. He thought for a moment, then said, "Okay, I'm Sam. You can slide with me. But you go first."
Ben smiled and thanked Sam. He slid down the slide and felt a warm glow in his heart. He had made a new friend. He waited for Sam at the bottom and said, "That was fun. Do you want to slide again?"
Sam nodded and smiled back. He felt a warm glow in his heart too. He had learned to share. He followed Ben to the ladder and said, "Yes, let's slide again. And maybe we can play with the swings and the sandbox too."
Ben and Sam played together for a long time. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot. They were both cheerful and kind. Their moms were proud of them and happy to see them get along.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy. It can also help you make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy who loved adventures. One day, she decided to explore the nearby forest. As she was walking along, she discovered a dragon. "Wow!" she gasped.

Amy replied, "I'm exploring the forest."
The dragon said, "Let me show you a secret. But first, you have to make a promise that you will keep it a secret."
Amy promised she would. The dragon continued, "If you do something difficult, it means that it will take more work and time to get what you want. But if you try something easy, then you will see results much faster."
Amy thanked the dragon for the wise advice. She promised to never forget it and to tell everyone she knew the power of an easy task.
The moral of this story is that it is simpler to do something easy then to do something difficult. So next time you think of doing something, remember to choose the easy way.

"No, these are mine too!" Tom said. He pushed Sam away and put all the toys in his arms.
Sam felt sad and angry. He did not like Tom's behavior. He thought Tom was not a good friend. He said, "Tom, you are not fair. You should share the toys with me. We are friends, remember?"
Tom did not listen to Sam. He said, "No, I found them first. They are all mine. Go away!"
Sam was hurt by Tom's words. He decided to leave Tom alone. He walked away from the box and looked for another place to play.
As he walked, he saw a girl sitting on a bench. She had a big book in her lap. She smiled at Sam and said, "Hi, do you want to read with me? This is a fun book. It has many pictures and stories."
Sam was curious about the book. He said, "Yes, I want to read with you. What is your name?"
The girl said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"
Sam said, "My name is Sam. Nice to meet you, Lily."
Lily and Sam became friends. They read the book together and had a good time. Lily showed Sam the pictures and told him the stories. Sam learned many new things from the book. He liked Lily's kindness and generosity. He said, "Lily, you are a good friend. Thank you for sharing your book with me."
Lily said, "You are welcome, Sam. You are a good friend too. Thank you for reading with me."
They hugged each other and smiled.

He walked towards the bench and said, "Sam, I am sorry. I was wrong. I should have shared the toys with you. You are my best friend. Can you forgive me?"
Sam looked at Tom and saw that he was sincere. He remembered that Tom was his best friend too. He said, "Tom, I forgive you. I am glad you came. You can play with us if you want."
Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are very kind. I want to play with you and Lily."
He put the toys on the ground and said, "These are for everyone. We can all play with them."
Sam and Lily accepted Tom's offer. They thanked him for the toys and invited him to join them. They picked up the toys and played together. They had fun and laughed a lot.
Tom learned a lesson that day. He learned that sharing is caring. He learned that being greedy is not good. He learned that being tough is not always right. He learned that being kind and generous is better. He learned that having friends is more important than having things.
He held Sam's and Lily's hands in his palms and said, "You are my best friends. I love you both."

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. They had a big jeep that they could drive around the yard. One day, they decided to go on an adventure with their jeep. They packed some snacks, water, and a map.
"Where are we going?" Tim asked Sam, who was holding the map.
"We are going to the big hill, where we can see the whole town," Sam said. "It will be fun!"
They drove their jeep along the road, past the houses, the shops, and the park. They saw many people and cars, but they did not stop. They wanted to reach the big hill. They followed the map until they saw a sign that said "Hill Road".
"Look, there it is!" Sam said, pointing to the sign. "Let's go!"
They turned their jeep onto the hill road, which was steep and bumpy. They had to go very slow and careful, or they would fall off. The jeep made loud noises as it climbed the hill. Tim and Sam held on tight and cheered.
"We are almost there!" Tim said, looking at the top of the hill.
They reached the top of the hill and parked their jeep. They got out and looked around. They saw the whole town below them, with the houses, the shops, and the park. They also saw the sky, which was blue and clear, with some white clouds.
"Wow, this is amazing!" Sam said, admiring the view.
"Look, a plane!" Tim said, pointing to the sky. "It is so high and fast!"
They watched the plane as it flew across the sky. It looked like a small bird, but with wings and a tail. It made a soft sound as it soared.
"I wish we could fly like that," Sam said, dreaming.
"Maybe we can," Tim said, smiling. "Come on, I have an idea."
He ran back to the jeep and opened the trunk. He took out a big sheet and two sticks. He tied the sheet to the sticks, making a kite. He gave one stick to Sam and kept the other.
"Let's fly our kite!" he said, excited.
They ran to the edge of the hill, where the wind was strong. They lifted their kite and let it catch the wind. The kite flew up in the air, like the plane. It soared and dipped and turned, following their movements.
"Wow, this is fun!" Sam said, laughing.
"We are flying!" Tim said, happy.
They flew their kite for a long time, until the sun began to set. They saw the town light up with colors, like a rainbow. They felt tired and hungry, but also proud and happy.
"Let's go home," Tim said, pulling the kite down.
"OK," Sam said, nodding.
They folded their kite and put it in the trunk. They got in their jeep and drove down the hill road, which was empty and dark. They followed the map until they reached their house, where their mom and dad were waiting for them.
"Hi, boys," their mom said, hugging them. "How was your adventure?"
"It was awesome!" Tim and Sam said together. "We went to the big hill, and we saw the whole town, and we flew a kite!"
They showed their mom and dad their kite and their map. They told them everything they saw and did. Their mom and dad listened and smiled.
"That sounds wonderful," their dad said, proud. "You are very brave and clever."
They ate their dinner and shared their snacks. They drank their water and brushed their teeth. They put on their pajamas and went to bed. They hugged their mom and dad and said good night.
They dreamed of flying and soaring, like the plane and the kite. They dreamed of going on more adventures, with their jeep and their map. They dreamed of being brothers, who liked to play with their toys.
