Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big cross on the grass. It was made of wood and had flowers on it.
"Look, a cross!" Tom said. He ran to it and touched it. "It is interesting. Maybe someone put it here for a reason."
Sam followed him. He did not like the cross. He thought it was scary and sad. "No, it is not interesting. It is bad. Maybe someone died here. We should go away."
Tom did not listen. He wanted to know more about the cross. He knelt down and looked at the flowers. He saw a card with some words on it. He tried to read it.
Sam was angry. He did not want to stay near the cross. He pulled Tom's arm. "Come on, let's go. This is not a toy. This is not fun."
Tom did not want to go. He wanted to read the card. He pushed Sam away. "No, let me see. This is important. Maybe someone needs our help."
They started to fight. They pushed and shouted and hit each other. They did not see the man who was walking to the cross. He was wearing black clothes and had a sad face. He was holding some more flowers. He was the one who put the cross there. He was the one who lost someone he loved.
He saw the boys fighting. He was angry and sad. He yelled at them. "Hey, stop that! What are you doing? This is not a place to play. This is a place to remember. This is a place to be quiet and kind."
The boys stopped fighting. They looked at the man. They felt scared and sorry. They did not know what to say. They did not know what to do.
The man came closer. He put the flowers on the cross. He knelt down and cried. He said some words to the cross. He said some words to the boys. He said he was sorry for yelling. He said he was sad because his wife died. He said he missed her very much. He said he put the cross there to honor her.
The boys listened. They felt sad too. They felt bad for the man. They felt bad for the wife. They felt bad for fighting. They said they were sorry. They said they did not know. They said they wanted to be nice.
The man smiled. He thanked them. He said they were good boys. He said they could stay and look at the cross. He said they could ask him questions. He said he would tell them about his wife. He said she was interesting. He said she liked to play in the park too.
The boys smiled. They thanked him. They said they wanted to hear about his wife. They said they wanted to be his friends. They said they wanted to be quiet and kind.
They knelt down with him. They looked at the cross. They listened to his stories. They learned something new. They felt something good. They were happy.

Ben feels sad. He really likes the bunny and the carrot. He waits for a long time, but Mia does not finish her puzzle. She keeps finding more pieces and making more pictures.

"Look, Ben, I made a cake!" Lily said, holding up a bowl of white powder. "Do you want some?"
"Yes, please!" Ben said, taking a spoonful. He made a face. "Yuck! This is not cake. This is icky!"
Lily laughed. "It's just flour, silly. We need to add other things to make it cake. Like eggs and milk and butter."
"Where are those things?" Ben asked.
"In the fridge," Lily said. "Let's go get them."
They ran to the fridge and opened it. They saw a carton of eggs, a bottle of milk, and a stick of butter. They grabbed them and brought them to the table.
"Now we can make cake!" Lily said.
She opened the carton of eggs and tried to crack one on the edge of the bowl. But she was too strong and the egg broke in her hand. The yolk and the white spilled on the floor.
"Oops!" Lily said.
She tried another egg, but the same thing happened. And another, and another. Soon, all the eggs were on the floor, making a mess.
"Stop, Lily, stop!" Ben said. "You are wasting the eggs!"
"I'm sorry, Ben. I don't know how to crack them," Lily said.
She looked at the bottle of milk. She thought maybe she could pour some in the bowl. She opened the cap and lifted the bottle. But it was too heavy for her and she dropped it. The milk splashed everywhere, on the table, on the chairs, on the floor.
"Uh-oh!" Lily said.
She looked at the stick of butter. She thought maybe she could cut some with a knife. She found a knife in the drawer and took the butter out of the wrapper. She tried to slice the butter, but it was too hard and the knife slipped. It cut her finger and made it bleed.
"Ow!" Lily said.
She dropped the knife and the butter and ran to the sink. She turned on the faucet and put her finger under the water. It hurt a lot and she started to cry.
"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.
He followed her to the sink and saw her finger. He felt sorry for her and gave her a hug.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry we made a mess. I'm sorry you hurt yourself," Ben said.
"It's okay, Ben. It's not your fault. I'm sorry too," Lily said.
They heard a noise. It was their mom. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She saw the flour and the sugar and the salt on the table. She saw the eggs and the milk and the butter on the floor. She saw the knife and the wrapper and the cap in the trash. She saw Lily and Ben by the sink, with Lily's finger wrapped in a paper towel.
"What happened here?" Mom asked.
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt scared and ashamed. They didn't know what to say.
"We were trying to make cake," Lily said in a small voice.
Mom sighed. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She knew they were just kids and they didn't mean to cause trouble. She knew they were curious and creative and wanted to have fun. She knew they loved cake and wanted to surprise her.
She smiled a modest smile and said, "Well, that was very sweet of you, but maybe next time you can ask me for help. Making cake is not easy. It takes a lot of steps and a lot of care. And it also takes a lot of cleaning up."
She took Lily and Ben by the hand and led them to the bathroom. She washed Lily's finger and put a band-aid on it. She gave them both a kiss and said, "I love you, my little chefs. Now let's go back to the kitchen and clean up our mess. And then maybe we can have some real cake. I have some in the fridge that I bought from the store."
Lily and Ben nodded. They felt better. They said, "We love you too, Mom. And we're sorry. And we're hungry."
They went back to the kitchen and helped Mom clean up. They threw away the trash and wiped the table and the chairs and the floor. They put away the pots and pans and spoons and bowls. They closed the cabinet and the fridge and the drawer.
They were done. The kitchen was clean and tidy again.

"Yes, dad, we understand," Lily said.

Tom and Lily waved goodbye to dad and went to play. They saw a big pile of wheat in the barn. It looked soft and yellow.
"Let's make a fort with the wheat!" Tom said.

"Yes, dad, we understand," Tom and Lily said.

"That sounds great, dad!" Tom and Lily said.

One day, they saw a new thing in the park. It was a big balloon. It was red and yellow and blue. It was very pretty. It was tied to a post near the pond. Tom and Mia wanted to see the balloon up close. They left their wagon near a bench and ran to the balloon.
"Wow, look at the balloon!" Tom said. "It is so big and round!"
"I want to touch it!" Mia said. "Maybe it is soft and bouncy!"
They stretched their arms to reach the balloon. But it was too high. They jumped and jumped, but they could not touch it. They felt sad and frustrated.
"Maybe we can use something to help us," Tom said. He looked around and saw a stick on the ground. He picked it up and tried to poke the balloon with it. But the stick was too short.
"Maybe we can use our wagon," Mia said. She had an idea. She ran back to the bench where they left their wagon. But the wagon was gone!
"Tom, our wagon is gone!" Mia shouted. "Someone took it!"
Tom ran to Mia and saw that she was right. Their wagon was not there. Their toys and snacks were not there. They felt scared and angry.
"Who took our wagon?" Tom asked. "We need to find them!"
They looked around and saw a boy and a girl with their wagon. They were pulling it away from the park. They had put their own toys and snacks in the wagon. They looked happy and proud.
"Hey, that's our wagon!" Tom yelled. "Give it back!"
The boy and the girl heard Tom and Mia. They turned and saw them. They did not look sorry. They looked mean and sneaky.
"Finders keepers, losers weepers!" the boy said. "This is our wagon now!"
"No, it's not!" Mia said. "We had it first! It's ours!"
They ran to the boy and the girl. They tried to get their wagon back. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They had a big fight. The balloon watched them from above. It felt sorry for them. It wished they could share and be friends. It had an idea. It used its string to untie itself from the post. It floated down to the children. It touched their heads gently. It made a soft sound.
"Pop!"

Girl: "Hello, Tom. I am Lisa. Would you like to come and play with me?"
Tom smiled and swam over to the bank. He climbed out of the river and started to play with Lisa. They chased each other around and had lots of fun.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. They always said, "This is mine, not yours!" and "You cannot borrow this, go away!"
One day, it was very cold outside. The snow was falling and the wind was blowing. Lily and Tom's family had to stay inside their house. They wanted to play, but they were bored of their own toys. They looked at each other's toys and thought, "Maybe I can borrow that for a while."
Lily saw Tom's train and said, "Can I borrow your train, please? It looks fun."
Tom said, "No, you cannot. This is my train, not yours. Find something else to play with."
Tom saw Lily's doll and said, "Can I borrow your doll, please? It looks pretty."
Lily said, "No, you cannot. This is my doll, not yours. Find something else to play with."
Lily and Tom were sad and angry. They did not want to play with each other. They sat in their corners and hugged their toys.
Their mom saw them and said, "What is wrong, Lily and Tom? Why are you not playing together?"
Lily and Tom said, "We are bored of our toys, but we do not want to share them. We do not want to borrow or lend anything."
Their mom said, "That is not nice, Lily and Tom. Sharing and borrowing are good things to do. They show that you care and respect each other. They make you happy and friendly. They are part of being a family. Do you want to be a happy and friendly family?"
Lily and Tom thought about what their mom said. They felt sorry for being selfish and mean. They looked at each other and said, "Yes, we do. We want to be a happy and friendly family."
They smiled and said, "Can I borrow your toy, please? And can you borrow mine, please? We can play together and have fun."
Their mom said, "That is wonderful, Lily and Tom. I am proud of you. You are a happy and friendly family."
Lily and Tom shared and borrowed their toys. They played together and had fun. They forgot about the cold outside. They were warm and cozy inside their house. They were a happy and friendly family.

Of course, Tommy didn't want to talk things out. He was determined to get up that hill. So he kept climbing, until Millie made him stop.
Tommy was so upset, but he knew that sometimes you have to be smart instead of being stubborn. He and Millie talked it out and decided to look for another hill to climb. In the end, they found an easier hill and both had a great time without getting hurt.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big machine that had many colors and sounds. The machine had a sign that said "Fun Games". Anna and Ben wanted to play the fun games.
But they needed a coin to play. They looked in their pockets, but they had no coins. They looked on the ground, but they saw no coins. They looked at each other, but they had no ideas.
Then they saw a man who was walking by. He had a big bag that made a jingle sound. Anna and Ben thought he had many coins in his bag. They ran to the man and asked him, "Please, can you give us a coin? We want to play the fun games."
The man looked at Anna and Ben. He smiled and said, "Sure, I can give you a coin. I have many coins in my bag. I work at the bank and I supply the coins to the machines. But you have to do something for me first."
Anna and Ben were curious. They asked, "What do we have to do?"
The man said, "You have to tell me a joke. If I laugh, I will give you a coin. If I don't laugh, I will keep my coin. Do you want to try?"
Anna and Ben nodded. They liked jokes. They thought hard and tried to remember a funny joke. Anna said, "Why did the chicken cross the road?"
The man said, "I don't know. Why did the chicken cross the road?"
Anna said, "To get to the other slide!"
The man did not laugh. He said, "That is not a joke. That is a fact. Chickens like slides. Try again."
Ben said, "What do you call a fish that wears a bow?"
The man said, "I don't know. What do you call a fish that wears a bow?"
Ben said, "A rainbow!"
The man laughed. He said, "That is a joke. That is funny. I like rainbows. Here is your coin."
He gave Ben a shiny coin. Ben was happy. He said, "Thank you, mister. You are very kind."
Anna was sad. She had no coin. She said, "I'm sorry, mister. I'm sorry I didn't make you laugh. Can I have a coin too?"
The man looked at Anna. He saw her sad face. He felt sorry for her. He said, "OK, I will give you a coin too. But you have to promise me something."
Anna said, "What do I have to promise?"
The man said, "You have to promise to keep practicing your jokes. Jokes are good for the soul. They make people happy. Do you promise?"
Anna said, "I promise. I will practice my jokes. Thank you, mister. You are very nice."
He gave Anna a shiny coin. Anna was happy. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"
Anna and Ben ran to the machine. They put their coins in the slot. They played the fun games. They had a lot of fun. They thanked the man again. The man waved and said, "You're welcome. Have a good day. And don't forget your jokes!"

They thought glue was white and sticky, like paint. They decided to mix glue with their paints and make more colors.
They took the jar of glue and poured some into their paint cups. They mixed glue and red and got pink. They mixed glue and blue and got light blue. They mixed glue and green and got light green. They were happy again and painted more pictures.
But then they noticed something was wrong. Their pictures were not dry. They were wet and gooey. The glue made the paint sticky and runny. The colors mixed together and became brown and gray. Their pictures were ruined.

They took a cloth and some water and tried to clean up. But it was hard. The glue and the paint were very sticky. They had to scrub and scrub and scrub. They had to march to the sink and back many times. They had to say sorry to the other children and the teacher. They learned a lesson.

When Lily came to her room, she opened her drawer to get her teddy bear. But she did not see her teddy bear. She saw a toy snake. She was very scared. She screamed and ran away.

Lily took the real snake and put it in Jake's drawer. She thought it was funny to scare Jake.

Lily heard his scream and laughed. She thought she was clever. She went to his room and took her teddy bear and the toy snake from his drawer. She said to Jake, "That was not nice to take my teddy bear. You should not play tricks on me. Now you know how it feels to be scared."

Lily said, "Be careful. And don't bring any more snakes home. They are not fun. They are scary."
Jake said, "I won't. I learned my lesson. Snakes are scary. Teddy bears are fun. And sisters are smart."

The cat jumped onto the table and sniffed the box. It was warm, just like the sunshine outside. The cat decided to take a nap on the box and soon fell asleep. 
Meanwhile, inside the black box was a recorder. It recorded the lazy cat's meowing and soft purring. The recorder was so excited that it quietly beeped and whirred with each sound it captured. 
After a while, the rain stopped and the cat woke up. She jumped off the table and walked away with a contented sigh. The recorder continued to quietly whir and record, content with its task.

In the end, Tim learned that having a fine car is nice, but helping others and making them smile is even better.

"Me too, Tim," Mia says. "Maybe we can wave to the people inside."

"Tim, Mia, watch out!" their mom screams. She runs after them and grabs them by their arms. She pulls them back to the gate and hugs them tight.
"Are you okay, Tim, Mia?" she asks. "That was very scary. You could have been hit by the car. You have to be careful and listen to me. I told you not to go outside without me. I love you and I want you to be safe."
Tim and Mia feel sorry and scared. They hug their mom back and say "sorry, mom, we love you too. We won't do that again. We will stay away from the train and the car. We will play with our train set inside. It is more fun and safe."

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big truck stop near their house. The truck had many boxes inside. A man came out of the truck and took out some boxes. He was the deliver man.
"Hello, kids. Do you live here?" the deliver man asked.
"Yes, we do. What are you doing?" Ben said.
"I'm delivering some packages to your neighbors. They ordered some things online. Do you know what online is?" the deliver man said.
"No, we don't. What is it?" Mia said.
"It's when you use a computer to buy things. You can find many things online. Books, toys, clothes, even animals!" the deliver man said.
"Animals? What kind of animals?" Ben said.
"Well, some people like to have pets that are not very common. Like snakes, for example. Do you know what snakes are?" the deliver man said.
"Yes, we do. Snakes are long and slimy and they hiss. We don't like snakes. They are scary!" Mia said.
"Not all snakes are scary. Some snakes are friendly and beautiful. They have different colors and patterns. Some people think they are gifted. They can do amazing things, like climb trees, swim in water, and squeeze their prey. Look, I have a snake in this box. Do you want to see it?" the deliver man said.
He opened the box and showed them a snake. It was green and yellow and had stripes. It looked at them with small black eyes. It flicked its tongue in the air.
"Wow, it's pretty!" Ben said.
"Can we touch it?" Mia said.
"Sure, you can. But be gentle. It's a baby snake. It's going to a new home today. Someone online bought it as a gift for their friend. They must really like snakes!" the deliver man said.
He let them touch the snake. It felt smooth and cool. It wrapped itself around their fingers. It didn't bite or hiss. It seemed to like them.
"Can we keep it?" Ben said.
"Sorry, kids. You can't. It belongs to someone else. Maybe you can ask your parents if you can have a pet someday. But not a snake, if you don't like them. There are many other animals you can choose from. Cats, dogs, birds, fish, hamsters, rabbits, turtles, and more. What kind of pet would you like?" the deliver man said.
"I would like a dog. A big and fluffy one. That can run and play and bark and lick me!" Ben said.
"I would like a cat. A small and soft one. That can purr and cuddle and chase mice and sleep with me!" Mia said.
"Those are good choices. Maybe you will get your wish someday. But for now, I have to go. I have more packages to deliver. Goodbye, kids. Have fun!" the deliver man said.
He put the snake back in the box and closed it. He took it and the other boxes and put them back in the truck. He waved at them and drove away.
Ben and Mia waved back. They looked at each other and smiled. They had learned something new today. They had seen a snake. A gifted snake. But they still liked dogs and cats better. They went back to their house and told their parents about their adventure. They hoped they would see the deliver man again. Maybe he would bring them a surprise someday. A nice surprise. Not a snake.

The bird showed the lion how to catch food and play with other animals. The lion was happy and not nervous anymore. They became good friends. The little lion learned that it is good to ask for help when you are nervous, and that friends can show you new things.

Sara and Tom were playing in the living room. They had many toys and books to play with. Sara liked to look at the magazine with pictures of animals. Tom liked to make noises with the cars and trucks.
"Look, Sara, this is a lion. It is big and scary. It can roar and bite," Tom said, showing Sara the magazine.
"I don't like lions. They are too scary. I like rabbits. They are soft and cute. They can hop and eat carrots," Sara said, pointing to another page.
"Rabbits are boring. Lions are fun. They can wash themselves with their tongues. See?" Tom said, licking his hand and rubbing it on his face.
"Yuck, Tom, that is dirty. You need to wash your face with water and soap. Come on, let's go to the bathroom," Sara said, pulling Tom by the hand.
"No, I don't want to wash my face. I want to play with the lion. It is not dirty. It is clean and strong," Tom said, resisting Sara.
"Yes, you do. Mommy said we have to wash our faces before lunch. If you don't, you will get germs and be sick. And the lion will not like you. It will smell you and run away," Sara said, trying to convince Tom.
"Really? The lion will not like me?" Tom said, looking sad.
"Really. But if you wash your face, the lion will like you. And I will like you too. And we can play with the lion and the rabbit together. OK?" Sara said, smiling.
"OK. Fine. Let's go wash our faces. But you have to wash yours too. And then we can play with the magazine," Tom said, agreeing with Sara.
They went to the bathroom and washed their faces with water and soap. They dried them with a towel and went back to the living room. They looked at the magazine and played with the lion and the rabbit. They were happy and not scared.

They came across a beautiful field of blueberries and their eyes lit up.

Jack said, "Let's pick some of the gray ones - they look yummy!" 
But Jill said, "No, no, it's better not to take things that don't belong to us."
Jack didn't listen, he just picked many of the gray blueberries and ate them. 
Jill said, "We better go now - or someone might meet us!"

He shouted, "What are you doing?! You're stealing my blueberries!"
Jill tried to explain, but the man wouldn't listen. 
He punished them for stealing, and they never saw each other again.
Moral of the story: Don't take things that don't belong to you.

"Let's play with the magic wand!" Lily said. She found the wand in a box of old things. It was shiny and had a star on the end. "Maybe it can do something cool!"
"Okay, let's try it!" Tom said. He took the wand and pointed it at the sofa. He said, "Sofa, shrink!" Nothing happened. He pointed it at the lamp. He said, "Lamp, shrink!" Nothing happened. He pointed it at Lily. He said, "Lily, shrink!"
Lily felt a tickle. She looked at her hands and feet. They were getting smaller and smaller. She screamed, "Tom, stop! You're making me shrink!"
Tom was shocked. He dropped the wand. He ran to Lily. He tried to pick her up, but she was too tiny. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry! I didn't know it would work! How can I make you big again?"
Lily was scared. She saw a big spider crawling near her. She said, "Tom, help! There's a spider! Quick, find the wand!"
Tom looked around. He saw the wand on the floor. He reached for it, but it was too far. He saw a pool of water on the table. It was from a glass that he spilled. He had an idea. He said, "Lily, jump on the pool! Maybe it will make you grow!"
Lily saw the pool. It was like a lake to her. She was afraid of the water, but she was more afraid of the spider. She said, "Okay, I'll try!" She ran to the pool and jumped in.
The water was cold and wet. She felt a splash. She felt another tickle. She looked at her hands and feet. They were getting bigger and bigger. She said, "Tom, it's working! I'm growing!"
Tom was happy. He saw Lily coming out of the pool. She was still wet, but she was normal size. He said, "Lily, you're back! I'm so glad! I'm sorry I made you shrink!"
Lily hugged Tom. She said, "Tom, it's okay. I'm not mad. I'm just glad you saved me! That was a scary adventure!"
They looked at the wand. They decided to put it back in the box. They said, "Let's never play with the magic wand again!" They went to dry themselves and find something else to do. They hoped the rain would stop soon.

One day, their mom came into the living room and saw them jumping on the sofa and the cushions. She was not happy. She said, "Stop jumping on the sofa and the cushions! You are making a mess and you could hurt yourself or break something. Go and play with your toys or read your books instead."
Lily and Tom did not listen to their mom. They said, "No, we want to jump on the sofa and the cushions! It is more fun and lively than playing with toys or reading books. You are boring and mean. Let us jump!" And they kept jumping and making noises.
Their mom was very angry. She said, "If you do not listen to me, you will not be allowed to play in the living room anymore. You will have to go to your room and stay there until you say sorry and behave." And she took away the sofa and the cushions and put them in another room.
Lily and Tom were very sad and sorry. They realized they had been rude and naughty. They missed the sofa and the cushions, and they missed their mom. They went to their room and said, "We are sorry, mom. We should have listened to you. You were right. Jumping on the sofa and the cushions was not a good idea. Can we please play in the living room again?"
Their mom heard them and came to their room. She hugged them and said, "I forgive you, Lily and Tom. I love you very much. Lily and Tom nodded and said, "We understand, mom. We promise. Thank you for forgiving us and for letting us play in the living room again. We love you too." And they went to the living room and played nicely and happily with the sofa, the cushions, the toys and the books.
The moral of the story is: We should listen to our parents and respect their rules, because they know what is best for us and they want us to be safe and happy. We should also be grateful for what we have and enjoy it in a good way.

Tim showed the crystal to his friend, Sally. "Look what I found!" he said. "It's so pretty!" Sally looked at the crystal and saw that it had a sharp edge. "Be careful, Tim," she warned. "It looks sharp and could hurt you."
But Tim didn't listen. He wanted to play a trick on Sally. He put the crystal in her bag when she wasn't looking. Later, Sally reached into her bag and felt a sharp pain. The crystal had cut her hand. She cried and ran home.
Sally's mom saw her crying and asked what happened. Sally told her about the crystal and Tim's naughty trick. Her mom was very angry and told Tim's mom about it. Tim's mom scolded him and took away his toys.
From that day on, Tim was no longer allowed to play with Sally. He was very sad and lonely. He wished he had never played that naughty trick with the sharp crystal.

Ben and Lily were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and cars. Ben had a lot of blue blocks and Lily had a lot of red blocks.
"Let's add our blocks and make a big rainbow tower!" Ben said.
"OK, that sounds fun!" Lily said. They started to add their blocks, one by one, on top of each other. They made a tall and colorful tower.
But then, Tom came along. Tom was older and bigger than Ben and Lily. He liked to make jokes, but not nice jokes. He liked to make jokes that made other kids sad or angry.
"Wow, what a silly tower!" Tom said. "It looks like a big candy cane. Can I have a bite?" He pretended to bite the tower, but he really pushed it with his hand. The tower fell down and the blocks scattered everywhere.
Ben and Lily were very sad. They had worked hard to make their tower. They did not think Tom's joke was funny. They thought it was mean.
"Tom, you are a bad boy!" Lily said. "You ruined our tower!"
"Ha ha, it was just a joke!" Tom said. "Don't be such babies. It's only blocks. You can make another one."
But Ben and Lily did not want to make another one. They were too upset. They picked up their blocks and went to find another place to play.
Tom was left alone. He looked at the mess he had made. He felt a little troubled. He wondered why Ben and Lily did not like his joke. He wondered why he had no friends to play with. He wondered if he should say sorry.

Dan and Mia went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They saw a big crab with a red shell and big claws. Dan wanted to touch it, but Mia was scared.
"Look, Mia, a crab!" Dan said. "Can I touch it?"
"No, Dan, it might pinch you!" Mia said. "It looks mean and angry."
Dan did not listen to Mia. He reached out his hand to the crab. The crab saw Dan and snapped its claws. Dan yelled and pulled back his hand. He had a small cut on his finger. It hurt a lot.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Dan cried. "The crab bit me!"
Mom and Dad heard Dan and ran to him. They saw the crab and the cut. Mom took Dan in her arms and Dad got a band-aid. They cleaned the cut and put the band-aid on it.
"Dan, you should not touch crabs. They are wild animals and they can hurt you," Mom said. "You should yield to them and leave them alone."
"I'm sorry, Mom. I was curious. I wanted to see the crab," Dan said. "But it was not nice. It was mean and angry."
Mia hugged Dan and said, "It's okay, Dan. I'm sorry you got hurt. Maybe the crab was scared too. Maybe it thought you were a bald eagle and wanted to eat it."
Dan and Mia laughed. They did not know what a bald eagle was, but they thought it sounded funny. They decided to play with their buckets and shovels instead of looking for crabs. They had fun at the beach and learned a lesson.

Anna and Ben are playing with magnets. They have many magnets of different colors and shapes. They stick them on the fridge, on the table, on the door. They have fun making patterns and noises.
"Look, Anna, I have a big red magnet. It is stronger than yours," Ben says. He shows Anna his magnet and tries to pull hers away.
"No, Ben, that is not nice. My magnet is important to me. It is a gift from Grandma. She gave it to me on my birthday. She said it is special," Anna says. She holds her magnet tight and does not let go.
Ben does not listen. He wants to have Anna's magnet. He thinks of a plan. He lies to Anna. He says, "Anna, I have a surprise for you. Close your eyes and hold out your hand."
Anna is curious. She likes surprises. She closes her eyes and holds out her hand. Ben quickly swaps his magnet for Anna's. He puts Anna's magnet in his pocket and gives her his magnet.
"Open your eyes, Anna. Here is your surprise," Ben says. He smiles.
Anna opens her eyes. She sees the red magnet in her hand. She feels something is wrong. She looks at Ben. She sees a bulge in his pocket. She realizes what he did. She is angry and sad.
"Ben, you lied to me. You took my magnet. That is not a surprise. That is a trick. That is not fair. That is not kind. Give me back my magnet," Anna says. She cries.
Ben feels bad. He knows he did something wrong. He sees Anna's tears. He remembers Grandma. He remembers how she loves them both. He remembers how she taught them to share and to be honest. He is sorry.
"Anna, I am sorry. I lied to you. I took your magnet. That was a bad thing to do. Here is your magnet. Please forgive me," Ben says. He takes out Anna's magnet and gives it to her.
Anna stops crying. She takes her magnet. She looks at Ben. She sees he is sorry. She remembers Grandma. She remembers how she loves them both. She remembers how she taught them to forgive and to be friends. She is happy.
"Ben, I forgive you. I am happy you are sorry. Thank you for giving me back my magnet. It is special to me. But you know what? You are more special to me. You are my brother. I love you," Anna says. She hugs Ben.
Ben hugs Anna back. He says, "I love you too, Anna. You are my sister. You are more important to me than any magnet. Let's play together. Let's share our magnets. Let's make Grandma proud."
Anna and Ben smile. They play together. They share their magnets. They make Grandma proud. They learn a lesson. They learn to be honest, to be fair, to be kind, to be forgiving, and to be loving. They are happy.

"Stop it, Ben!" Sara said. She pulled the doll away from Ben. "You are being mean!"

"Give me the doll, now!" Ben shouted. He pushed Sara and made her fall. He snatched the doll from her and ran away.

Mommy was very angry. She went to Ben and took the doll from him.

Ben did not want to say sorry. He did not want to give the doll back. He threw a tantrum. He kicked and screamed and cried.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room. They liked to jump on the sofa and pretend they were flying. Lily saw a big spring under the sofa. She wanted to see what it was.
"Look, Ben, a spring!" she said. "Can I have it?"
Ben looked at the spring. It was shiny and coiled. He thought it looked fun.
"OK, you can have it," he said. "But be careful. It might be broken."
Lily took the spring and held it in her hands. She felt it was hard and cold. She pulled it and let it go. It made a funny sound.
"Boing, boing, boing!" she said. "This is a fun spring!"
She pulled it harder and harder. She wanted to make it longer. But then, the spring snapped. It flew out of her hands and hit the window. The window cracked and made a loud noise.
"Crash!" the window said.
Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the spring and ran to the sofa. They hid behind the cushions.
"Mama, mama!" they cried. "The window is broken!"
Mama came into the living room. She saw the broken window and the spring on the floor. She was angry and sad.
"Who did this?" she asked. "Who broke the window?"
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry and ashamed. They knew they had done something bad.
"We did, mama," they said. "We were playing with the spring. We didn't mean to break the window."
Mama sighed. She picked up the spring and the broken glass. She put them in the trash.
"Playing with the spring was not a good idea," she said. "The spring was broken. It was dangerous. You could have hurt yourselves or someone else. You have to be more careful with what you play with. And you have to tell me when you find something strange or broken. Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They hugged mama and said they were sorry.
"It's OK, my loves," mama said. "I forgive you. But you have to help me fix the window. And no more jumping on the sofa. OK?"
Lily and Ben agreed. They helped mama fix the window. They learned their lesson. They never played with the spring again.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Mom will be angry. We have to clean up."
Tom nodded. He grabbed a cloth and tried to wipe the dirt from the carpet. Lily picked up the broken pieces of the vase and put them in a bag. They worked hard, but they could not fix everything.
Suddenly, they heard the door open. Mom was home. They hid behind the sofa and hoped she would not see them.
"Hello, kids. I'm back. How was your day?" Mom said.
She walked into the living room and saw the mess. She gasped.
"What happened here? Who did this?" she asked.
Lily and Tom looked at each other. They were scared. They did not want to lie, but they also did not want to get in trouble.
Lily decided to tell the truth. She came out from behind the sofa and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. It was us. We were playing with our toys and we were clumsy. We broke some things and we tried to clean up, but we couldn't."
Mom looked at Lily and then at Tom, who also came out. She was not happy, but she was also proud of them for being honest.
"Thank you for telling me the truth, Lily and Tom. I'm glad you did not lie. But you also have to be more careful and respectful of our things. You have to learn to play without making a mess. Do you understand?" she said.
Lily and Tom nodded. They felt sorry for what they did.
"We understand, Mom. We're sorry. We love you," they said.
Mom smiled and hugged them.
"I love you too, kids. Now, let's go and wash your hands and faces. Then we can have some cookies and milk and talk about how to avoid being clumsy next time," she said.
Lily and Tom followed Mom to the bathroom. They were happy that she forgave them. They learned a lesson about being careful and telling the truth. They also learned that Mom loved them no matter what.

One day, a little girl came into the kitchen to make food. She saw the lonely pan on the shelf and thought it looked sad. She wanted to help the pan, so she took it down to use it. But as she was carrying the pan, she tripped and dropped it on the floor.
The loud noise from the drop made the other kitchen things wake up. They saw the lonely pan on the floor and felt bad. They all decided to be friends with the pan, so it would not be lonely anymore. From that day on, the pan was happy and had many friends in the kitchen.

Sara liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily was a princess with a pink dress and a crown. Sara liked to pretend that Lily was going to marry a prince.
One day, Sara's brother Tom came into her room. He saw Sara playing with Lily and her other dolls. He wanted to join the game.
"Can I play with you?" he asked.
Sara looked at him. She did not want to play with Tom. He was noisy and messy. He always broke her toys.
"No, you can't," she said. "This is a princess game. You are not a princess."
Tom frowned. He did not like Sara's answer. He saw a doll on the floor. It was a prince with a blue suit and a hat. He picked it up.
"I can be a prince," he said. "I have a prince doll. See?"
Sara shook her head. She did not want Tom to touch her dolls. She snatched the prince doll from his hand.
"No, you can't," she said again. "This is my prince. He is going to marry Lily. You can't have him."
Tom was angry. He wanted to play with the prince doll. He tried to grab it back from Sara.
"Yes, I can," he said. "Give me the prince. He is mine."
Sara and Tom started to fight over the prince doll. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not listen to each other. They were both stubborn.
Their mother heard the noise. She came into the room. She saw Sara and Tom fighting over the prince doll. She was not happy.
"Stop it, both of you," she said. "What are you doing?"
Sara and Tom stopped fighting. They looked at their mother. They both wanted to explain.
"Sara won't let me play with her dolls," Tom said. "She is mean."
"Tom wants to take my prince," Sara said. "He is rude."
Their mother sighed. She knew that Sara and Tom did not get along well. They always argued and complained. They were both persistent.
She took the prince doll from Sara's hand. She held it up.
"Listen to me," she said. "This is not your prince or Tom's prince. This is a toy. A toy is something that you can share and enjoy with others. You can't insist on having it all to yourself. That is selfish and unfair."
She looked at Sara and Tom. She hoped that they would understand.
"Do you want to play nicely together?" she asked. "Or do you want to go to your own rooms?"
Sara and Tom looked at each other. They did not want to go to their own rooms. They wanted to play.
They nodded. They said sorry to each other. They agreed to share the prince doll and the other dolls.
Their mother smiled. She gave them the prince doll. She hugged them.
"That's better," she said. "Now you can have fun together. Remember, sharing is caring."
Sara and Tom smiled. They thanked their mother. They started to play with the dolls. They pretended that the prince and Lily were getting married. They invited their mother to the wedding.
They were happy. They learned a lesson. They were not persistent anymore. They were friendly.

Lila and Ben were playing in the woods. They liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things. They saw a hut made of sticks and leaves. It looked old and fragile.
"Let's go inside!" Ben said. He ran to the hut and pushed the door.
"Wait, Ben! It might break!" Lila said. She followed him slowly.
But it was too late. The door fell down and the hut collapsed. Ben was trapped under the sticks and leaves. He cried out in pain.
"Lila, help me! It hurts!" Ben said.
Lila was scared. She tried to lift the sticks and leaves, but they were too heavy. She looked around and saw a man walking nearby. He had a bag and a hat.
"Help, help!" Lila shouted. She waved her arms.
The man heard her and came over. He saw Ben under the hut. He put down his bag and hat. He was a doctor. He knew how to heal people.
"Don't worry, children. I'll help you," the man said. He moved the sticks and leaves carefully. He took out a bandage and a cream from his bag. He wrapped Ben's arm and leg where they were cut and bruised. He gave him a hug and a candy.
"There, there. You'll be fine soon," the man said. He smiled at Lila and Ben.
"Thank you, mister. You are very kind," Lila said. She hugged the man too.
"You're welcome, little ones. But you should be careful. This hut was very old and fragile. It could have hurt you more," the man said. He picked up his bag and hat.
"Where are you going, mister?" Ben asked.
"I'm going to the village. I have to heal more people. There are many sick and hurt people there," the man said.
"Can we go with you, mister? We want to see the village and help you heal people," Lila said.
The man thought for a moment. He nodded.
"Sure, you can come with me. But you have to ask your parents first. And you have to promise me to be careful and listen to me," the man said.
Lila and Ben nodded. They ran to their parents, who were nearby. They told them what happened and asked them if they could go with the man. Their parents agreed, but they told them to be back before dark.
Lila and Ben were happy. They thanked their parents and ran back to the man. They held his hands and walked with him to the village. They learned many things from him. They saw how he healed people with his bag and his hat. They helped him by giving water and smiles to the people. They made many new friends.
They had a wonderful day. They learned how to heal and how to be kind. They also learned how to be careful and not to play with fragile things. They thanked the man and said goodbye to the people. They went back to their parents, who hugged them and kissed them. They told them their story and showed them their bandages and candies. They were proud and happy.
They slept well that night. They dreamed of the hut, the man, and the village. They dreamed of healing and kindness. They dreamed of being explorers and finding new things. They dreamed of being happy.

Suddenly, Danny had an idea. He said, “Let’s play hide and seek. You can hide and I’ll find you.” Jake was so excited! He quickly found a good spot to hide and waited for Danny to come find him.
Danny searched for a long time, but he couldn’t find Jake. Suddenly, he heard laughter from behind a shelf. When he looked, he saw Jake laughing and thought he was just teasing him. Danny was mad, but then he remembered the idea of being independent.
He said, “No, I won’t get mad. Instead of teasing you, I want you to experience success. I know you can find me, Jake.” Jake nodded and smiled. He went around the room and finally found Danny.
The moral of the story is to be independent and find your own successes. Teasing may be funny, but it’s better to appreciate success and help others find it too.

One day, Lily came home from school and wanted to play with her comb. She opened her drawer, but her comb was not there. She looked around her room, but she could not find it. She felt sad and angry. Who took her comb?
She went to ask her brother, Ben. Ben was playing with his cars on the floor. Lily saw something shiny in his hand. It was her pink comb!
"Ben, give me back my comb!" Lily shouted. "That is mine!"
Ben looked at her and smiled. He said, "No, this is my comb now. I like it. It makes my cars go faster. See?" He rubbed the comb on his car and zoomed it across the floor.
Lily tried to grab the comb, but Ben was stronger. He pushed her away and said, "Go away, Lily. You are a baby. You don't need a comb. You have ugly hair."
Lily felt hurt and angry. She started to cry. She ran to her mom and told her what Ben did. Mom was busy making dinner. She said, "Lily, calm down. It's just a comb. You can share it with Ben. He is your brother. You should forgive him."
Lily did not want to forgive Ben. She wanted her comb back. She said, "No, Mom. He is mean. He stole my comb. He made fun of my hair. I hate him."
Mom sighed and said, "Lily, don't say that. You don't hate your brother. You love him. He loves you too. He just made a mistake. He will give you back your comb later. Now, go and play nicely."
Lily did not listen to Mom. She was still angry. She went back to her room and looked for something to get back at Ben. She saw his favorite teddy bear on his bed. She had an idea. She took the teddy bear and ran to the bathroom. She turned on the faucet and soaked the teddy bear in water. Then she took some scissors and cut off its ears and eyes. She smiled and said, "There, Ben. Now you know how I feel."
She threw the teddy bear on the floor and ran back to her room. She hid under her bed and waited for Ben to come.
Ben came to his room after dinner. He saw his wet and ruined teddy bear on the floor. He screamed and cried. He ran to Mom and showed her what Lily did. Mom was shocked and angry. She said, "Lily, what have you done? This is terrible. How could you do this to your brother? You are a very naughty girl. You need to apologize and make up with Ben right now."
Lily did not want to apologize or make up with Ben. She said, "No, Mom. He deserved it. He took my comb. He was mean to me. I hate him."
Mom said, "Lily, that is no excuse. You did something very wrong. You hurt your brother's feelings. You destroyed his toy. You are not forgiven. You are grounded. You have to stay in your room for a week. And you have to give back your comb to Ben. You don't deserve it."
Lily felt shocked and scared. She did not expect Mom to be so mad. She realized she made a big mistake. She wished she had listened to Mom and forgiven Ben. She wished she had not hurt his teddy bear. She wished she had her pink comb back. She wished she could say sorry and hug her brother. But it was too late. She had no comb, no teddy bear, no brother, and no Mom. She was alone and sad. She cried and cried. She had a bad ending.

"Okay," Lily says. "But they are sour. Do you like sour things?"
"I don't know," Ben says. "Let's try."
They each take a lemon. They peel the lemon. They bite the lemon. They make a funny face.
"Yuck!" Ben says. "This is sour!"
"I told you," Lily says. "They are sour. Do you want something else?"
"Yes, please," Ben says. "Do you have something sweet?"
Lily looks around. She sees a jar of honey. She takes the jar. She opens the jar. She gives Ben a spoon of honey.
"Here," Lily says. "This is sweet. Do you like sweet things?"
Ben tastes the honey. He smiles.
"Mmm," Ben says. "This is sweet. I like sweet things. Thank you, Lily."
"You're welcome, Ben," Lily says. "Do you want to share the honey?"
"Yes, let's share," Ben says. "We can have honey and lemons. That's a good snack."
They eat the honey and the lemons. They like the snack. They are happy. They understand each other. They are friends.

Sam and Mia saw the cat. They were scared and screamed. They jumped off the swings and ran away. The cat chased them, but it was not fast enough. Sam and Mia reached the gate of the park. They ran out and looked for their mom.

One day, Lily's cousin Tom came to visit. Tom was a big boy who liked to play with cars and trucks. He did not like dolls at all. He saw Lily playing with Rosie and said, "Dolls are silly. Cars are better. Give me your doll."
Lily did not want to give Tom her doll. She said, "No, Rosie is mine. Go play with your cars." She hugged Rosie and turned away from Tom.
Tom was angry. He wanted to take Rosie from Lily. He ran to Lily and tried to grab Rosie. Lily held on to Rosie and said, "Stop, Tom. You are hurting me and Rosie."
Tom did not stop. He pulled Rosie harder and harder. Lily felt Rosie's blouse rip in her hands. She cried out, "No, Tom. You broke Rosie's blouse. You are mean."
Tom did not care. He pushed Lily and ran away with Rosie. Lily fell to the floor and sobbed. She looked at the torn blouse in her hands and felt very sad. She loved Rosie and did not want her to be hurt.
Lily's mom heard Lily crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily on the floor and the torn blouse in her hands. She saw Tom running away with Rosie. She was angry with Tom and said, "Tom, come back here. You have to say sorry to Lily and give her back her doll. You cannot push and take things that are not yours."
Tom did not want to say sorry or give back Rosie. He said, "I don't care. I don't like dolls. They are stupid."
Lily's mom said, "Dolls are not stupid. They are Lily's toys and she loves them. You have to respect her feelings and her things. You have to be kind and share. Now, give Rosie back to Lily and say sorry."
Tom did not want to, but he knew he had to. He gave Rosie back to Lily and said, "Sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have pushed you and taken your doll."
Lily took Rosie and hugged her. She said, "Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. But please don't do that again. Rosie is my friend and I don't want her to be hurt."
Lily's mom said, "That's very good, Lily. You are very sweet and generous. And Tom, you have to learn to be more gentle and polite. You can play with your cars, but you have to ask before you touch other people's toys. And you have to say please and thank you. Do you understand?"
Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I understand. I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, mom. Can I play with you and Rosie?"
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice and careful. Rosie likes to play with cars too, sometimes. But she also likes to have her hair brushed and her blouse fixed. Can you help me with that?"
Tom said, "OK, I can try. Maybe dolls are not so silly after all."
Lily's mom said, "That's very good, Tom. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go and find some thread and a needle and fix Rosie's blouse. And then you can all play together nicely."

Lily asked her mom for some soup to share with the bird. Her mom said yes and gave her a small bowl. Lily went outside and put the soup near the bird. The bird saw the soup and flew down to eat it. The bird loved the soup too! From that day on, Lily and the bird were the best of friends. They always shared the tasty soup that Lily's mom made.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to travel on their bikes. They go to the park, the shop, and the lake. They have fun together.
One day, they see a big hill. They want to go up the hill. They think it will be fun. They pedal hard and fast. They feel the wind in their hair.
But the hill is tough. It is steep and rocky. Tom's bike hits a crack. His tire pops. He falls off his bike. He hurts his knee. He cries.
Sue stops her bike. She runs to Tom. She sees his bike and his knee. She says, "Oh no, Tom! Are you okay?"
Tom says, "No, Sue. My bike is broken. My knee is bleeding. It hurts a lot."
Sue says, "Don't worry, Tom. I will help you. We can fix your bike. We can clean your knee. We can go home."
She takes Tom's hand. She pushes his bike. They walk down the hill. They find a shop. They buy a new tire and a band-aid. They fix Tom's bike. They clean Tom's knee. They put the band-aid on.
Tom says, "Thank you, Sue. You are a good friend. You helped me a lot."
Sue says, "You're welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too. You are brave and strong."
They hug. They smile. They get on their bikes. They travel home. They are happy.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big board lying on the grass. Sam wanted to use it as a slide.
"Look, Mia, a slide!" he said. "Let's go on it!"
Mia was not sure. The board looked old and dirty. She thought it might break or hurt them.
"Sam, I don't think that's a good idea," she said. "The board is not fit for sliding. It might have nails or splinters. And it's too high. We could fall and get hurt."
Sam did not listen. He was too excited. He ran to the board and climbed on it. He tried to slide down, but the board was not smooth. It was rough and bumpy. Sam felt a sharp pain in his leg. He cried out loud.
"Mia, help! I'm stuck! The board has a nail in it! It poked my leg!"
Mia ran to Sam. She saw the blood on his leg. She felt scared and sorry. She wished they had not played with the board.
"Sam, I'm sorry. I'll get help. Don't move. Stay calm," she said.
She ran to the nearest adult. She told them what happened. They called an ambulance. They took Sam to the hospital. They fixed his leg. He had to wear a bandage for a while.
Sam learned his lesson. He never played with boards again. He listened to Mia more. She was his best friend. She always looked out for him. They played with safer things. They had fun. They were happy.

His mommy said, "I can make you a new crown. It will be nice and clean and you can be the king of our castle."
So the mommy fetched the glitter and ribbon, then she and the little boy crafted a beautiful, sparkling crown together. The little boy put it on and said, "I am the king!" with a big smile. 
The moral of the story is that it's better to create something new and special than to hold on to something old or dirty.

"My license?" Anna says, confused. She stops her car and looks at Ben.
"Yes, your license. You need a license to drive a car. It is a card with your name and picture on it," Ben explains.
"Oh, I don't have a license," Anna says, frowning.
"That's not good, Anna. You can't drive without a license. You might get in trouble," Ben says, shaking his head.
"But I like driving my pink car. It is fun," Anna says, pouting.
"I have an idea. Why don't we make you a license?" Ben says, brightening up.
"How do we do that?" Anna asks, curious.
"Come on, I will show you," Ben says, taking her hand. He leads her to the kitchen, where they find some paper, crayons, scissors and tape. They draw a card with Anna's name and picture on it, and cut it out. Then they tape it to the back of her pink car.
"Look, Anna, now you have a license!" Ben says, proudly.
"Wow, Ben, you are so smart! Thank you for helping me!" Anna says, happily.
"You're welcome, Anna. Now let's go back to driving our cars!" Ben says, excitedly.

She heard a voice behind her. It was her daddy. He said, "Lily, what are you doing? That cake is for mommy's birthday. You can't have it now. You have to wait until later."
Lily turned around and saw her daddy. He was smiling, but he looked a little angry. She felt sorry and scared. She said, "I'm sorry, daddy. I just wanted to see the cake. It's so blue and pretty. Can I have a little bit, please?"

He lifted Lily off the chair and carried her to the living room. Lily hugged her daddy and said, "I love you, daddy. And I love mommy. And I love cake. Can we sing happy birthday now?"
Daddy laughed and said, "Yes, Lily. We can sing happy birthday now. You are a sweet and silly girl. But next time, don't crawl to the cake. Ask me first, okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, daddy. I will ask you first. But can I still crawl to the closet?"

Mommy said, "Yes, Lily. You can have some now. But first, let's sing happy birthday to me. And then, let's make a wish and blow the candles. And then, let's share the cake and have fun. How does that sound?"
Lily said, "That sounds great, mommy. Happy birthday, mommy. You are the best mommy ever."
They sang happy birthday to mommy. They made a wish and blew the candles. They shared the cake and had fun. Lily ate a big piece of blue cake. She liked it very much. She was happy and full. She crawled to the closet and took a nap. She dreamed of blue cakes and cats and snakes and bugs. She was a happy little girl.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and dress up. One day, Lily got a new bracelet from her mom. It was bright and shiny, with many colors. Lily was very happy and showed it to Anna.
"Wow, your bracelet is so pretty!" Anna said. "Can I try it on?"
"Okay, but only for a little bit," Lily said. She took off her bracelet and gave it to Anna. Anna put it on her wrist and smiled.
They played for a while, but then Lily wanted her bracelet back. She asked Anna to give it to her.
"Please, Anna, can I have my bracelet back? It is mine and I miss it," Lily said.
"But I like it too," Anna said. "It is so bright and shiny. Can I keep it for a little longer?"
"No, Anna, you can't. It is not yours, it is mine. Give it back to me now," Lily said. She reached for her bracelet, but Anna pulled away.
"No, Lily, you can't. It is mine now. I won't give it back to you," Anna said. She ran away with the bracelet.
Lily was very sad and angry. She cried and shouted. She wanted her bracelet back. She did not want to be friends with Anna anymore.
Then, Lily's mom came. She saw Lily crying and asked her what was wrong.
"Anna took my bracelet and won't give it back. She is mean and selfish. I hate her," Lily said.
Lily's mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily, that was not nice of Anna. But you shouldn't hate her. Maybe she likes your bracelet so much because she doesn't have one of her own. Maybe she is lonely and wants to be your friend. Maybe you can share your bracelet with her and make her happy."
Lily thought about what her mom said. She remembered that Anna was her best friend. She remembered that they had fun playing together. She remembered that she liked to make Anna smile.
Lily wiped her tears and said, "You're right, mom. I don't hate Anna. I love her. Maybe I can share my bracelet with her and make her happy. Maybe we can be friends again."
Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's very kind and generous of you, Lily. I'm proud of you. Come, let's go find Anna and talk to her."
Lily and her mom went to look for Anna. They found her sitting on a bench, holding the bracelet. She looked sad and guilty.
Lily walked up to her and said, "Hi, Anna. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I know you like my bracelet. Do you want to share it with me?"
Anna looked up and saw Lily and her mom. She felt ashamed and sorry. She said, "Hi, Lily. I'm sorry I took your bracelet. It was wrong of me. I know it is yours. Here, you can have it back."
She handed the bracelet to Lily. Lily took it and said, "Thank you, Anna. But you don't have to give it back. You can keep it for a while. I don't mind. I want you to be happy. You are my best friend."
Anna smiled and said, "Really? Thank you, Lily. You are very sweet and nice. You are my best friend too."
They hugged and said sorry to each other. They put the bracelet on each other's wrist and said, "We can take turns wearing it. It is our friendship bracelet."
Lily's mom watched them and said, "That's wonderful, girls. You are both very good and kind. You have learned to share and forgive. That is the moral of this story. Sharing and forgiving are important for friendship."

Then, something unexpected happened. The ball started to move! It rolled out of the box and turned into a big, friendly dog! The sheep was so surprised! The dog said, "I am a magic dog! I can be your friend, too!" The mighty sheep was very happy. From that day on, the sheep and the magic dog played together in the big field. They had lots of fun and became best friends.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park and pretend they were knights and princesses. One day, they saw a big hill with a cave. They wondered what was inside.
"Let's go and see!" said Ben. "Maybe there is a dragon!"
Lily was scared. She did not like dragons. They were big and loud and had fire. She said, "No, Ben, I don't want to go. What if the dragon hurts us?"
Ben said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will protect you. I have a sword and a shield. And I promise, I will not leave you alone. Come on, it will be fun!"
Lily trusted Ben. He was her best friend. He always kept his promises. She said, "Okay, Ben, I will go with you. But you have to hold my hand."
Ben nodded. He took Lily's hand and they walked to the cave. They were brave and curious. They wanted to see the dragon.
When they reached the cave, they heard a roar. It was the dragon! It was big and green and had scales and horns. It saw Lily and Ben and opened its mouth. It was ready to breathe fire.
Lily and Ben were scared. They wanted to run away. But Ben remembered his promise. He said, "Lily, stay behind me. I will fight the dragon. You are my friend and I will not leave you alone."
He raised his sword and shield and faced the dragon. He shouted, "Go away, dragon! This is our park and you are not welcome here!"
The dragon was surprised. It did not expect a little boy to challenge it. It was curious and amused. It said, "Who are you, little boy? And why do you have a sword and a shield?"
Ben said, "I am Ben, the knight. And this is Lily, the princess. We are playing in the park and you are ruining our game. You are big and loud and have fire. You are scary and mean. You have to leave!"
The dragon said, "I am not scary and mean. I am lonely and bored. I have no friends and no games. I only have fire. And I like fire. It is warm and bright and beautiful. Do you want to see my fire?"
Ben said, "No, we don't want to see your fire. Your fire is dangerous and hot and hurts. We don't like fire. We like flowers and trees and swings. We like to play and laugh and hug. We don't want to play with you. You are a dragon and we are not."
The dragon said, "But I want to play with you. You are brave and curious and have swords and shields. You are fun and interesting and have friends and games. I want to be your friend and play your games. Can I be your friend and play your games?"
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for the dragon. He was lonely and bored. He wanted to be their friend and play their games. Maybe he was not so scary and mean. Maybe he was just different and misunderstood. Maybe they could be his friends and play his games.
Lily said, "Okay, dragon, you can be our friend and play our games. But you have to be nice and gentle and not breathe fire. You have to be careful and quiet and not hurt us. You have to promise, promise, promise!"
The dragon nodded. He said, "I promise, promise, promise! I will be nice and gentle and not breathe fire. I will be careful and quiet and not hurt you. I will be your friend and play your games. Thank you, thank you, thank you!"
Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "You're welcome, welcome, welcome! Come on, let's go and play!"
They took the dragon's hand and they walked out of the cave. They were happy and excited. They had a new friend and a new game. They were successful and proud. They had found the dragon and made him their friend. They had kept their promises and had fun. They were the best knights and princesses in the park.

Timmy played with the car, but he was not careful. He broke the car. Everyone at the event was sad. The car was not useful anymore. The event was not fun anymore.
The moral of the story is to always be careful with things that are not yours. If you break something, it might not be useful anymore and make others sad.

Lila was a shy girl who did not like to talk to new people. She liked to play with her dolls and read her books in her room. She did not like to go to the doctor, because he was a new person and he had a big needle.
One day, Lila had a bad cough and a fever. Her mom said she had to go to the doctor, because he could make her feel better. Lila was scared and did not want to go. She cried and hid under her bed.
Her mom tried to calm her down and said, "Lila, the doctor is a nice man who wants to help you. He will not hurt you, he will just check your throat and give you a pill. The pill will make your cough go away and your fever go down. You can take the pill with some juice or water. It will not taste bad, I promise."
Lila did not believe her mom and said, "No, no, no! I don't want to go! I don't want the pill! I don't want the needle!"
Her mom sighed and said, "Lila, you have to be brave and trust me. The doctor and the pill are good for you. If you don't go, you will feel worse and worse. You will not be able to play with your dolls or read your books. You will miss your friends at school. You will make me worry. Please, Lila, let's go."
Lila looked at her mom and saw that she was sad and worried. She felt sorry for making her mom feel that way. She also felt tired and sick. She did not want to feel worse and worse. She wanted to feel better and play again. She decided to be brave and trust her mom.
She came out from under her bed and said, "Okay, mom, I will go. But I am still scared."
Her mom smiled and hugged her and said, "I am proud of you, Lila. You are a brave girl. I will be with you all the time. Don't be scared, everything will be okay."
They went to the doctor and he was a nice man who smiled and talked to Lila. He checked her throat and said she had a sore throat. He gave her a pill and said it was a magic pill that would make her cough go away and her fever go down. He said she could take it with some juice or water. He did not use the needle, he said he did not need it.
Lila was still shy, but she was also curious. She grabbed the pill and looked at it. It was small and white and round. She asked, "What is this pill made of?"
The doctor said, "It is made of sugar and medicine and love. Sugar to make it sweet, medicine to make you well, and love to make you happy."
Lila smiled and said, "Thank you, doctor. You are a nice man."
She took the pill with some juice and swallowed it. It did not taste bad, it tasted sweet. She felt a warm feeling in her chest and throat. She felt better and happier.
She said to her mom, "Mom, I am sorry I was scared and cried. I was wrong. The doctor and the pill are good for me. I love you, mom."
Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. You are a good girl. You learned a lesson today. Sometimes we have to do things that we don't like, but they are good for us. Sometimes we have to trust people who want to help us, even if they are new. Sometimes we have to be brave and face our fears, and we will find out that they are not so bad. Do you understand, Lila?"
Lila nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I will try to be brave and trust people more. I will not be so shy anymore."
Her mom said, "That's wonderful, Lila. I am happy for you. Now let's go home and rest. Tomorrow you will feel much better and you can play with your dolls and read your books again."
Lila said, "Yes, mom, let's go home. And thank you, doctor, for the magic pill."
The doctor said, "You're welcome, Lila. You are a smart and sweet girl. Take care and get well soon."
They said goodbye and left. Lila was happy and proud. She had a good day. She learned a lot. She made a new friend. She was brave. She was good.

"Can we feed the ducks?" Anna asked her mom.
"Yes, but be careful. Don't go too close to the water," her mom said.
Tom and Anna took some bread from their moms. They broke the bread into small pieces. They threw the pieces to the ducks. The ducks came and ate the bread. They quacked and splashed.
Tom and Anna laughed. They wanted to see the fish. They walked along the edge of the lake. They looked into the water. They saw some fish swimming.
"Look, Anna, a red fish!" Tom said.
"Wow, it's pretty!" Anna said.
Tom wanted to touch the fish. He leaned over the water. He reached out his hand. But he lost his balance. He fell into the lake. Splash!
Anna screamed. Tom's mom and Anna's mom ran to the lake. They saw Tom in the water. He was wet and scared. He cried.
"Tom, Tom, are you okay?" his mom asked. She pulled him out of the lake. She hugged him.
"I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry," Tom said. He shivered.
"It's okay, Tom, it's okay. You're safe now," his mom said. She wrapped him in a towel.
Anna felt sorry for Tom. She walked to him. She gave him a hug.
"I'm sorry, Tom, I'm sorry," Anna said.
"It's okay, Anna, it's okay. You're my friend," Tom said. He smiled.
They both sighed. They were glad they were okay. They learned a lesson. They would not go too close to the water again. They would be careful. They would still play with the ducks and the fish. But from a distance.

You should cut them off!" Lily was scared and said, "No, don't touch my bunny! I love its ears. They are soft and warm." But Ben did not mind Lily. He grabbed her bunny and ran away. He found a pair of scissors and started to cut one of the ears.
Lily heard her bunny cry and ran after Ben. She saw him with the scissors and the ear. She was very angry and sad. She snatched her bunny back and hugged it. She said, "You are mean, Ben! Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She said, "It's not funny to joke like that. You should mind other people's feelings and things. You should be kind and gentle. The moral of the story is: You should mind other people's feelings and things. You should be kind and gentle. You should not hurt or tease others. You should say sorry and make up when you do something wrong. You should be friends and help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a raven who liked to hop. Every day, he'd hop from tree to tree, from one side of the forest to the other.
One day, he saw a group of strange birds, who didn't hop. Curious, he flew over and spoke to them.
“What are you doing?” the raven asked.
“We’re walking, this is the normal way to move,” the birds replied.
So the raven joined them, walking alongside them, but he found it difficult and difficult to keep up.
Finally, he stopped and spoke again. “I think I like hopping better,” he said.
The birds laughed. “But hopping isn’t normal!” they said.
The raven smiled and said, “Maybe not, but just because it isn’t normal, doesn’t mean it isn’t right. We should all find our own way to do things, even if it’s different to what everyone else does.”
And so the raven returned to hopping happily through the forest, knowing that it was ok to be different.
The moral of the story is that it is ok to be different and we should be brave enough to choose our own paths, even if they go against the norm.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But sometimes they got bored and wanted to try something new.
One day, they saw a big gate at the end of the park. It was closed and had a sign that said "Keep Out". Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to see what was behind the gate. They looked around and saw no one was watching. They decided to sneak in and explore.
They pushed the gate open and walked inside. They saw a lot of trees and flowers and animals. They felt like they were in a fairy tale. They ran and laughed and chased each other. They forgot about the time and the sign and the gate.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It was coming towards them. It was carrying a lot of dirt and rocks. It was going to dump them on the ground. Lily and Tom were scared. They tried to run away, but they did not know where to go. They were lost.
They saw a small hut in the distance. They thought maybe someone could help them. They ran towards the hut and knocked on the door. A kind old man opened the door. He saw the children and smiled.
"Hello, little ones. What are you doing here?" he asked.
"Please, help us. We are in trouble. There is a big truck that wants to disappear us. We don't know how to get out of here. We are sorry we came in. We were just curious. Please, don't be mad at us." Lily and Tom said.
The old man was not mad. He was kind. He understood the children. He said, "Don't worry, I will help you. Come inside and stay with me. I will show you the way out when the truck is gone. But you have to be quiet and listen to me. Do you promise?"
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "We promise. Thank you, sir. You are very nice."
The old man took them inside and gave them some cookies and milk. He told them stories and jokes. He made them feel safe and happy. He waited until the truck was gone. Then he took them by the hand and led them to the gate. He opened the gate and said, "There you go. You can go back to the park now. But remember, never go inside the gate again. It is dangerous and forbidden. You are lucky I found you. Next time, you might not be so lucky. Do you understand?"
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "We understand. We are sorry we disobeyed the sign. We learned our lesson. We will never go inside the gate again. We will stay in the park and play safely. Thank you, sir. You are very wise."
The old man smiled and said, "You are welcome, little ones. Now, go and have fun. But be careful and respectful. And don't forget to tell your parents where you are. Goodbye."
Lily and Tom hugged the old man and said, "Goodbye, sir. We will do as you say. We will tell our parents everything. We are grateful to you. You are our hero."
They ran back to the park and found their parents. They told them the truth and apologized. Their parents were angry and worried, but also relieved and proud. They hugged and kissed them and said, "We love you, Lily and Tom. We are glad you are safe and honest. But don't ever do that again. It was very dangerous and wrong. You could have been hurt or lost. You have to follow the rules and listen to the signs. They are there for your protection and good. Do you understand?"
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "We understand, Mom and Dad. We are sorry we scared you. We love you too. We will follow the rules and listen to the signs. We will be good and smart. We will never forget what the old man taught us. He was very kind and wise. He saved us from the big truck. He was our hero."
The end.

The vehicle did not like the fight. It felt sad and hurt by the twins. It tried to tell them to stop, but they did not hear it. It decided to teach them a lesson. It started to move by itself, and drove away from the twins. It went out of the door, and into the street.
Lily and Max were shocked. They ran after the vehicle, but they could not catch it. They saw it go far away, and disappear. They felt sorry and scared. They cried and hugged each other. "We were bad," said Lily. "We spoiled our vehicle," said Max. "We want it back," they said together.
Their mom came and comforted them. She said, "I'm sorry you lost your vehicle, but you learned a valuable lesson. You should always share and be kind to each other, and to your toys. Maybe your grandpa can fix your vehicle, or make you a new one. But you have to promise to be good and grateful."
Lily and Max nodded and said, "We promise, mom. We love you, and we love each other, and we love our vehicle. We hope it comes back to us." They hugged their mom, and hoped that their unusual vehicle would forgive them.

Suddenly, from out of the trees, a spirit appeared. It was a fairy, with wings as big as a butterfly's. The spirit said, "Ahh, the delicious berry was my magic berry. It shrinks those who eat it! Don't worry, though, because if you trust me I will take you on a magical journey."
Jane was very scared, but she trusted the spirit and said, "OK, I will go with you". The fairy smiled and took Jane on an amazing journey, full of beautiful sights and wonderful adventures.
When the journey was over, the fairy brought Jane back to the same spot in the forest. She was back to her usual size. She thanked the spirit, who smiled at Jane and said, "Remember to trust your instincts, and great things will happen." Jane smiled back, and returned home.

"I'm doing it, I'm doing it!" he shouted.
He stopped swinging and noticed a soccer game was happening nearby. He wanted to join in.
“Can I play?” he asked.
The other players nodded and welcomed Mick to join the game. He ran and tried to kick the ball but missed it.
“I thought I could get the score,” said Mick sadly.
Everyone laughed and said, “It’s ok, Mick. You can keep trying. Just don’t get too bitter if you don’t succeed the first time around.”
Mick smiled and nodded. He kept trying and eventually he scored and everyone cheered.

Lily and Max were playing in the park with their toy lasers. They liked to pretend they were space heroes, fighting bad aliens. They made loud noises and ran around the slides and swings.
But then, the sky became gloomy. Dark clouds covered the sun, and the wind blew hard. Lily and Max felt cold and scared. They heard thunder and saw lightning. They wanted to go home.
"Come on, Max, let's go!" Lily said. "It's going to rain soon!"
But Max did not want to leave. He liked his laser too much. He said, "No, Lily, I want to play more. My laser is so cool. Look, it can make red lights!"
Lily tried to pull Max by the hand, but he shook her off. He said, "Go away, Lily, you are no fun. I don't need you. I have my laser."
Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "Fine, Max, be that way. I'm going home. Bye!"
She ran to the gate, where their mom was waiting. She told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily, Max will learn his lesson soon. Come on, let's go home and prepare some hot chocolate."
They got in the car and drove away. Max was left alone in the park. He played with his laser for a while, but then he got bored. He looked around and saw no one. He felt lonely and sorry. He wished he had gone with Lily and his mom.
He decided to go home, too. He put his laser in his pocket and ran to the gate. But he was too late. The rain started to fall. It was heavy and cold. Max got wet and shivered. He had no umbrella or coat. He had no one to help him.
He cried and said, "Lily, mom, where are you? I'm sorry, I was wrong. I want to go home. Please, come back!"
But no one heard him. He had to wait in the rain until his dad came to pick him up. His dad was angry and worried. He scolded Max and said, "Max, what were you thinking? You should have listened to Lily and your mom. They were trying to protect you. You were selfish and foolish. You could have gotten sick or hurt. You are lucky I found you."
Max felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, dad, I know I was bad. I won't do it again. I love Lily and mom. I love you, too. Can you forgive me?"
His dad hugged him and said, "Of course, I forgive you, Max. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be kind and respectful to your sister and your mom. You have to be careful and responsible with your toys. You have to be grateful and happy with what you have. Do you understand?"
Max nodded and said, "Yes, dad, I understand. Thank you, dad. I will do better next time."
They got in the car and drove home. Max hoped Lily and his mom would forgive him, too. He learned that playing with lasers was not as important as playing with his family. He learned that being gloomy was not as fun as being sunny. He learned that being prepared was better than being sorry.

"Look, we tidied our blocks. The floor is clean. The box is full. We are good children." Ben says.
"Yes, we are. We are good and tidy. We are ready for bed. Good night, Ben. Good night, tower. Good night, sun. Good night, west." Lily says.
