"No, we can't," Ben said. "These are not our coppers. They belong to someone else. We have to put them back in the sack."
"But they are so pretty and shiny," Sam said. "Can we keep just one? Please?"
Ben thought for a moment. He saw one copper that was different from the others. It had a picture of a bird on it. He had never seen a copper like that before. It was original.
"Okay, we can keep one," Ben said. "But only one. And we have to hide it well. How about this one? It has a bird on it. Do you like it?"
Sam nodded. He liked the bird copper. He took it and put it in his pocket. He felt happy.
They closed the sack and put it back in the garage. They did not know that the sack was stolen from a bank. They did not know that the bird copper was very rare and valuable. They did not know that someone was looking for it. They only knew that they had a secret treasure.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting?"
"We both want the car!" Ben and Anna say.
Mom shakes her head. "That is not nice. You have to share. Sharing is good. Sharing makes friends happy. Do you want to be happy?"
Ben and Anna nod. They want to be happy.
"Then you have to take turns. You can play with the car for a little while, and then give it to the other. That is fair. That is kind. Do you understand?"
Ben and Anna nod. They understand.
"OK, then. Who wants to go first?" Mom asks.
Ben and Anna look at each other. They smile.
"You can go first, Anna," Ben says.
"Thank you, Ben. You can go next," Anna says.
They give each other a hug. They share the car. They take turns. They are happy. They are friends.
Mom smiles. She is proud of them. She says, "Well done, Anna and Ben. You have learned a very important lesson. Sharing is caring. And caring is unique."

Fleas are tiny bugs that bite and itch. They live in Benny's fur and make him scratch and whine. Benny tried to get rid of them by rolling on the grass and shaking his head, but they did not go away. He wished his human would provide him with something to make them stop.
One day, a new human came to visit. He had a bag and a smile. He said hello to Benny and petted him. Benny liked the new human. He smelled good and was gentle. The new human took out a bottle from his bag and said, "This is a brilliant flea spray. It will kill all the fleas on your dog and make him feel better. Can I use it on him?"
Benny's human nodded and said, "Sure, go ahead. I've been meaning to get something for him, but I've been busy. Thank you for helping him."
The new human sprayed the bottle all over Benny's fur. Benny felt a cold and wet sensation. He did not like it. He tried to run away, but the new human held him. He said, "Don't worry, it will be over soon. It's for your own good."
Benny started to feel funny. He felt dizzy and weak. He could not breathe. He looked at his human with scared eyes. He wanted to say, "Help me, something is wrong." But he could not make a sound. He fell to the ground and did not move.
The new human looked at Benny and said, "Oops, I guess I used the wrong bottle. This is not flea spray, this is poison. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hurt him. I mixed them up."
Benny's human screamed and cried. He ran to Benny and hugged him. He said, "No, no, no, this can't be happening. Benny, please wake up. Please don't die. You're my best friend. I love you."
But Benny did not wake up. He did not hear his human. He did not feel anything. He was gone. The fleas were gone too. But so was Benny. The end.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make up stories with their dolls and cars. Lily had a pink doll that she called Rosie, and Ben had a blue car that he called Zoom. They pretended that Rosie and Zoom were friends who went on adventures.
One day, they decided to play a game where Rosie and Zoom had to find a treasure. They used a map that Lily drew with crayons. The map showed a big X where the treasure was. They followed the map around the room, looking for clues.
"Look, Rosie, there is a clue!" Ben said, pointing to a piece of paper under the sofa. He reached for it, but it was too far. He twisted his arm, trying to grab it, but he could not. He felt a pain in his elbow. He cried out loud.
"Ben, are you okay?" Lily asked, dropping her doll and running to him. She saw his face was red and wet with tears. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. It was just a game. You don't have to twist your arm. Let me see."
She looked at his elbow and saw a bruise. She said, "It's okay, Ben. It's not bad. It will go away soon. Do you want some ice?"
Ben nodded, still sniffling. Lily said, "Come on, let's go to the kitchen. Mommy will give us some ice and some cocoa. Cocoa makes everything better."
They held hands and walked to the kitchen. Mommy was there, making cookies. She saw them and smiled. She said, "Hello, my sweeties. What are you doing?"
"We were playing a game, Mommy, but Ben hurt his elbow. He twisted it under the sofa. Can we have some ice and some cocoa, please?" Lily said.
"Of course, my darlings. Here, Ben, put this ice on your elbow. It will make it feel better. And here, Lily, help me pour some cocoa for you and Ben. Be careful, it's hot." Mommy said.
She gave them each a mug of cocoa and a cookie. She said, "You are such good children. I love you very much. Now, tell me about your game. What treasure were you looking for?"
Lily and Ben smiled. They forgot about the pain and the clue. They told Mommy about their game and their map. They said, "The treasure was a big hug from you, Mommy."
Mommy laughed and hugged them tight. She said, "That's the best treasure ever. You are my treasure, Lily and Ben."

Tom was a boy who liked to take things. He took toys from his friends, books from his teacher, and candy from his mom. He did not care if they were sad or angry. He only wanted to have more things.
One day, he saw a bald man walking on the street. The bald man had a shiny ring on his finger. Tom thought the ring was very pretty. He wanted to take it for himself. He ran after the bald man and tried to grab his hand.
But the bald man was not a normal man. He was a wizard. He had a lot of wisdom and magic. He knew what Tom was trying to do. He did not like it. He turned around and looked at Tom with his bright eyes.
He said, "You are a greedy and rude boy. You do not deserve to have anything. You need to learn a lesson. I will take something from you. I will take your hair!"
He waved his hand and said a strange word. Tom felt a tingling on his head. He touched his hair and screamed. It was all gone. He was bald like the wizard.
The wizard laughed and said, "Now you know how it feels to lose something. Maybe you will be more kind and respectful from now on. Goodbye, bald boy!"
He walked away with his ring, leaving Tom crying on the street. Tom was very sorry and ashamed. He wished he had not tried to take the ring. He wished he had more wisdom and less greed. But it was too late. He had to live with his bald head. He had a bad ending.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily screamed. They tried to run away, but the monster was faster. It caught them and bit them. It destroyed them.
Mom heard the screams and came to the yard. She saw the door open and the monster. She saw Tom and Lily on the ground. She was very sad and angry. She wished Tom and Lily had listened to her. She wished they had not opened the door.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run on the grass. They saw many animals, like birds, dogs and squirrels. They were having fun.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a large vehicle. It was red and shiny, and it had a long ladder and a hose. It was a fire truck. It was going very fast, and it had a siren that went "wee-woo-wee-woo". Lily and Sam were scared. They did not like the noise. They ran to their mom and hugged her.
"Mom, what is that?" Lily asked.
"That is a fire truck, sweetie. It is a vehicle that helps people when there is a fire. The firefighters drive it and use the ladder and the hose to put out the fire. They are very brave and kind," mom explained.
"Why does it make that noise?" Sam asked.
"It makes that noise to let other vehicles and people know that it is coming. It is a way of saying 'please move out of the way, we have an emergency'. It is very important that we listen and follow the noise, so we do not get in the way of the fire truck," mom said.
"Oh, I see. Thank you, mom. Can we wave to the firefighters?" Lily asked.
"Of course, you can. They will appreciate it. They work very hard to keep us safe," mom said.
Lily and Sam smiled. They were not scared anymore. They understood what the fire truck was and why it made that noise. They waved to the firefighters as they passed by. The firefighters waved back and smiled. They were happy to see the children. Lily and Sam felt proud and happy. They learned something new today. They went back to playing in the park with their mom. They had a great day.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and make mud pies. They found many things in the earth, like stones, worms and shells.
One day, they saw something shiny in the earth. They dug it out and saw that it was a toy car. But the car was broken. One wheel was missing and the paint was scratched.
"Look, Lily, a car!" Tom said.
"But it is broken, Tom. We can't play with it," Lily said.
"Maybe we can repair it, Lily. We can find a new wheel and some paint," Tom said.
They looked around the garden for something to use as a wheel. They tried a bottle cap, a button and a cookie, but none of them fit. Then they saw a nut on the ground. It was round and had a hole in the middle.
"Look, Lily, a nut! Maybe this can be the wheel," Tom said.
They put the nut on the car and it fit. The car had four wheels now, but it still looked old and dirty.
"We need some paint, Tom. What color do you like?" Lily said.
"I like red, Lily. Red is fast and bright," Tom said.
They looked around the garden for something red. They saw some flowers, some berries and some tomatoes, but none of them were good for painting. Then they saw a can of paint in the shed. It was red and had a brush inside.
"Look, Lily, paint! Maybe this can make the car look new," Tom said.
They opened the can and dipped the brush in the paint. They painted the car with red strokes, covering the scratches and the dirt. The car looked shiny and new.
"Look, Lily, we repaired the car! It is not broken anymore," Tom said.
"It is beautiful, Tom. We did a good job," Lily said.
They smiled and hugged each other. They put the car on the ground and pushed it. The car rolled and beeped. Tom and Lily laughed and played with the car. They were happy.

She does not like green spots. She thinks they are yucky. She shakes her head. She disagrees with Tom. She does not want the strawberry.
Tom does not understand. He thinks the green spot is okay. He tries to make Lily take the strawberry. He says it is good. He pushes it to her mouth. Lily does not like that. She pushes Tom away. She says it is bad. She runs to the other side of the plant. She looks for a strawberry without a green spot.
Tom is angry. He thinks Lily is silly. He follows her. He wants to show her that all the strawberries are good. He picks another one. He does not see the green spot on it. He bites it. It is sour and bitter. He makes a face. He spits it out. He feels something on his tongue. He looks at the strawberry. He sees a green worm on it. He screams. He drops the strawberry.
Lily hears Tom scream. She turns around. She sees the green worm on the ground. She feels sorry for Tom. She runs to him. She hugs him. She says she is sorry. She says she will share her strawberry with him. She picks a big red strawberry without a green spot. She breaks it in half. She gives one half to Tom. Tom smiles. He says thank you. He says he is sorry too. He says he will not disagree with Lily again. They eat the strawberry. It is sweet and juicy. They are happy. They pick more strawberries. They do not see any more green worms. They are careful. They have fun.

They were the best of friends ever since. Sandy visits the diamond in the forest everyday and they have great adventures together.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a farm. They liked to play with the animals, but they did not like to help with the chores. One day, their father asked them to feed the goat. Ben and Sam did not want to do it. They said, "The goat is not fun. The goat is not cute. The goat is not useful. Why do we have to feed the goat?"
Their father was angry. He said, "The goat is very useful. The goat gives us milk and cheese. The goat eats the grass and weeds. The goat keeps us company. You should be kind to the goat and feed him every day. If you do not feed the goat, you will not get any milk or cheese or grass or company."
Ben and Sam did not listen. They ran away to play with the dog and the cat. They forgot about the goat. The goat was hungry and lonely. He started to yell. He yelled very loud. He yelled, "Baa! Baa! Baa!"
The father heard the goat. He went to see what was wrong. He saw that the goat had no food or water. He was very sad. He said, "Poor goat. You are so useful, but no one cares for you. I will feed you and give you water. I will pet you and talk to you. You are a good goat."
The goat was happy. He stopped yelling. He said, "Maa! Maa! Maa!" He licked the father's hand. He thanked him for his kindness.
Ben and Sam heard the goat and the father. They felt ashamed. They realized that they were wrong. They said, "We are sorry, father. We are sorry, goat. We were selfish and rude. We did not appreciate you. You are very useful and very nice. Can we help you feed the goat and give him water? Can we pet him and talk to him? Can we be his friends?"
The father smiled. He said, "Yes, you can. I am glad that you learned your lesson. The goat is a part of our family. We should treat him with respect and love. He will reward us with his gifts and his friendship. Come, let us feed the goat together."
Ben and Sam nodded. They followed their father. They fed the goat and gave him water. They petted him and talked to him. They became his friends. The goat was happy. He said, "Baa! Baa! Baa!" He gave them milk and cheese and grass and company. They all lived happily on the farm.
The moral of the story is: Be kind to animals. They are useful and friendly. They deserve our care and attention. They will make us happy and grateful.

Lily and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. Lily liked the elephants best, because they had long noses and big ears. Ben liked the monkeys best, because they jumped and played.
Then they came to the ostriches. Ostriches are big birds with long necks and legs. They cannot fly, but they can run very fast. One ostrich was very curious. It came close to the fence and looked at Lily and Ben.
"Hello, ostrich!" Lily said. "Do you want to be my friend?"
The ostrich nodded and made a funny sound. It stretched its neck and pecked at Lily's hat. Lily giggled and gave the ostrich her hat.
"Hey, that's my hat!" Ben said. "Give it back, ostrich!"
The ostrich shook its head and ran away with the hat. Ben chased after it, but he was too slow. The ostrich ran to a pond and jumped in. It splashed water everywhere and made the hat wet.
"Stop, stop, stop!" Ben shouted. "That's not nice, ostrich!"
The ostrich did not stop. It swam in the pond and played with the hat. It looked very happy and wet.
Lily and Ben ran to Mom and Dad. They told them what happened.
"Oh, no!" Mom said. "That's a naughty ostrich!"
"Don't worry, Ben," Dad said. "We'll get your hat back. Come on, let's talk to the zookeeper."
They went to the zookeeper and told him about the ostrich. The zookeeper smiled and said he would help. He went to the pond and called the ostrich. The ostrich came out of the water and gave the hat back. The hat was very wet and dirty.
"Thank you, zookeeper," Ben said. "But my hat is ruined!"
"I'm sorry, Ben," the zookeeper said. "The ostrich didn't mean to be bad. It just wanted to have fun. Here, I have a new hat for you. It has a picture of an ostrich on it. Do you like it?"
Ben looked at the new hat. It was dry and clean. It had a picture of an ostrich on it. It was a nice hat.
"Yes, I like it," Ben said. "Thank you, zookeeper!"
"You're welcome, Ben," the zookeeper said. "And you, ostrich, be good and don't take things that are not yours."
The ostrich nodded and made a funny sound. It looked sorry and sad.
Lily felt sorry for the ostrich too. She took off her hat and gave it to the ostrich.
"Here, ostrich," Lily said. "You can have my hat. It's a gift. Be my friend, okay?"
The ostrich nodded and made a happy sound. It put the hat on its head. It looked very funny and cute.
Lily and Ben laughed and hugged the ostrich. The ostrich hugged them back. They became friends.
Mom and Dad took a picture of them. They smiled and said it was a good day at the zoo.

Lila was a spoiled princess who had many toys and dresses. She liked to show off and make fun of other children who had less. One day, she went to a party with a new veil that sparkled like stars. She saw a girl named Sara who wore a plain dress and no veil. Lila laughed at Sara and said, "You look so ugly and poor. You can't come to my party. Go away!"
Sara felt very sad and ran away. She cried in a corner and wished she had a friend. Then, she saw a boy named Ben who was playing with a ball. He smiled at her and said, "Hi, I'm Ben. Do you want to play with me?" Sara nodded and wiped her tears. She and Ben had fun playing with the ball and talking.
Lila saw them and felt angry. She wanted to spoil their fun. She ran to them and snatched the ball from Ben. She said, "This is my ball now. You can't have it. You are both losers." She threw the ball over a fence and ran away.
Ben and Sara felt very mad and hurt. They wanted to get the ball back, but they couldn't. They looked at each other and decided to do something. They went to the fence and climbed over it. They found the ball in a garden full of flowers and butterflies. They also saw Lila's veil that had fallen off her head. It was torn and dirty from the thorns and mud.
Ben and Sara had an idea. They could take the veil and make Lila feel bad. They could tear it more and throw it away. They could make her cry and laugh at her. But then, they remembered how they felt when Lila was mean to them. They didn't want to be like her. They wanted to be kind and good.
They picked up the veil and cleaned it as best as they could. They went back to the party and looked for Lila. They found her crying and looking for her veil. She was afraid that her mother would scold her. She saw Ben and Sara and expected them to mock her. But instead, they gave her the veil and said, "We found your veil. We're sorry that it's torn and dirty. We hope you can fix it."
Lila was shocked and confused. She didn't understand why they were nice to her. She felt ashamed and sorry for what she had done. She said, "Thank you for giving me my veil. I'm sorry for being mean to you. I was wrong and selfish. Can you forgive me?"
Ben and Sara smiled and said, "Yes, we can forgive you. We all make mistakes, but we can learn from them. We can be friends if you want."
Lila nodded and said, "Yes, I want to be friends. I want to be better. I want to share and care. Can we play together?"
Ben and Sara agreed and invited Lila to join them. They played with the ball and the veil and had fun. They learned that being kind and forgiving is better than being spoiled and rude. They learned that friendship is more precious than things. They learned a valuable lesson that day.

The bee tells the flowers not to worry. She will protect them from Sara and Tom. She says they are good flowers and they deserve to live.

"I am delivering books to the library," the man said. "Books are things you can read and learn from. They have words and pictures and stories."
"Can we see the books?" Tim and Sue said.
"Sure, but be careful. Some of these books are very old and rare. They are written in different languages. Languages are the ways people talk and write. Some people speak English, like us, and some people speak other languages, like Spanish or Chinese or Arabic."
The man opened one of the boxes and showed Tim and Sue some of the books. They looked at the covers and the pages. They saw letters and symbols and colors they did not know. They thought the books were very interesting and pretty.
"Can we have one?" Tim and Sue said.
"No, you can't. These books are not for you. They are for the library. The library is a place where people can borrow books and read them and return them. You have to ask your mom or dad to take you to the library if you want to read these books."
"But we want one now," Tim and Sue said. They did not listen to the man. They grabbed one of the books and ran away. The book was very big and heavy. It was enormous.
The man shouted at them. "Hey, stop! That book is very valuable. It is one of a kind. It is written in a language that no one knows. It is a mystery. You can't take it. Give it back!"
But Tim and Sue did not stop. They ran to their house and slammed the door. They wanted to keep the book for themselves. They wanted to look at it and play with it and make up their own stories.
They opened the book and saw the strange words and pictures. They tried to read them, but they could not. They did not understand the language. They did not care. They thought the book was fun.
They turned the pages and ripped them. They drew on them and cut them. They made paper planes and hats and boats. They laughed and shouted and made a mess.
They did not know that the book was very old and fragile. They did not know that the book was very important and rare. They did not know that the book was very dangerous and cursed.
They did not know that the book had a spell on it. A spell that made anyone who damaged it pay a price. A price that was very high and terrible.
They did not know that the book was angry. Angry at them for ruining it. Angry at them for stealing it. Angry at them for not respecting it.
They did not know that the book was alive. Alive and waiting. Waiting for the right moment. The moment to deliver its revenge.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and pictures on the wall. One day, their mom gave them a new picture in a frame. It was a picture of a lion and a mouse. The frame was shiny and pretty.
"Look, Ben, a new picture!" Lily said. "It is so nice. I want to touch it."
"No, Lily, don't touch it!" Ben said. "Mom said we can only look, not touch. The frame can break and the picture can tear. Then mom will be sad and angry."
"But I want to touch it!" Lily said. "It is so soft and furry. I want to feel the lion and the mouse. They are friends, like us."
Lily reached out her hand and touched the picture. But she touched too hard and the frame fell off the wall. It hit the floor and broke into pieces. The picture also ripped in the middle. Lily and Ben were scared and sorry.
"Oh no, what have we done?" Ben said. "Mom will be so mad at us. We should have listened to her. She is smart and knows what is best."
"I'm sorry, Ben, I'm sorry, mom," Lily said. "I was wrong to touch the picture. I was curious and silly. I should have obeyed mom. She is smart and loves us."
They heard mom coming up the stairs. They ran to her and hugged her. They told her what happened and said they were sorry. Mom was not happy, but she was not mad either. She hugged them back and said she forgave them.
"I'm glad you told me the truth," mom said. "That shows you are brave and honest. But next time, please listen to me and don't touch things that are not yours. They can be damaged or dangerous. You can look and ask, but not touch. That shows you are smart and respectful."
Ben and Lily nodded and said they understood. They helped mom clean up the mess and fix the picture. They learned their lesson and never touched the picture again. They still liked to look at it and remember the story of the lion and the mouse. They also tried to be friends, like them.

One day, a little bear named Ben found a big basket of blueberries in the forest. He was very hungry and wanted to eat them all. He did not see a sign that said, "These blueberries belong to Mama Fox. Please do not touch."
Ben took the basket and ran to his cave. He locked the door with a big key. He said to himself, "These are my blueberries. I will not share them with anyone."
Soon, he heard a knock on the door. It was Mama Fox. She said, "Ben, please open the door. I need my blueberries. I picked them for my cubs. They are very hungry and sick."
Ben did not care. He said, "No, these are my blueberries. Go away."
Mama Fox was sad and angry. She said, "Ben, you are very greedy and mean. You should be humble and kind. Sharing is caring. If you do not open the door, I will call the big bad wolf. He will huff and puff and blow your door down."
Ben was scared. He did not want the big bad wolf to come. He said, "Please, do not call the big bad wolf. I am sorry. I will open the door and give you your blueberries."
Ben unlocked the door and gave the basket to Mama Fox. Mama Fox smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good bear. I forgive you. Here, you can have some blueberries too. They are more tasty when you share them with friends."
Ben felt happy and ashamed. He said, "Thank you, Mama Fox. You are a good fox. I am sorry for being greedy and mean. I learned my lesson. I will be humble and kind. Sharing is caring."
Ben and Mama Fox ate some blueberries together. They became friends. They lived happily in the forest. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many green leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.
"Come on, Lily, let's go up the tree!" Tom said.
"OK, Tom, but be careful. Don't fall down," Lily said.
They climbed the tree and found a big branch to sit on. They looked around and saw many things. They saw birds, flowers, clouds, and cars. They also saw a monkey.
"Look, Lily, a monkey!" Tom said.
"Wow, a monkey! Where did it come from?" Lily said.
The monkey was brown and furry. It had a long tail and big ears. It was holding a yellow fruit. It looked at Lily and Tom and smiled.
"Hello, monkey. What are you doing here?" Tom said.
The monkey did not answer. It peeled the fruit and took a bite. It made a funny face and spat out the fruit.
"Yuck, sour!" the monkey said.
Lily and Tom laughed. They wanted to try the fruit too. They asked the monkey to share.
"Please, monkey, can we have some of your fruit?" Lily said.
The monkey nodded and threw the fruit to Lily and Tom. They caught the fruit and peeled it. They took a bite and made the same funny face as the monkey.
"Yuck, sour!" they said.
They spat out the fruit and threw it away. They did not like the fruit. They liked the monkey.
"Thank you, monkey, for sharing your fruit. But we don't like it. It is too sour," Tom said.
The monkey shrugged and jumped to another branch. It found another fruit and ate it. It was sweet and juicy.
"Mmm, sweet!" the monkey said.
Lily and Tom watched the monkey and smiled. They forgot about the sour fruit. They were happy to see the monkey. They wanted to play with the monkey.
"Monkey, monkey, come back. Let's play together," Lily said.
The monkey looked at Lily and Tom and nodded. It jumped back to their branch and joined them. They played in the tree and had fun. They did not want to leave the tree. They forgot about everything else. They only remembered the monkey.

One day, they saw a jolly bird on a tree. It was singing a happy song and had bright feathers. Tim and Lily wanted to say hello to the bird. They tried to call it, but it did not come down.
"I have an idea," said Tim. "Let's throw a brick to the bird. Maybe it will catch it and play with us."
"No, no, no," said Lily. "That is not a good idea. The brick is too heavy and hard. It will hurt the bird and make it sad. We should not throw bricks at birds. We should be kind to them."
But Tim did not listen to Lily. He picked up a brick and threw it to the bird. He missed the bird, but he hit the tree. The tree shook and a lot of leaves and nuts fell down. One of the nuts hit Tim on the head. It made a loud sound and Tim felt a big pain.
"Ow, ow, ow," cried Tim. "That hurt a lot. Why did the nut hit me?"
Lily ran to Tim and hugged him. She tried to make him feel better. She said, "I'm sorry, Tim. The nut hit you because you threw the brick. The tree did not like that. You should not throw bricks at trees either. You should be careful and gentle with them."
Tim nodded and said, "You are right, Lily. I was silly and mean. I'm sorry, bird. I'm sorry, tree. I will not throw bricks at you again. I will be nice to you."
The bird heard Tim and Lily. It forgave them and sang another song. It was a song of friendship and peace. Tim and Lily smiled and clapped. They learned a lesson and had a happy day.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Jack and Jake. They both wanted to play together at the playground, but Jack wanted to play on the swings while Jake wanted to go down the slide. 
Jack said to Jake, "Let's both go down the slide!"
But Jake shook his head and said, "No, I want to go down the slide, and you want to go on the swings. Let's test it out, and see who is right!"
Jack was getting angry and said, "No, it's not fair! I don't want to test it, because then I won't get what I want."
Then a wise old man, who was sitting on a nearby desk, spoke to them. He said, "When you test something and you don't get what you want, it doesn't mean it's not fair. Sometimes it's just the way things are. Don't be angry, be kind to each other and you will have lots of fun."
Jack and Jake listened to the old man and decided to go down the slide together. They both had lots of fun and learnt a valuable lesson - it's better to be kind than to be angry.

"What was that?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. It was not a ball. It was something else." Lily said.
They looked at the ball. It was not a ball anymore. It was a broken, black thing. It had wires and metal inside.
"Maybe it was a toy. Maybe it had a battery." Tom said.
"Maybe. But it was not a good toy. It was a bad toy. It hurt us." Lily said.
They dropped the ball. They ran to their mom. They told her what happened.
"Are you okay?" Mom asked.
"Yes, we are okay. But the ball was not okay. It was a bad ball. It squeezed and popped and made sparks." Tom said.
Mom hugged them. She was glad they were okay.
"That was not a ball. That was a firework. It was dangerous. You should not play with it. You should only play with safe toys." Mom said.
"Sorry, Mom. We did not know. We will not play with it again." Lily said.
Mom threw away the firework. She gave them a real ball. A soft, blue ball. They played with it. They had fun. They did not squeeze it. They did not see sparks. They were happy.

Lily was a curious girl who liked to explore the kitchen. One day, she saw a green thing on the table that looked like a ball. She picked it up and felt its smooth skin. She wondered what was inside.
She asked her mom, "What is this, mom?"
Her mom smiled and said, "That is an avocado, Lily. It is a fruit that you can eat. But you have to cut it open first."
Lily wanted to see what was inside the avocado. She looked for something to cut it with. She saw a knife on the counter. She reached for it, but her mom stopped her.
"No, no, Lily. You can't use the knife. It is sharp and dangerous. You can hurt yourself. Give it to me, please."
Lily was not happy. She wanted to cut the avocado herself. She did not want to give the knife to her mom. She held it tight and said, "No, mom. I want to cut it. I want to see."
Her mom was worried and firm. She said, "Lily, you have to listen to me. The knife is not a toy. You can rub the avocado with your hands, but you can't cut it. Give me the knife, now."
Lily did not want to listen. She tried to pull the knife away from her mom. But her mom was stronger and took the knife from her. Lily started to cry. She felt angry and sad.
Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I know you are curious, but you have to be careful. The knife can hurt you and make you bleed. I don't want you to get hurt. I love you."
Lily calmed down and said, "I love you too, mom. But I still want to see the avocado."
Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, Lily. I will show you the avocado. But you have to promise me to never touch the knife again, okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I promise."
Her mom cut the avocado in half and showed Lily the soft flesh and the big seed inside. Lily was amazed. She rubbed the avocado with her fingers and tasted it. She liked it. She said, "Mmm, the avocado is yummy. Thank you, mom."
Her mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you like it. But remember, be careful and listen to me, okay?"
Lily said, "Okay, mom. I will."

One day, Tim was drawing a big tree. He saw his friend, Sam, come near. Tim did not want Sam to use his pencil. So, he tried to hide it. He put the pencil in a box and gave it a big shake.
Suddenly, the pencil started to shake too. The box opened, and the pencil turned into a magic wand! Tim was so surprised. The wand could draw things that came to life. Tim drew a big cake, and it became real. Sam saw this and was very happy.
Tim thought about it and decided to share the magic wand with Sam. They both drew many fun things together. Tim was not selfish anymore. Sharing made both Tim and Sam very happy.

"No, you have to do it my way. I'm the boss," Lily said.
She took the passenger car from Ben and gave him the coal car. Ben was sad and angry. He didn't like to play with Lily when she was bossy.

"Ben, help me lift the train to the chimney. It will be fun to see it go up and down," she said.
"But that's dangerous. The chimney is hot and dirty. And we might lose the train," Ben said.
"No, it will be fine. Trust me. I'm the boss," Lily said.
She grabbed the train and tried to put it in the chimney. But the train was too big and heavy. It got stuck in the chimney and made a loud noise. Smoke came out of the chimney and filled the room. Lily and Ben coughed and cried. Their mom came running and saw what happened.
"Lily, Ben, what did you do? You could have started a fire. And you ruined your toy train. How could you be so careless?" she said.
She took them out of the room and scolded them. She told them to never play with the chimney again. And she told Lily to stop being so bossy and to listen to Ben sometimes. Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They learned their lesson. They hugged each other and said sorry. They decided to play with their toy train nicely and share it. They also promised to be more careful and respectful. They realized that being bossy is not fun and that playing together is better.

Lily and Ben were very happy today. They moved to a new house with Mom and Dad. They had many boxes to unpack, but they also wanted to play.
"Can we unpack our toys first?" Lily asked Mom.
"Yes, you can," Mom said. "But only one box each. Then you have to help me with the other things."
Lily and Ben ran to their room and picked one box each. Lily opened her box and found her doll, her tea set, and her dress-up clothes. Ben opened his box and found his cars, his train, and his superhero cape.
"Let's play together!" Lily said. She put her doll on the tea table and poured some pretend tea. "Do you want some tea, Ben?"
"No, thank you," Ben said. He put his cars on the floor and made zooming noises. "I want to race my cars!"
Lily frowned. She wanted Ben to play with her. She grabbed one of his cars and put it on the tea table. "This is your car, Ben. It wants some tea too."
Ben got angry. He snatched his car back and pushed Lily's doll off the table. "No, it doesn't! This is my car, Lily. It doesn't like tea. It likes to go fast!"
Lily cried. She picked up her doll and hugged it. "You're mean, Ben. You ruined my tea party!"
Mom heard the noise and came to their room. She saw Lily crying and Ben scowling. She sighed and sat down with them.
"What's going on here?" Mom asked.
"Lily took my car and put it on her tea table. She said it wanted tea, but it didn't. It wanted to race!" Ben said.
"Ben pushed my doll and made it fall. He said his car didn't like tea, but it did. It wanted to join my tea party!" Lily said.
Mom smiled and hugged them both. "I see. You both have different ways of playing, and that's okay. But you also have to respect each other's toys and feelings. How about you take turns playing with each other's toys and games? Maybe you can find something fun that you both like."
Lily and Ben looked at each other and nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged. Then they decided to play with the train and the dress-up clothes. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the other boxes. Mom was happy to see them get along and helped them unpack later.

Lily liked hide and seek. She said, "Okay, mom. You count and I hide."
Her mom said, "All right, Lily. I will count to ten and then I will find you. One, two, three..."

Her mom looked around the room. She saw the cake, the balloons, the games, and the box. She had a twinkle in her eye. She knew where Lily was. She walked to the box and said, "Hmm, I wonder what's in this box. Maybe it's something for Lily's party. Maybe it's something she will like."

Lily popped out of the box and said, "Surprise!"

Her mom said, "Your friends gave them to you. They felt bad that they could not come to your party, so they sent you these gifts. They wanted to make you happy. They love you, Lily. And so do I."
Lily felt very happy. She said, "I love you too, mom. And I love my friends. This is the best party ever."

Tim and Sam were playing knights in the park. They had sticks for swords and cardboard for shields. They liked to pretend they were brave and strong.
"Let's fight the dragon!" Tim said. He pointed to a big rock that looked like a dragon's head. "You go first, Sam. I'll help you."
Sam nodded and ran towards the rock. He lifted his stick and shouted, "Take that, dragon!" He hit the rock hard with his stick. But the stick was old and weak. It snapped in two. Sam gasped and dropped the broken stick.
"Oh no!" Tim said. He ran to Sam and gave him his stick. "Here, use mine. It's stronger. I'll use your shield."
Sam took Tim's stick and thanked him. He tried to hit the rock again. But the rock was too hard and the stick bounced off. The stick hit Sam's shield and made a loud noise. The noise scared a bird that was hiding behind the rock. The bird flew out and splashed water on Sam and Tim. The water came from a puddle that the bird was drinking from.
Sam and Tim were wet and cold. They dropped their stick and shield and ran away from the rock. They laughed and shivered. They looked like wet knights.
"That was a silly dragon," Sam said.
"Yes, it was," Tim said. "But we had fun, right?"
"Right," Sam said. "Let's go home and get dry."
They held hands and walked home. They were still friends and still knights.

The kitten looked around and noticed its own paw. It remembered that by tracing its paw steps, it would eventually get back home. With this in mind, the kitten felt much less worried.
The kitten eventually got back home safely. Through this experience, the kitten learned a valuable lesson - that it can always find its way home by doing the same things it did to get there in the first place.

Jill hopped on her bike and started to ride around the neighborhood. It felt so good to ride on her own! Everywhere she went, it was exciting and fun.
Then, she came upon a big, messy mud puddle. Jill stopped and looked around. Then, a voice came from behind her.
"Hello Jill," it said. "Do you want to ride through the muddy puddle with me?"
Jill turned around and saw a new friend, a boy her age named Tom. She smiled, and the two of them had a great time riding back and forth through the mud puddle. They even had a race!
When it was time for them to go, Jill gave Tom a big hug and thanked him for the fun ride. As she left, she heard Tom saying "Bye, come back soon!"
Jill waved and smiled, happy knowing that she didn't have to wait any longer for her next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and her three year old daughter, Olivia. Olivia was a spoiled little girl who loved to have everything she wanted. One day, Mommy decided to teach Olivia about behaving better.
“Olivia, why do you think I want you to behave?” asked Mommy. “Because you like it when I'm naughty,” answered Olivia. “No,” said Mommy, “I want you to behave because it’s the kind and polite thing to do.”
Olivia didn’t understand, so Mommy asked another question. “What should you do when you want something?” Olivia thought for a moment and said, “Ask nicely?” “That’s right,” Mommy said. “When you behave and ask nicely, people are much more likely to give you what you want.”
Olivia finally began to understand why it was important to behave. From then on, she was always polite and asked questions in a respectful way. Mommy knew that Olivia had learned her lesson and was proud of her! 
The moral of the story is that it’s important to always behave properly and use good manners!

"Look, a goose!" Sara said. "Do you think it is friendly?"
"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe we can discuss with it. Hello, goose, can we play with you?"
The goose looked at them and honked again. It flapped its wings and walked towards them. Sara and Tom were scared. They thought the goose was angry.
"Run, run!" Sara said. "The goose is not regular. It is mean!"
They ran away from the goose and hid behind a bench. The goose followed them and pecked at the bench. Sara and Tom cried for help.
A man who worked in the park heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw the goose and shooed it away. He told Sara and Tom that the goose was not mean, but it was protecting its nest. He showed them the nest with some eggs in it.
"See, the goose is a mommy," he said. "She was afraid you would hurt her babies. That's why she honked and chased you. You have to be careful and respectful around animals."
Sara and Tom felt sorry for the goose. They said sorry to the goose and the man. They learned a new word: nest. They decided to play somewhere else and leave the goose alone. They were still friends who liked to play in the park.

"Hey Jim, look down," said his dad, who was flying the airplane. "Do you think what those mountains are made of?"
Jim thought for a minute before answering. He remembered something he had learned in school. "Are those mountains made of oxygen?"
His dad laughed. "Yes, that's right, oxygen. It's all around us, like the air we breathe. But up this high, there's a lot more of it than at ground level."
Jim smiled. He was glad that he had been able to remember what he'd learned. He enjoyed flying, even though it was high up in the sky. He felt safer now that he knew what the mountains were made of.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their toy cars and rockets. They liked to make noises and pretend they were flying and racing. Lily had a red rocket that she called Missile. She said it was the fastest and strongest rocket in the world.
"Look, Tom, I can make Missile go zoom, zoom, zoom!" Lily said, throwing her rocket in the air.
"Wow, that's cool, Lily. But my car is faster and stronger than your rocket. It can go vroom, vroom, vroom!" Tom said, pushing his car on the ground.
"No, it's not. Missile can beat your car any day. Let's have a race and see who wins!" Lily said, picking up her rocket.
"OK, let's do it. But we have to be careful. There are some elderly people sitting on the bench over there. They might not like our noise and our toys." Tom said, pointing to the bench.
"OK, OK. We'll be quiet and nice. But we'll still have fun. Come on, let's go!" Lily said, running to the other side of the park.
They found a spot where they could start their race. They counted to three and then let their toys go. Missile flew in the air, making a whoosh sound. Tom's car rolled on the ground, making a rumble sound. They both cheered for their toys, hoping they would win.
But then, something bad happened. Missile flew too high and too far. It went over the fence and landed in the street. Lily gasped and ran after it. Tom followed her, worried. They saw a big truck coming towards Missile. It was going to hit it and break it.
"Missile, Missile, come back!" Lily cried, reaching for her rocket.
"Stop, Lily, stop! It's too dangerous!" Tom shouted, pulling her back.
But it was too late. The truck hit Missile and smashed it to pieces. Lily and Tom heard a loud bang and saw smoke and fire. They were scared and sad. They hugged each other and cried.
The elderly people on the bench heard the noise and saw the smoke. They got up and walked to the street. They saw Lily and Tom crying and holding each other. They felt sorry for them and wanted to help.
"Are you OK, children? What happened?" one of them asked, bending down to them.
"Our toys, our toys. They're gone. The truck hit them and broke them." Lily sobbed, pointing to the street.
"Oh, dear, that's terrible. I'm so sorry. What were your toys?" another one asked, looking at the street.
"They were a car and a rocket. The rocket was called Missile. It was the best rocket ever." Tom sniffed, wiping his eyes.
"A rocket? That's a very big and dangerous toy for children. Where did you get it?" the first one asked, frowning.
"It was a gift from my uncle. He works at a place where they make rockets. He said it was a special rocket. He said he recommended it for me." Lily said, looking at the street.
"He recommended it for you? That was very foolish of him. Rockets are not for children. They are for grown-ups who know how to use them safely. He should have given you something else. Something more suitable and fun." the second one said, shaking his head.
"Like what?" Lily asked, looking up.
"Like a ball, or a doll, or a book, or a puzzle. There are many things that children can play with and enjoy. Things that don't make noise and fire and hurt people." the first one said, smiling.
"Really? Do you have any of those things?" Tom asked, curious.
"Of course we do. We have many things that we used to play with when we were children. And we still play with them sometimes. Would you like to see them?" the second one asked, inviting.
"Yes, please. We would like to see them. And maybe play with them. If you don't mind." Lily said, nodding.
"We don't mind at all. We would love to share them with you. Come on, let's go to our house. It's not far from here. We'll show you our toys and tell you some stories. And maybe we can make you some cookies and milk. How does that sound?" the first one said, holding their hands.
"That sounds great. Thank you. You're very kind and nice." Tom said, smiling.
"Yes, thank you. You're very sweet and friendly." Lily said, smiling.
They walked with the elderly people to their house. They forgot about their broken toys and their sadness. They found new toys and new friends. They had fun and learned a lot. They were happy and grateful

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play games. One day, they received a big box from their aunt. Inside the box, there was a maze made of cardboard and paper. It had many paths and doors and pictures of animals and flowers.
"Wow, this is so cool!" Anna said. "Let's play with it!"
"Okay, but I want to be the leader," Ben said. "You have to follow me and do what I say."
Anna did not like that. She wanted to explore the maze by herself and find her own way. She did not want to listen to Ben all the time.
"No, I don't want to," she said. "I want to play my own game."
Ben got angry. He pushed Anna and said, "You have to! It's my game and my rules!"
Anna pushed him back and said, "No, it's not! It's our game and our maze!"
They started to fight and pull the maze apart. They tore the paper and broke the cardboard. The maze became a mess.
Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken maze and the crying twins.
"What happened here?" she asked. "Why did you ruin your gift?"
Anna and Ben stopped fighting and looked at their mom. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"We were playing with the maze, but we had a fight," Anna said.
"We wanted to be the leader, but we couldn't agree," Ben said.
Mom sighed and said, "You know, the maze was not real. It was fake. It was just a toy to have fun with. But you are real. You are my children and you are twins. You should love each other and share your things. That's more important than any game."
Anna and Ben nodded and hugged each other. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We're sorry, twin."
Mom smiled and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But next time, try to play nicely and respect each other. And maybe we can fix the maze together."
Anna and Ben agreed and said, "Yes, mom. We will."

Tom was a restless boy who liked to question everything. He always asked his mom and dad why the sky was blue, why the grass was green, why the sun was hot, and so on. Sometimes they had answers, sometimes they did not.
One day, Tom found a big book in his dad's study. It had many strange words and pictures on it. Tom was curious and opened the book. He saw a word that looked like this: A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A. He wondered what it meant.
He ran to his mom and showed her the book. "Mom, what is this word?" he asked.
Mom looked at the book and smiled. "That is a spell, Tom. It is a word that some people use to do magic. But you have to be careful with spells. They can be good or bad."
Tom was amazed. He wanted to do magic. He asked his mom, "Can I say the spell, Mom? Can I do magic?"
Mom shook her head. "No, Tom. You are too young to say spells. You don't know what they can do. Maybe they can make things disappear, or change, or fly. Maybe they can make you happy, or sad, or scared. You have to be very careful with spells. They are not for playing."
Tom was disappointed. He wanted to try the spell. He thought his mom was just being mean. He decided to wait until his mom was busy and then say the spell. He thought it would be fun.
He hid the book under his bed and waited for his mom to go to the kitchen. When she did, he took the book and ran to the backyard. He looked around and saw a big tree. He thought it would be cool to make the tree fly. He opened the book and found the spell. He said it out loud: "A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A!"
Suddenly, the tree shook and lifted off the ground. Tom was shocked and happy. He had done magic! He laughed and clapped his hands. He said the spell again and again, making the tree go higher and higher.
But then, something went wrong. The tree stopped flying and started falling. It was falling fast and hard. It was falling towards Tom. Tom was scared and sorry. He had done a bad spell. He wanted to stop it. He tried to say the spell backwards, but he could not remember it. He screamed for his mom.
Mom heard Tom's scream and ran to the backyard. She saw the tree falling and Tom in danger. She was scared and angry. She grabbed Tom and pulled him away from the tree. The tree crashed to the ground, making a loud noise and a big mess.
Mom hugged Tom and checked if he was hurt. He was not, but he was crying. He was sorry for what he had done. He told his mom he had said the spell and made the tree fly and fall. He said he was sorry and he would never say spells again.
Mom was relieved and glad that Tom was safe. She was also sad and mad that Tom had disobeyed her and used the book. She told Tom he had been very naughty and foolish. She told him he had to go to his room and think about what he had done. She told him he had to give back the book and never touch it again.
Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He gave back the book and went to his room. He felt bad and scared. He wished he had listened to his mom. He learned that spells were not for playing. They tried to swim away from the reef and the boat. But the water was strong and pushed them. Lila felt something cut her foot. It was a piece of the reef. It hurt.
"Ow, ow!" Lila cried. "My foot is bleeding!"
Ben saw Lila's foot. He saw the blood and the reef. He was worried.
"Come on, Lila!" Ben said. "We have to reach the shore. We have to be safe."
He took Lila's hand and helped her swim. They swam as fast as they could. They reached the shore and got out of the water. They saw their mom and dad. They ran to them and hugged them.
"Mom, dad!" Lila and Ben said. "We were at the reef and a boat came and Lila got hurt!"
Their mom and dad looked at Lila's foot. They saw the cut and the blood. They were sorry and angry.
"Oh, Lila, I'm so sorry," their mom said. "You need a bandage and some medicine. Let me see your foot."
"Who was driving that boat?" their dad said. "They were too close to the reef and the kids. They were reckless and dangerous."
They took Lila and Ben to their car. They gave Lila a bandage and some medicine. They gave Lila and Ben a hug and a kiss. They told them they were brave and smart.
"You did well, Lila and Ben," their mom and dad said. "You swam to the shore and you reached safety. You are good swimmers and good friends. We are proud of you."
Lila and Ben felt better. They still liked the reef and the fish. But they also liked the shore and their mom and dad. They were safe and happy.

One day, she decided to make a bowl with her clay. She took a big piece of blue clay and rolled it into a ball. Then she pressed her thumb in the middle of the ball and made a hole. She used her fingers to make the hole bigger and bigger until it looked like a bowl. She was very proud of her bowl.
She wanted to show her bowl to her mom. She picked up her bowl carefully and walked to the kitchen. She saw her mom making soup on the stove. She said, "Mom, look what I made!" She raised her bowl high in the air to show her mom.
But she raised her bowl too high. Her bowl hit the lamp that was hanging from the ceiling. The lamp made a loud noise and swung back and forth. The bowl fell out of Lily's hand and broke into pieces on the floor. Lily was very sad. She started to cry.
Her mom turned off the stove and hugged Lily. She said, "It's okay, honey. I'm sorry your bowl broke. It was very original and beautiful. You are very creative and talented. We can make another bowl together later. How about we have some soup now?" She gave Lily a spoon and a bowl of soup. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you." She ate her soup and felt better. She still liked to make things with clay.

Jack: "Hello Bird! What are you doing?"
The bird stopped moving and looked at Jack.
Bird: "I'm resting. I want to fly away but I can't because I'm stuck here."
Jack glanced at the bird's feet and noticed a thin tie tied around them.
Jack: "Don't worry Bird! I can help you. I'm sure I can cut off the tie."
The bird was relieved and Jack carefully snipped the tie with his scissors. Then the beautiful bird gracefully fluttered its wings and flew away.
Jack: "Goodbye, Bird!" 
The bird waved goodbye with its tiny wing before disappearing out of sight. Jack smiled and went on his way.

"What is in the pot?" Tim asked.
"I don't know. Maybe soup," Sue said.
"Can we try it?" Tim asked.
"Okay. But be careful. It might be hot," Sue said.
Tim got a spoon. He opened the pot. He saw brown liquid. He dipped the spoon in the liquid. He brought it to his mouth.
"Yuck!" Tim spat. "This is not soup. This is weird."
"What is it?" Sue asked.
"I don't know. It tastes bad. Like dirt and metal," Tim said.
"Let me see," Sue said. She took the spoon from Tim. She looked at the liquid. She saw something shiny. She saw a label. It said "motor oil".
"Tim, this is not soup. This is oil. For cars. Not for people," Sue said.
"Oil? Why did mom put oil in the pot?" Tim asked.
"I don't know. Maybe she made a mistake. Maybe she wanted to pour oil on the turkey. To make it crispy," Sue said.
"That sounds good. Let's do that," Tim said.
"Okay. But be careful. The oven is hot," Sue said.
Tim got the red bottle. He opened it. He saw red liquid. He thought it was ketchup. He liked ketchup. He poured the red liquid on the turkey.
"Look, Sue. I made the turkey red. Like ketchup," Tim said.
"Good job, Tim. Let's eat it," Sue said.
They opened the oven. They took out the turkey. They smelled the turkey. It smelled bad. Like fire and smoke. They did not know why.
They bit the turkey. They felt pain. They screamed. They dropped the turkey.
The red liquid was not ketchup. It was hot sauce. Very hot sauce. It burned their mouths. It burned their eyes. It burned their hands.
Mom came back. She heard them scream. She ran to the kitchen. She saw the mess. She saw the oil. She saw the hot sauce. She saw the turkey. She saw Tim and Sue. They were crying. They were red. They were hurt.
Mom was angry. Mom was scared. Mom was sad.
She called the doctor. She called dad. She said sorry. She said why. She said how.
Tim and Sue learned a lesson. They learned to not touch the oven. They learned to not pour things on the turkey. They learned to not eat weird things.
They never ate turkey again.

Suddenly, he saw a big cat on a tree. Patch did not like cats. He barked and ran towards the tree. He wanted to catch the cat. Ben followed him and shouted, "No, Patch, stop! The cat is scared!"
But Patch did not listen. He jumped on the tree and tried to bite the cat. The cat hissed and scratched Patch's nose. Patch yelped and fell down. He hurt his nose and it bled.
Ben ran to Patch and hugged him. He said, "Patch, you are silly. The cat did not do anything to you. You should be nice to other animals. Come, I will take you to the vet. He will make your nose better."
Patch felt sorry and sad. He licked Ben's face and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. You are right. I was not nice. Thank you for being my friend. You saved me from the cat and from being more hurt."
Ben smiled and said, "You are welcome, Patch. You are my best friend. I love you. Come on, let's go. The vet is available now. He will give you a bandage and a treat." They walked to the vet together, holding each other. Patch learned his lesson and never chased cats again.

Sara and Tom were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were pirates and look for treasure. They used pillows, blankets and toys to make a big ship on the floor.
"Ahoy, matey! I see a shiny chest over there!" Tom said, pointing to the armchair. "Let's go and open it!"
Sara followed Tom to the armchair. She climbed on it and reached for the chest. It was really a box of cookies that Mom had left on the table. Sara opened it and smiled.
"Wow, look at all these cookies! They are our treasure!" Sara said. "Let's eat them all!"
Tom nodded and grabbed a cookie. He took a big bite and made a happy sound. Sara did the same. They ate and ate until the box was empty.
"Yum, that was good!" Tom said, wiping his mouth. "But I feel a bit sick now. Do you?"
Sara nodded. She felt a pain in her tummy. She wished she had not eaten so many cookies. She regretted being greedy.
"Me too. I think we ate too much," Sara said. "Maybe we should tell Mom. She can help us."
Tom agreed. He felt sorry for taking the cookies without asking. He regretted being naughty.
They got off the armchair and walked to the kitchen. They saw Mom washing the dishes. She looked normal, but they knew she would be angry when she found out.
"Mom, we have something to tell you," Tom said in a small voice.
"What is it, sweeties?" Mom asked, turning around. She saw their faces and the empty box. She frowned.
"Oh no, did you eat all the cookies?" Mom asked. "Those were for later. You know you should not eat so many sweets. They are bad for you."
Sara and Tom nodded. They felt ashamed. They knew Mom was right.
"We are sorry, Mom," Sara said. "We were playing pirates and we found the cookies. We thought they were treasure. We did not think. We were silly."
Mom sighed. She was not happy, but she loved them. She hugged them and kissed them.
"I forgive you, my loves," Mom said. "But you have to promise me not to do that again. And you have to drink some water and rest. You will feel better soon."
Sara and Tom promised. They drank some water and went to their room. They lay down on their beds and closed their eyes. They hoped their tummy would stop hurting. They learned their lesson. They decided to be normal and good pirates next time.

"That's nice, Ben, but my doll can talk!" Lily says, pressing a button on the doll's back.
Suddenly, they hear a loud bark. It is their dog, Rex, who has come to join them. Rex is a big, brown dog with a long, fluffy tail. He likes to play with Lily and Ben, but he also likes to chase their toys.
"Rex, no!" Lily shouts, as Rex runs towards her doll. "That's my doll, not your toy!"
But Rex does not listen. He grabs the doll with his mouth and shakes it. The doll makes a funny sound and its hair falls off.
"Hey, stop that!" Ben yells, as Rex drops the doll and goes for his car. "That's my car, not your chew!"
But Rex does not care. He bites the car and breaks one of its wheels. The car makes a sad noise and stops moving.
Lily and Ben are very upset. They run to their toys and try to fix them. But they are too broken. They look at Rex, who is wagging his tail and panting. He thinks he has done a good job.
"Bad dog, Rex!" Lily and Ben say. "You ruined our toys! You are not useful at all!"
Rex does not understand. He thinks they are playing with him. He licks their faces and wags his tail more.
"Go away, Rex!" Lily and Ben say. "We don't want to play with you!"
Rex feels sad. He lowers his ears and walks away. He finds a stick and tries to play with it. But it is not fun. He misses Lily and Ben.
He looks at them from a distance. He sees that they are still sad. He wants to make them happy. He thinks of a way to do that.
He picks up the stick with his mouth and runs to them. He drops the stick in front of them and barks.
"Look, Lily, Ben, I found a stick!" he seems to say. "You can play with it! It is not broken! It is useful!"
Lily and Ben look at the stick. They look at Rex. They see that he is trying to be nice. They feel sorry for him.

"Yes, please!" they said.

Sara and Ben thought hard. They had seen pictures of caterpillars and butterflies in their books.
"Is it a butterfly?" Sara guessed.
"Yes, you are right!" the caterpillar said. "We become butterflies after we make a cocoon. A cocoon is a shell that we make around ourselves. Inside the cocoon, we change our shape and color. Then we break out of the cocoon and fly away."
"That is amazing!" Ben said. "Can we see you make a cocoon?"
"Maybe, if you come back tomorrow. I am almost ready to make one. But you have to be very quiet and careful. Do not touch or disturb me when I am in the cocoon. It is very important for me to rest and change."
"We promise!" Sara and Ben said.
They thanked the caterpillar for teaching them something new. They said goodbye and went back to their house. They told their mom and dad about the caterpillar. They were very excited to see it again the next day.

One day, Tim and his mom made a big pot of soup on the stove. Tim said, "Mom, can we share this soup with our friends?" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tim. That's a great idea. Sharing is very important."
So, Tim and his mom took the soup to their neighbors. Everyone was so happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and mom!" Tim felt good inside because he helped his mom and shared with his friends.
The moral of the story is that it's good to be generous and share what you have with others.

The little girl thought hard and then said, “I can try!”
She walked up to the door and tugged hard on the handle. She tried to push it open. She was so small that she couldn't get it to budge. 
“I need help,” she said, tears filling her eyes.
Suddenly, her dad appeared. He could see how hard the little girl had tried and he said, “Let me help you.” He put his strong hands on the door handle and pulled. The door opened with a creak and the curious little girl was thrilled!

One day, they got in a fight. Sam said he was going to quit being friends with Buddy and started to walk away. Buddy started to cry and ran after Sam, asking him to stay and giving him a big hug. But Sam didn't want to stay. He pushed Buddy away and said it was too late. 
Buddy looked very sad. He was about to quit too, but he remembered what his mom had told him: never give up. So he went back and tried again. He asked Sam if he could stay, but Sam was too angry to listen. He had made up his mind and there was nothing Buddy could do.
This story has a bad ending, but it also has a moral value: never give up. Even if things don't go your way, keep trying to be clear and never quit.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the garage. They wondered what was inside. They opened the box and saw a lot of strange things. There were wires, buttons, lights, and a screen.
"Wow, what is this?" Tom asked.
"I don't know, maybe it's a game," Lily said.
They decided to try the things in the box. They put the wires on their arms and legs. They pressed the buttons and saw the lights flash. They looked at the screen and saw their bones.
"Look, Tom, we can see our bones!" Lily said.
"That's cool, Lily, maybe this is an x-ray," Tom said.
They were having fun with the x-ray. They moved their fingers and toes and saw them on the screen. They made funny faces and saw their teeth. They laughed and giggled.
But then, Tom had an idea. He wanted to be more creative. He took a wire and poked Lily with it.
"Ow, Tom, that hurts!" Lily cried.
"Sorry, Lily, I just wanted to see what happens," Tom said.
He looked at the screen and saw a spark. He poked Lily again and saw another spark.
"Stop it, Tom, stop it!" Lily shouted.
But Tom didn't stop. He poked Lily harder and harder. He wanted to see more sparks. He didn't care that Lily was in pain.
Suddenly, the x-ray made a loud noise. It started to smoke and shake. The wires got hot and burned. The screen went black. The x-ray was broken.
Tom and Lily were scared. They ran out of the garage. They saw their mom and dad coming home.
"What happened here?" their mom asked.
"We were playing with the x-ray," Tom said.
"The x-ray? What x-ray?" their dad asked.
They showed their parents the box and the broken x-ray. Their parents were shocked and angry.
"Where did you get this x-ray?" their mom asked.
"We found it in the garage," Lily said.
"That's not a toy, that's a dangerous machine. It belongs to your uncle, who is a doctor. He lent it to us for a project. You could have hurt yourselves or started a fire. How could you be so careless and foolish?" their dad said.
Tom and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had done something wrong. They apologized to their parents and their uncle. They learned their lesson. They learned that they should not play with things they don't understand. They learned that they should not poke each other with wires. They learned that being creative is good, but being safe is better.

Anna and Ben were having breakfast with their mom. They liked to eat toast and eggs and juice. But today, mom had a surprise for them. She put a plate of sausages on the table.
"Look, kids, I made some sausages for you. They are very yummy and healthy. They are not real sausages, they are fake sausages. They are made from plants and beans. Do you want to try them?" mom said.
Anna and Ben looked at the sausages. They did not look like the sausages they saw at the store. They looked brown and lumpy and dry. They did not smell good either.
"Yuck, mom, what are these? They are not sausages, they are gross. We don't want to eat them. We want real sausages, like the ones dad makes on the grill. They are juicy and tasty and smell good. Can we have those instead?" Anna said.
"No, sweetie, we don't have any real sausages. Dad is away on a trip, remember? He will be back tomorrow. These are the only sausages we have. They are good for you, they have a lot of protein and fiber and vitamins. They are better than real sausages, which have a lot of fat and salt and chemicals. Please, give them a chance. Just take one bite and see if you like them." mom said.
Anna and Ben did not want to hurt mom's feelings, but they also did not want to eat the fake sausages. They looked at each other and made a plan. They each took a sausage from the plate and pretended to bite it. Then, they quickly removed the sausages from their mouths and hid them under their napkins. They smiled at mom and said, "Mmm, mom, these are very good. Thank you for making them. Can we have some more toast and eggs and juice, please?"
Mom was happy that they liked the sausages. She did not notice the napkins moving on their laps. She gave them more toast and eggs and juice. She said, "You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you enjoyed the sausages. Maybe next time, we can try some other fake foods, like fake cheese or fake bacon or fake chicken nuggets. They are all very yummy and healthy, too."
Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Sure, mom, that sounds great." But they secretly hoped that dad would come back soon and make them some real food. They did not like fake food. They thought it was yucky and gross. They wondered what they would do with the sausages under their napkins. They hoped mom would not find out. They hoped the dog would not smell them. They hoped they would not get in trouble. They hoped breakfast would be over soon.

"Look, the otter is sliding on its belly!" Lily said, pointing at the pool.
"Wow, that looks fun!" Tom said. He took out his toy camera and pressed a button. "I want to record the otter. Then I can show it to my friends."
"Can I record too?" Lily asked, reaching for the camera.
"Sorry, Lily, this is my camera. You can watch with your eyes," Tom said, holding the camera away from her.
Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to record the otter too. She tried to grab the camera from Tom, but he was too strong. They started to fight and pull on the camera.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said, hearing the noise. She came over and took the camera from them. "You are not being nice to each other. Sharing is caring. If you want to record the otter, you have to take turns."
"But I saw it first!" Tom said.
"But I like it more!" Lily said.
Mom shook her head. "That doesn't matter. You are brother and sister, and you should be kind and fair. How about this: Tom, you can record the otter for one minute, then you give the camera to Lily, and she can record for one minute. Then you can both watch the video together. OK?"
Tom and Lily looked at each other. They knew Mom was right. They nodded and said, "OK."
Mom smiled and gave the camera back to Tom. He recorded the otter for one minute, then he gave the camera to Lily. She recorded the otter for one minute, then she gave the camera back to Mom. Mom played the video for them, and they watched the otter slide and splash on the screen.
"Wow, the otter is so cute and funny!" Lily said.
"Yeah, it is!" Tom said. He hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry I didn't share with you. You are my sister, and I love you."
"I'm sorry I tried to take your camera. You are my brother, and I love you too," Lily said.
They smiled and hugged Mom and Dad. Then they went to see more animals at the zoo. They had a happy day.

Lily and Max felt better. They thanked Mommy and drank their milk. They looked out the window and saw the hurricane pour water on the yard. They hoped their toys were okay. "Sure, why not?" mom said, smiling. "Let's dance like the bird!"
Lily and Ben started to dance next to the cage, copying the parrot's moves. They twisted and turned, jumped and spun, and laughed and shouted. The parrot seemed to like their dance, and joined them with more noises and gestures.

"We are okay, mom, just dizzy," Lily said.

Mia is scared. She wants Tom to stop. She sees a big sign near the wire. It has a picture of a lightning bolt and a word she does not know. "Danger," it says.
"Tom, put down the wire!" Mia says. "It is danger!"
But Tom does not hear her. He is too busy playing. He throws the wire in the air and tries to catch it. He does not see the other end of the wire. It is connected to a big box with wires and buttons. The box makes a loud noise. It is a generator.
The wire touches the generator. There is a flash of light and a loud bang. Tom falls to the ground. He does not move. He does not laugh. He does not clap.
Mia screams. She runs to Tom. She tries to wake him up. But he does not wake up. He is still. He is cold. He is gone.
Mia cries. She wishes she had stopped Tom. She wishes he had listened to her. She wishes he had not played with the wire. She wishes he was still her friend.

They start to fight over the candle and the lighter. They pull and push and yell. They do not share. They do not listen. They are angry and mean.
The lighter falls on the floor. It makes a spark. The spark hits the candle. The candle lights up. The flame is hot and bright. It burns the box. It burns the toys. It burns the garage.
Lily and Ben are scared. They drop the doll and the car. They run away from the fire. They scream for help. But it is too late. The fire is big and fast. It burns the house. It burns everything.
Lily and Ben are sad. They lose their toys and books. They lose their home. They lose their friend. They are sorry. They wish they did not fight. They wish they did not play with the candle and the lighter. They wish they were safe and happy. But they are not. The end.

They ate the treat and laughed. Suddenly, Sam started to change. He became smaller and smaller. Then, he turned into a little fish just like Fin. Sam was really a fish who had been under a spell. Now, they were both happy little fish, and they swam away to have more fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a brown cow. She liked to do tricks and she was always trying to twist and turn her body in new ways. One day, she tried to twist and turn so much that she got all mixed up! She walked in circles and couldn't get untangled. She mooed and mooed, but still couldn't get untwisted.
A friendly farmer and his little girl saw the cow. The farmer smiled and said, "Let me help you, cow". He took the cow's hooves and carefully twisted and turned her body until she was back to normal.
The cow thanked the farmer and the little girl. She was so happy to be untwisted and she could go back to doing her tricks. She gave the little girl a friendly nose to nose and then went back to work.
The farmer and the little girl smiled and waved goodbye as the brown cow trotted off. They both knew that the cow was very lucky to have been untwisted by their helpful hands.
The End.

Once there was a very restless rabbit who loved to chew anything and everything he could get his paws on. One day, he heard about a delicious apple tree at the far end of a long line that stretched for miles. He was so excited to get his paws on those sweet, juicy apples that he hopped as quick as he could towards it.
As the rabbit hopped along, he started to get really hungry and decided to take a bite of the long line he was following. He chewed it so much he started to make his way through. Suddenly, a voice called out, "Hey little rabbit! I'm right here!"
Startled, the rabbit looked around and spotted an old wise owl perched in the nearby tree. The owl asked the rabbit what he was doing. The rabbit confessed that he was trying to get to an apple tree at the other side of the line.
The kind old owl smiled and told the rabbit not to worry. He said "All you have to do is chew through the other side of the line and you'll be there in no time!"
The rabbit thanked the owl and started to chew straight away. He was soon on the other side, and ready to find those sweet, juicy apples!

He turned his yacht around and went back to Tim. He helped him pick up his speed boat and put it back in the water. "It's okay, Tim," he said. "Your boat is not broken. It just needs to dry a little. They climbed on Sam's yacht and sailed together. They did not care who won the race anymore. They just had fun playing with their boats and talking to each other. They were happy brothers who loved each other and their boats.

"But the pot was hot," Anna said.
"It burned our hands," Tom said.
"And our lips," Anna said.
They showed Mom their red lips.

Tom was scared. He ran away from the bear. He dropped his gun and his hat. He ran and ran until he reached his car. He got in and drove away. He was safe, but he was also embarrassed.
He went to his friend Bob's house. Bob was also a hunter. He had many animal heads on his wall. He was proud of them.
"Hi, Tom," Bob said. "Did you have a good hunt?"
Tom did not want to tell Bob what happened. He lied. He said, "Yes, I saw a big bear. But I let it go. I felt sorry for it."
Bob did not believe Tom. He saw Tom's face. He saw that Tom had no gun and no hat. He knew that Tom was lying.
"Really?" Bob said. "Then where is your gun and your hat?"
Tom did not know what to say. He was very embarrassed. He wished he could remove his lie. He wished he could remove the bear. He wished he could remove himself.

As he watched, the father found a cave hidden in the forest. He called his son to crawl inside with him. Inside the cave, the father found a pile of gold coins, glimmering in the darkness.
The father and son were both filled with wisdom. They knew that all this wealth did not belong to them, so they rushed to put the coins back where they came from.
 
But, as they were leaving the cave, the ground started to shake and the cave began to crumble. The father and son were stuck inside and could not get out. All their wisdom couldn’t help them now.
The shaking stopped, the cave was filled with rubble. The father and son were buried beneath the rubble, never to be seen again. 
The family mourned their loss, their healthy spirits gradually becoming sad and broken. They never found out the wisdom of the cave and the riches that lay within.
