Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a big case in the park. It was red and shiny and had a lock on it. They wondered what was inside.
"Maybe it has toys or candy or something fun," Lily said.
"Let's open it and see," Ben said. He tried to break the lock with a stick, but it was too hard.
"Maybe we can find the key somewhere," Lily said. She looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a hat and a coat and a newspaper. He also had a key chain on his belt.
"Maybe he has the key," Ben said. He ran to the man and grabbed his key chain. The man was surprised and angry.
"Hey, what are you doing? Give me back my keys!" he shouted.
Ben was scared and ran away with the key chain. Lily followed him. They ran back to the case and tried the keys. One of them fit and opened the lock. They lifted the lid and saw what was inside.
It was not toys or candy or something fun. It was a lot of smelly cheese. The cheese was old and moldy and had worms in it. It made them feel sick.
"Yuck, this is gross!" Lily said.
"Let's taste it, maybe it's good," Ben said. He picked up a piece of cheese and put it in his mouth. He spat it out right away. It was the worst thing he ever tasted. It was sour and bitter and made his tongue burn.
"Ugh, this is horrible!" Ben said.
They heard the man coming. He was looking for his keys and his case. He saw them and was very mad.
"Hey, you little thieves! You stole my keys and opened my case! That's my cheese, I was going to sell it at the market!" he yelled.
Lily and Ben were very sorry. They felt bad for stealing and opening the case. They felt uncomfortable for lying and tasting the cheese. They gave back the keys and the case to the man and said they were sorry.
The man was still angry, but he saw that they were sorry. He decided to forgive them and teach them a lesson.
"Next time, don't take things that are not yours. And don't judge things by how they look. You never know what's inside. Sometimes, things that look good are bad, and things that look bad are good. Like this cheese, some people like it and pay a lot of money for it. But you don't, and that's okay. Everyone has different tastes. But you should always be honest and respectful," he said.
Lily and Ben learned their lesson. They thanked the man and promised to be good. They went home and told their parents what happened. Their parents were not happy, but they were glad that they told the truth and said they were sorry. They hugged them and gave them some cookies and milk. They tasted much better than the cheese.

One day, Lily and Ben decided to pretend they were pirates and their bed was a ship. They put a sheet over the frame to make a sail and used pillows and stuffed animals as their crew. They took turns being the captain and shouting orders.
"Ahoy, matey! Lean to the left, we're going to attack that island!" Ben said, pointing to a chair with a blanket on it.
"Aye, aye, captain!" Lily said, leaning to the left with her toy sword.
They had fun sailing and fighting, but they did not notice that the bed was making creaking noises. The ancient wood was weak and could not hold their weight. Suddenly, there was a loud crack and the bed collapsed. Lily and Ben fell to the floor with a thud, along with the sheet, the pillows and the stuffed animals. They were hurt and scared and started to cry.
Their mom heard the noise and ran to their room. She saw the broken bed and the crying twins and gasped. She quickly picked them up and hugged them.
"Oh, my babies, are you okay? What happened?" she asked, worried.
"We were playing pirates and the bed broke," Lily sobbed.
"We're sorry, mom, we didn't mean to break it," Ben sniffled.
Mom shook her head and sighed. She was glad they were not badly injured, but she was sad about the bed. It was a precious heirloom that could not be fixed. She had many memories of sleeping on it as a child and listening to her grandma's stories. She wished she had told Lily and Ben how special it was.
"It's okay, sweeties, I know you didn't mean to break it. But you have to be careful with old things. They are not as strong as new things. And they have a lot of history and meaning. This bed was ancient and belonged to our family for generations. It was a gift from your great-great-grandma. She brought it from her home country when she came here. She said it was magic and could take you to different places in your dreams. She told me many stories about it when I was your age. I was going to tell you those stories too, but now I can't. The bed is gone and so are the stories," mom said, sadly.
Lily and Ben felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had listened to mom and not played so roughly on the bed. They wished they had heard the stories about the bed and its magic. They wished they could have the bed back. But it was too late. The bed was broken and the stories were lost. They had ruined something ancient and precious. They hugged mom and said they were sorry. Sam ran to him and saw what happened. He felt sorry for his friend. He said, "Don't cry, Tim. It's okay. I will comfort you. Here, take my laser. You can play with it. I don't need it. I have you."
Tim looked at Sam and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Sam. You are very kind. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I broke my laser. I will share mine with you when I get a new one."
Sam hugged Tim and said, "You're welcome, Tim. You don't have to be sorry. It was an accident. Lasers are just toys. Friends are more important."
The moral value of the story is: Friendship is more valuable than material things. Friends should comfort each other when they are sad or hurt. Friends should share and be generous with each other.

He smiled, took it out and held it in his hand. "Mommy, can I eat it?", he asked.
 
"Yes, John", his mom replied. "But only if you promise to be very careful. Tomatoes can be a bit tricky."
John nodded in agreement. He knew that he had to be intelligent about it. He very carefully peeled away the skin and then sliced it into small pieces.
He was relieved that he had done it without making a mess.
"Well done John", his mom said. "You've been very intelligent. You can now enjoy your delicious tomato!"

Lila thought hard. She remembered seeing a picture of a big gray animal with a long nose and big ears. "Is it an elephant?" she said.
"Very good, Lila. You are right. Now, watch this." The magic man pressed a button and the box made a loud noise. Then, a small elephant popped out of the box. It was soft and fluffy and had a red bow on its tail.
"Wow!" Lila and Ben said. They clapped their hands and laughed. They petted the elephant and thanked the magic man.
"You are very welcome, children. You can keep the elephant as a gift. But remember, it is a magic elephant. It can do many things, but you have to be kind and gentle with it. And don't let anyone else see it, or they might take it away from you." The magic man said.
"OK, we will. Thank you, magic man. You are very nice." Lila and Ben said.
The magic man smiled and waved. He put his box back in his coat and walked away. Lila and Ben hugged their elephant and ran back to their mom. They had a new friend and a secret to share. They were very happy.

She looks at Ben. She needs help.
"Ben, can you help me? The gum is too sticky. We need to make it soft." She says.
Ben thinks. He has an idea.
"I know. We can use water. Water can make the gum soft. We can strike the gum with water. Then we can pull it out." He says.
He looks around. He sees a fountain. He runs to the fountain. He fills his hands with water. He runs back to the dog.
He strikes the gum with water. He strikes it again and again. The water makes the gum soft. The gum loosens from the dog's teeth.
Lily and Ben pull the gum out. They throw it away. The dog can open his mouth. He can bark. He can shake his head. He can run.

Lily and Ben are happy. They hug the dog. They are friends.

One day, Jenny wanted to show her dictionary to her friend Tom. She carried the book to the living room, where Tom was waiting. But the book was too heavy for Jenny. She tripped on the rug and dropped the book. The book opened and many pages flew out. The pages scattered all over the floor.
"Oh no!" Jenny cried. "My book is broken!"
Tom looked at the mess. He saw the pages with the letters and the words. He had an idea. He picked up a page and said, "Look, Jenny, this is a soft word. It says 'fluffy'. Fluffy means something that is soft and nice to touch. Like your teddy bear."
Jenny smiled. She picked up another page and said, "And this is a hard word. It says 'crunchy'. Crunchy means something that is hard and makes a noise when you bite it. Like your apple."
Jenny and Tom had fun finding soft words and hard words on the pages. They forgot about the broken book. They made a game of matching the words with the things they knew.
Jenny's mom came into the living room. She saw the book and the pages on the floor. She was not happy. She said, "Jenny, what did you do to your dictionary? You ruined it!"
Jenny and Tom looked at each other. They felt sorry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were playing with the words. We didn't mean to break the book."
Jenny's mom sighed. She said, "I know you like books, Jenny, but you have to be careful with them. Books are not toys. They are treasures. They have many wonderful words that you can learn and use. But you have to treat them with respect and care. Do you understand?"
Jenny and Tom nodded. They said, "We understand, mom. We're sorry."
Jenny's mom smiled. She said, "It's okay. I'm glad you like words. Words are powerful and beautiful. They can make you happy and smart. But you have to use them wisely and kindly. Do you understand?"
Jenny and Tom nodded. They said, "We understand, mom. We're sorry."
Jenny's mom hugged them. She said, "It's okay. I love you. Come on, let's clean up this mess and find you another book to read. Maybe a book with pictures and stories. And maybe a book with soft words and hard words. But not a book with too many pages."

Johnny's mum said, “Let’s look somewhere else.” 
But before they could do so, the unfriendly people surrounded them. Johnny’s mum was scared. 
One of the people said, “You have to give us all your money!” Johnny and his mum had no choice. Johnny looked away as his mum gave away all their money.
The unfriendly people went away, but Johnny and his mum were left with no money. Their holiday was ruined. Johnny and his mum sadly walked back home without any money.

Once upon a time there was a bear. He was very attractive. He wanted to stay in a cozy place. He went for a walk in the woods and found a nice tree. He put his arms and paws around the trunk and relaxed. 
Suddenly, he heard a voice calling out. It was a little bird. "Hello, bear. What are you doing in my tree?" the bird asked.
The bear couldn't believe it. He was so surprised that he almost lost his grip on the tree. He quickly warmed up to the bird and replied, "Hi, bird. I wanted to find a nice place to relax. Do you like it here too?" 
The bird answered, "Yes, I find this tree very cozy. I enjoy staying here."
The two friends parted ways after that. The bear found a nice spot under the tree to relax and the bird fluttered away to go explore. The bear was so happy that he had found such an attractive and comfortable place to stay.

It was expensive, so she paused. She looked desperately at John and said, "It's not very often that something like this comes at such a good price. Maybe we should buy it". John's heart raced with excitement. He wanted it so badly. 
With one look, Mom knew and said, "Let's buy it. It'll be a memory that we'll never forget". John smiled and they made their purchase. On their way out of the store they passed by the cheap items they had looked at earlier. The silence was deafening. 
John and Mom made it all the way home with the new item when, suddenly--with a crash--it broke. It was ruined. John was so disappointed as he stared at the broken item. Mom was heartbroken too. She had ruined the only memory she'd been able to give her son.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the snow. They had cheap mittens that their mom had bought from the store. The mittens were red and blue and had holes in them.
One day, they decided to make a snowman in their backyard. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot, a hat and a scarf to decorate their snowman. They were very happy with their work.
"Look, our snowman is so nice!" Lily said.
"Yes, he is! But he needs something else," Ben said.
"What does he need?" Lily asked.
"He needs mittens, like us!" Ben said.
"But we only have two mittens, and they are not good," Lily said.
"That's okay, we can share them with him," Ben said.
He took off his blue mitten and spread it over the snowman's left hand. He asked Lily to do the same with her red mitten. They put their mittens on the snowman's right hand.
"There, now he has mittens too!" Ben said.
"But now our hands are cold," Lily said.
They hugged each other and ran inside the house. Their mom saw them and smiled.
"You made a snowman! He looks very cute with your mittens," she said.
She gave them hot chocolate and new mittens that she had knitted for them. They were warm and soft and had no holes in them.
"Thank you, mom! We love our new mittens!" Lily and Ben said.
They drank their hot chocolate and put on their new mittens. They went back outside to play with their snowman. They were very happy.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to race. They raced on their bikes, on their feet, and on their sleds. They always had fun, but sometimes they argued about who was faster.
One day, they saw a big hill with snow. They wanted to race down the hill on their sleds. They found two sleds near the hill. One was red and shiny, and one was gray and old.
"I want the red sled!" Tom said. "It looks faster and nicer!"
"No, I want the red sled!" Lily said. "You always get the best things!"
They both grabbed the red sled and pulled hard. They did not see the boy who owned the sled. He was angry and shouted at them.
"Hey, that's my sled! Give it back!"
But Tom and Lily did not listen. They let go of the sled and it slid down the hill. They ran after it, hoping to catch it.
The boy was sad and picked up the gray sled. He decided to go down the hill too. He got on the sled and pushed off.
Tom and Lily reached the bottom of the hill, but they did not find the red sled. They looked around and saw it in the distance. It had crashed into a tree and broken into pieces.
They felt sorry and scared. They had broken someone else's sled and they did not even say sorry.
They looked up and saw the boy on the gray sled. He was smiling and waving at them. He had reached the end of the hill safely and had fun.
He stopped near them and said, "Do you want to try my sled? It's not very pretty, but it works well."
Tom and Lily felt ashamed and said, "No, thank you. We're sorry we took your sled. We were wrong and selfish."
The boy nodded and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But next time, you should ask before you take something. And you should not judge by the color. Sometimes, the gray things are better than the red things."
Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They thanked the boy and walked away. They did not race anymore that day. They felt sad and sorry for what they had done.
The moral of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. Do not judge by the color. Be kind and share.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. They also liked to discover new things.
One day, they saw a big jar on a bench. It was shiny and red. They were curious. They went to the jar and opened it. Inside, there was something soft and wobbly. It was jelly!
"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. "It is so funny and yummy!"
"Can we eat it?" Ben asked.
"I don't know. Maybe we should ask someone first," Lily said.
But Ben was too playful. He dipped his finger in the jelly and licked it. It was sweet and sticky. He liked it. He dipped his finger again and again. He did not share with Lily.
Lily was sad. She wanted to try the jelly too. She asked Ben to share. But Ben said no. He said it was his jelly. He ate more and more. He did not care about Lily.
Soon, Ben felt sick. His tummy hurt. He felt dizzy. He wished he had not eaten so much jelly. He wished he had shared with Lily.
Lily saw that Ben was sick. She felt sorry for him. She went to find help. She saw a lady near the bench. She told her about Ben and the jelly. The lady was angry. She said the jelly was hers. She said she had made it for a party. She said Ben was naughty and greedy.
She took Ben to a doctor. The doctor gave him some medicine. He said Ben had to rest and drink water. He said Ben had to learn to share and be polite.
Lily stayed with Ben. She gave him some water. She said she was sorry he was sick. She said she hoped he would feel better soon. She said she still wanted to be his friend.
Ben felt ashamed. He said he was sorry he had eaten the jelly. He said he was sorry he had not shared with Lily. He said he was sorry he had been rude and selfish. He said he wanted to be a good friend.
Lily smiled. She said she forgave him. She said they could still play in the park. She said they could still discover new things. She said they could still have fun. But they had to be careful and kind.
Ben nodded. He said he agreed. He said he had learned his lesson. He said he would never eat jelly without asking again. He said he would always share with Lily. He said he was glad they were best friends.
The end.
Moral value: Sharing is caring. Be polite and respectful. Don't be greedy and selfish.

"Don't worry, Lucy," said her mum. "Let's have a look around and see if we can find it."
They searched everywhere but Lucy couldn't find her balloon. Suddenly, she saw it up in a tall tree.
"Look, mum! It's up there!" She said.
But they couldn't reach it.
"Don't worry," said her mum again. "I'm sure we'll find a way to get it down."
Lucy was still angry, but she did her best to mind her mum and wait. 
Luckily, a man walking by had a long pole. He kindly offered to help Lucy get her balloon. Together, they managed to grab hold of it, and Lucy was very happy again.
"See, I told you we'd find a way to get it down," said her mum.
Lucy grinned and hugged her beloved balloon tightly. She realized that sometimes it's important to mind your mum and have patience.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She was very curious and loved to explore the world around her. One day, as Mia was out playing, it started to rain. She started to get very wet and, as she shivered, she asked her mom why the rain was so cold. 
Mia's mom was very wise and told her: "Mia, rain is very flexible. It can change from hot to cold, depending on the temperature outside. So, when it's cold outside, it will rain cold."
Mia thought about this for a moment. Then, it hit her--just like the rain! She immediately knew what she could do to help. Mia ran to the house, opened the dishwasher, and started to fill it with rainwater! 
Mia's mom was very proud of her and said, "Mia, you are so flexible, just like the rain! That is why your hard work will be rewarded. Now you can use the rainwater to quench your thirst, or even to help your family." 
Mia was very proud of herself and knew that being flexible pays off!

Once upon a time, in a bright sunny day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big puddle and wanted to jump in it. He thought it would be fun to splash the water around.
As he was about to jump, a small bird flew down and said, "Please don't destroy my home!" Tim looked at the bird and asked, "Is this your home?" The bird nodded and said, "Yes, and if you jump, my home will be gone."
Tim felt sad and decided not to jump in the puddle. He didn't want to destroy the bird's home. Instead, he found a dry spot to play. The bird was so happy that it started to sing a beautiful song.
Just then, something unexpected happened. The sun came out and dried up the puddle. The bird was sad, but Tim had an idea. He took the bird home and gave it a new home in his garden. They became best friends.
The moral of the story is to always think about how your actions can affect others.

The bird says, "You are welcome, children. You are good students. You are nice friends."
Lily and Ben smile. They say, "We are friends. We like your song. We like you, bird."
The bird smiles. It says, "I like you, too, children. You make me happy. You are my friends, too."

"Oh, no!" Milo said.
His pet parrot looked at him and said, "I'm sorry, Milo. I was so hungry."

Anna decided that she wanted to sing a song with pastels. She gathered all her pastels, but the sun was hot and she kept melting them. 
Anna was getting frustrated and tried to be patient, but eventually she decided to try taking them outside.
Anna walked out onto the balcony and held up her pastels. "She sings", she said proudly. 
Suddenly, the hot sun melted all her pastels and they ran down her arm. Anna was so sad, she started to cry. 
Her mom heard her cries and came to comfort her. "It's OK, my love", she said, as she hugged Anna and wiped her tears away. 
Anna never tried to sing with pastels again.

Lily was a bunny who loved to hop. She hopped all over the meadow, looking for carrots and flowers. She had a lot of friends who also liked to hop, like Ben the frog and Mia the mouse.
One day, Lily saw a big patch of green grass. She thought it would be fun to hop there and find some yummy snacks. She hopped and hopped until she reached the patch. But when she got there, she saw something that made her sad.
There was a big hole in the patch, and inside the hole was a trap. A mean man had put the trap there to catch bunnies. Lily saw a carrot hanging from a string, but she knew it was not a real carrot. It was a trick.
Lily was very scared. She wanted to hop away, but she did not know if the mean man was nearby. She did not want to get caught. She wished her friends were there to help her.
Just then, she heard a voice. It was Ben the frog. He had followed her to the patch, and he saw the trap too. He said, "Lily, don't be sad. I have an idea. I can hop over the hole and pull the string. Then the trap will close, and the mean man will think he caught a bunny. But he will only find a stick. And you can hop away with me."
Lily smiled. She was happy that Ben was so smart and brave. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Let's do it."
Ben nodded. He hopped over the hole and pulled the string. The trap snapped shut, and a stick fell inside. Lily hopped away with Ben, and they ran back to the meadow. They met Mia the mouse, who had brought them some flowers. They told her what happened, and she hugged them. They were glad they were safe and together.
They decided to never hop to the patch again. They knew there were many other places to hop and have fun. They also knew they had each other, and that made them happy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They live on a farm with their mom and dad. They like to play with the animals and help with the chores.
One day, they see a big truck near the barn. The truck has a sign that says "Animal Rescue". Sara and Ben are curious. They run to the truck and peek inside.
"Wow, look at all the animals!" Sara says. She sees dogs, cats, rabbits, and birds. They are in cages and look sad.
"Who are they?" Ben asks. He sees a small mouse in a corner. He reaches out to touch it.
"Stop!" a voice says. It is a man who works for the animal rescue. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He looks angry.
"These animals are not for you. They are sick or hurt or lost. We are taking them to a safe place where they can get better. You should not bother them."
Sara and Ben feel scared. They did not mean to bother the animals. They just wanted to see them and be nice.
"We are sorry, sir," Sara says. "We like animals. We have animals on our farm. We take good care of them."
The man softens his voice. He sees that Sara and Ben are not bad kids. They are just curious.
"I see. Well, maybe you can help me then. Do you want to help me?"
Sara and Ben nod. They want to help.
"OK, then. You can help me by giving these animals some water and food. And you can talk to them and pet them gently. But do not squeeze them. They are fragile and need space. Can you do that?"
Sara and Ben smile. They can do that. They take some bowls and fill them with water and food. They go to each cage and give the animals what they need. They talk to them and pet them gently. They do not squeeze them.
The animals perk up. They drink and eat and make noises. They look at Sara and Ben with gratitude. They feel less sad and scared.
Sara and Ben feel happy. They are helping the animals. They are making new friends.
The man watches them and smiles. He is glad that Sara and Ben are kind and gentle. He is not angry anymore. He is proud of them.
"Thank you, Sara and Ben," he says. "You are very good helpers. You are very good with animals. Maybe one day you can work for the animal rescue too. Would you like that?"
Sara and Ben nod. They would like that. They hug the man and say goodbye to the animals. They run back to their mom and dad, who are waiting for them. They tell them what they did and what they learned.
Mom and dad are happy. They are not worried anymore. They are proud of Sara and Ben too. They hug them and kiss them and say they love them.
Sara and Ben are happy. They love their mom and dad. They love their farm. They love their animals. And they love each other.

When his friends came to the tree, they looked around and wondered where Leo was. Suddenly, Leo jumped out of the hole and roared loudly. All his friends were surprised and laughed. They played the game all day long and had lots of fun. Leo's promise came true, and they all had a great time together.

Ben and Mia were young friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big box under a tree. They wondered what was inside. Maybe it was a toy, or a cake, or a mystery.
"Let's open it!" Ben said.
"OK, but be careful," Mia said.
They ran to the box and lifted the lid. Inside, they saw a lot of shiny things. They looked like stars, but they were hard and cold. Ben and Mia were very happy. They took some of the shiny things and put them in their pockets.
"Wow, these are so pretty!" Mia said.
"Maybe they are magic!" Ben said.
They decided to take the box home and show their moms and dads. They dragged the box along the path, but it was very heavy. They got tired and thirsty. They saw a fountain and decided to stop and drink some water.
They lay the box on the grass and ran to the fountain. They drank and splashed and laughed. They forgot about the box for a while.
But they were not the only ones who saw the box. A mean man with a big hat and a long coat was walking by. He saw the box and the shiny things inside. He smiled and licked his lips. He wanted the shiny things for himself. He looked around and saw that Ben and Mia were busy at the fountain. He sneaked to the box and grabbed it. He ran away with the box as fast as he could.
Ben and Mia heard a noise and turned around. They saw the mean man with their box. They shouted and cried.
"Hey, that's our box! Give it back!" Ben said.
"Stop, thief! Stop!" Mia said.
But the mean man did not stop. He disappeared behind a corner. Ben and Mia ran after him, but they could not catch him. They lost their box and their shiny things. They were very sad and angry.
They went back to the fountain and sat on the edge. They hugged each other and sobbed. They wished they had never opened the box. They wished they had never seen the shiny things. They wished they had never met the mean man. They wished they had a happy ending. But they did not. They had a bad ending.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the farm. They see many animals. They see cows, pigs, chickens and goats.
One day, they see a new goat. The goat is white and has a bell. Lila and Tom want to pet the goat. They go near the goat. The goat is shy. It runs away.
"Come back, goat!" Lila says. "We want to be your friends!"
The goat does not listen. It runs to the fence. It jumps over the fence. It runs to the road.
"Oh no, goat!" Tom says. "The road is dangerous! There are cars and trucks!"
Lila and Tom run after the goat. They want to save the goat. They shout to the goat. The goat does not hear them. It runs faster.
A big truck is coming. The truck is loud and fast. The goat does not see the truck. The truck does not see the goat.
Lila and Tom are scared. They think the goat will get hurt. They close their eyes.
But then, they hear a horn. They open their eyes. They see the truck stop. They see the goat run to the other side. They see a man get out of the truck.
The man is the goat's owner. He is happy to see his goat. He thanks Lila and Tom for chasing the goat. He says the goat is lucky. He says Lila and Tom are brave.
Lila and Tom are happy. They are happy the goat is safe. They are happy the man is nice. They pet the goat. The goat likes them. The goat is not shy anymore.
The end.

Sara likes to play with her plastic toys. She has a plastic doll, a plastic car, a plastic cup and a plastic spoon. She likes to make pretend tea and cake for her doll and her car. She seats them on a wide mat on the floor and gives them each a cup and a spoon.
One day, Sara sees a new plastic toy in the store. It is a plastic chair. It is pink and shiny and has a sticker of a princess on it. Sara wants the plastic chair very much. She asks her mom if she can have it. Her mom says no, it is too expensive and she has enough toys.
Sara is sad. She goes home and plays with her plastic toys. But she does not have fun. She thinks about the plastic chair all the time. She wishes she could seat her doll and her car on the plastic chair and make them feel like royalty.
The next day, Sara's mom has a surprise for her. She says she found something in the garage that she can use for her play. She gives Sara a big cardboard box. Sara does not understand. She says she does not want a box, she wants a plastic chair.
Her mom smiles and says, "Look, you can make a chair out of this box. You just need to cut a hole for the seat and decorate it with some paper and stickers. It will be your own special chair, and you can seat your doll and your car on it."
Sara thinks about it. She likes the idea of making her own chair. She says thank you to her mom and gets some scissors, paper and stickers. She works hard to cut and glue and stick. She makes a beautiful chair out of the box. It is not pink and shiny, but it is colorful and cozy. She seats her doll and her car on the chair and gives them some tea and cake. She is happy. She does not want the plastic chair anymore. She loves her cardboard chair.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in a big pond with his family. One day, Fin heard his friends worry about something called "oxygen." Fin did not know what oxygen was, so he asked his mom.
"Mom, what is oxygen?" Fin asked. "Oxygen is what we need to breathe underwater," his mom said. "But don't worry, we have enough in the pond."
One day, a rare bird came to the pond. The bird told Fin and his friends that some ponds didn't have enough oxygen. Fin started to worry again. "What if our pond runs out of oxygen?" he asked his mom.
"Don't worry, Fin," his mom said. "Our pond is big and full of plants that make oxygen. We will always have enough to breathe." Fin felt better and swam happily with his friends, knowing they would always have enough oxygen to breathe.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to observe the birds, the flowers and the people. They saw a man with a big coat and a hat. He had many buttons on his coat. Some were red, some were blue, some were shiny and some were weird.
"Look at his buttons!" Lily said to Max. "They are so different!"
Max nodded. He wanted to touch the buttons. He ran to the man and said, "Hello, sir. Can I see your buttons?"
The man smiled and bent down. He said, "Sure, little boy. These are my buttons. I collect them from different places. Do you like them?"
Max nodded again. He touched the buttons. They felt smooth, rough, cold and warm. He said, "They are very nice. Where did you get this one?" He pointed to a weird button. It had a picture of a frog on it.
The man said, "This one is from France. It is a souvenir from a museum. Do you know what a museum is?"
Max shook his head. He did not know what a museum was. He said, "No, sir. What is a museum?"
The man said, "A museum is a place where you can observe many things. Things from the past, things from other countries, things from nature. You can learn a lot from a museum."
Max said, "Wow, that sounds fun. Can we go to a museum?"
The man said, "Maybe someday. But first, you have to ask your parents. They have to take you there."
Max said, "OK, sir. Thank you for showing me your buttons. They are very cool."
The man said, "You're welcome, little boy. Have a nice day."
Max ran back to Lily. He said, "Lily, Lily, I saw the man's buttons. They are from a museum. Do you know what a museum is?"
Lily shook her head. She did not know what a museum was. She said, "No, Max. What is a museum?"
Max said, "A museum is a place where you can observe many things. The man told me. He said we can go there someday."
Lily said, "That sounds fun. Let's ask our parents. Maybe they can take us there."
Max and Lily smiled. They liked to observe new things. They hoped to go to a museum soon.
